#2212. Cesar Peixoto must manage Wolves’ creative machine carefully with star potential emphasised in Cardiff City win

Wolves continued their improved run of form on Saturday as they defeated Cardiff City 3-0 at Molineux. The triumph made it 10 points from the last 12 available for Wanderers, continuing their fine response to back-to-back losses in the first two games after the September-October international break.

Cesar Peixoto‘s side were two up within 15 minutes thanks to goals from Fer Lopez and Adam Armstrong, Ladislav Krejci made it three just before the hour mark to really secure the points, heading home from a Kieran Tripper corner.

Alongside assisting the third goal, right-back Trippier was a standout creative threat for Wolves with the joint-most chances made at three – tied with Bluebirds winger Chris Willock. The 36-year-old and captain on the day showed why he has a key role to play at Molineux through his technical ability and leadership.

Trippier was Wolves’ leading creator on Saturday with his three opportunities made. He hugged the right-hand side for the vast majority of the match and saw a lot of the ball, with his 74 touches more than any other player for the Old Gold.

He completed 35 passes, 11 of which were into the final third and 14 of which were line-breaking. He made two accurate crosses too, showing how he mixed up his work in possession with deliveries into the box and others into spaces occupied by Lopez, Jean-Ricner Bellegarde and Armstrong.

Trippier did his defensive duties too, with 12 defensive contributions the joint-most in the game. He made four tackles, five clearances and three interceptions, so it was a very well-rounded display from the veteran right-back.

Creatively, his display saw the theme of his performances continue. Trippier currently ranks in the top 4% of Championship right-backs for successful passes (52.53), accurate long balls (4.35), line-breaking passes (16.39), chances created (3.01) and chances created (3.01) per 90 (all stats via Fotmob).

From deep areas on the right-hand side, Trippier is a major creative outlet and a go-to player in possession. This paired with his vast experience and leadership from a storied career to date make him a crucial asset for Wolves.

There are few doubts over what Trippier can contribute at Wolves. His past at the very top of club and international football means he provides a level of pedigree few in the Championship can offer, and he sets an example on and off the pitch as a vocal leader.

He’s a standout creatively too, serving as a key asset in possession and from set-pieces. Such traits mean that, in an ideal world, Trippier could play every minute of every match.

However, at 36 and with injury issues arising over his last two years at Newcastle United and early on this term, Peixoto faces the challenge of managing his workload. Trippier can not be expected to play every minute of a Championship season, so they must be careful not to demand too much of the right-back to limit the risk of injury.

It will be a tough balance to strike, but it is key to getting the best out of him all season. Trippier needs to be rotated with Jackson Tchatchoua to keep him fit and at the top of his game.

#2211. Morton may be struggling but charity is bringing hope to the community

Christmas is an important time of the year for Morton in the Community. Since 2019 the social impact arm of the struggling Championship club has taken part in Festive Friends, the programme run by the SPFL Trust to provide turkey and trimmings for those who need them most.

For the first time families from the east end of Greenock will also be invited to Cappielow for a separate dinner this year while a Boots and Pieces pop up shop in the town centre provides sports kit and equipment for  a community ranked the most deprived in the country.

“Think of the pressure families come under at Christmas,” says charity Chief Executive Brian McLaughlin. “They come under pressure to put stuff on their credit cards and it’s such a difficult time for everyone. Even for businesses and football clubs….”

For the local football club in Greenock this Christmas threatens to be more difficult than usual. Morton face a financial short-fall of £320,000 after main sponsors Dalrada failed to make promised payments on time.

A recent financial update from Financial Director Kenneth Weldin refused to rule out administration by ‘early to mid December’ unless a solution arrives soon. A fans’ Fighting Fund has raised over £70,000 and might buy a little more time.

The best hope now lies with a consortium of local businessmen led by businessman Raj Samrai and featuring local billionaire Sandy Easdale.

A £150,000-a-year investment package is on offer in return for 60 per cent of the club and ownership of Cappielow.

While there appears to be no great enthusiasm for an offer amongst members of Morton Club Together - the fan ownership group - 427 of the 1200 members voted in favour of a period of due diligence in order to give both parties a chance to work through the structure and terms of a deal. Alternative options are thin on the ground.

Working from an office in Cappielow, the charitable arm of the football club can do nothing but continue to offer help and support for a community which now has one more financial hardship to fret over. Shipyards and heavy industry left Greenock decades ago and the loss of the football club which has played out of Cappielow since 1879 would feel like another savage blow.

“This club has been a big part of my life for 20 years,” says McLaughlin. “My grandad used to be a steward at Cappielow and my dad and his twin brother used to jump the turnstiles.

“Saturday at 5pm is either the best or the worst part of a supporter’s week. And these are difficult times.

“But we can’t control what happens on that side of things.

“What we can control is the work that we do to support the wider community during difficult times.”

A former player with Greenock Juniors, McLaughlin always had a plan to forge a career out of football in some capacity.

After completing a degree in Sport Development he worked as a community coach for Street League before joining his local club as a Development Officer in 2014. In 2018 he was appointed Chief Executive of Morton in The Community, an award winning operation running over 20 initiatives to engage locals aged from 18 months to 80.

Billed as ‘The Heartbeat of Inverclyde’ the ticker of the local club has faltered more than once over the years.

There was a previous brush with administration until the Rae family - local confectioners - stepped in to prop things up and absorb years of losses. A move to community ownership in 2021 saw Morton Club Together assume majority control of a debt free club.

Where other fan owned operations appointed a figurehead, a captain of industry, to run the show Morton rely on volunteers with little or no experience of running a football club. And placing all their eggs in one financial basket proved a calamitous mistake when the Dalrada money dried up.

An investment package by Dutch ownership group Estrella has since been turned down and MCT members now debate why the local consortium should gain a 60% stake in the club and control of Cappielow simply for handing over the same amount of money every month as they do.

Resigned to the fact that fan ownership at Morton in its current form has failed many now fear that rejection of the consortium’s offer would render Greenock Morton the ghost of Christmas past.

“I am optimistic about everything,” says McLaughlin. “What I say to our staff and volunteers is that we need to focus on controlling the controllables.

“We are here to support the club any way we can. Because the club is a key part of the community and we really hope that the future is positive.

“If we do our bit we will be okay and we will continue to support people and I think we will be alright.

“And, touch wood, I think the football club will be okay as well.

“If they can continue to provide the football we will continue to build and provide the projects that Inverclyde needs.”

The needs of Greenock and its surrounding areas are deep-rooted. In the Scottish Index of Multiple Deprivation of 2020 Inverclyde was found to be the most deprived data zone in Scotland, with extreme scores for income, employment, health (including drug related hospital admissions), education and crime.

Around half of the region’s population live in the three of the most deprived localities. Workless households are amongst the highest in the UK while premature mortality is in the top 10 across local authorities.

“Inverclyde is top of the league table in so many areas for the wrong reasons,” says McLaughlin.

“At one point we were the covid capital of Scotland.

“We are top in terms of health and poverty rates and child poverty is through the roof.

“As a father that really affects me because I look at my two year old son and wonder what kind of life I want to give him. And what can I do to help other people have a better life?”

While the national game is regarded as a curse on society by some politicians at Holyrood, Morton in the Community are just one of the club charity arms reaching into local areas to improve lives through the power of football. Their work is neither sexy or appreciated and goes largely unseen.

This week marked the 50th anniversary of Morton’s greatest ever player, Andy Ritchie, moving to Greenock from Celtic.

Signing in time for a Wednesday night game against Davie Cooper’s Clydebank in October 1976 his first impressions of Cappielow were unfavourable. An old fire in the home dressing room stunk of gas and he gained the impression that Vikings had just looted the main stand stand and moved to for the escape boats 20 minutes before his arrival.

Viewed as a slightly archaic, shambolic, old school 20th century football stadium, Cappielow hasn’t changed a great deal in the five decades since. And yet, where the old shutters only opened for games and training sessions in days gone by, Morton in the Community have spent the last seven years since 2019 quietly turning the old place into a multi-purpose hub for those who need someone to talk to.

“That time from three to five on a Saturday is so important to a lot of people. But it can’t be the only time a stadium is open,” McLaughlin observes.

“What I really love about this job is that it’s not just dealing with the people who live for the three to five on a Saturday.

“People come in here and say, ‘I’m not a football fan, I have never been in here.’

“And that doesn’t bother me one bit because what happens on the pitch will happen. We can’t control that.

“What we can control is the impact we have on peoples’ lives.

“We can offer them a bit of hope. We can give them a wee bit of direction. Or a bit of support.

“That’s probably the biggest source of satisfaction for me. When I look back and say, ‘you know what? We helped someone today.”

Grassroots football offers weekly sessions. Worried that football is becoming a middle class game, McLaughlin grew up kicking a ball around the streets of Braeside but sees the cost of participation rising to a level parents can no longer meet.

“Football is becoming very expensive now. When I grew up I was fortunate because we played football in the street with a plastic ball using lampposts or bottles for goalposts and a driveway as a pitch.”

For a number of reasons that doesn’t happen now. Inverclyde has some of the highest stats in Scotland for childhood obesity in the under-fives and McLaughlin wants to introduce the kids of the area to movement, physical activity, sport, football, gymnastics via the charity’s nursery programme. To play football any way they can.

“We have delivered free provision for football holiday camps. We have also trialled ‘pay what you can’ for parents to walk in and put a tenner in a bucket, a pound in a bucket or nothing at all.

“And what you find is that the numbers are double or triple what we would normally get.

“We did a background survey asking people if they could afford to pay the normal £12 a day and the overwhelming answer was ‘no. The cost of playing football is a real issue now.”

Football now accounts for just 60 per cent of the charity’s activities they roll out. On a Monday night Team Talk opens the stadium up for those who feel the need to have a cup of a tea, a biscuit and just talk. On a Friday morning they co-host a session with Moving On Inverclyde, a local drug and alcohol recovery charity.

“Last week we had 16 men in a room. Some were 18 some were 50 plus, some had high flying careers, some less so.”

He takes pride in the story of one man who refused to leave his own home for years. He is now one of the charity’s volunteer facilitators, delivering programmes for Scottish Action for Mental Health after completing a degree.

“And all that started with coming to a freezing cold Cappielow on a Monday night for a cup of tea...”

For Inverclyde finding the money to keep the lights on at Cappielow is not just a case saving one of Scotland’s oldest football clubs. For some of the area’s most vulnerable people it’s a lifeline.

#2210. Perché a Napoli la cabala non basta: come funziona davvero la roulette

Centottantadue estrazioni di assenza durò, tra il 2003 e il febbraio del 2005, l’attesa del 53 sulla ruota di Venezia, il ritardatario più celebre nella storia del Lotto italiano, su cui gli scommettitori riversarono diversi miliardi di euro nella convinzione che la sua uscita fosse ormai questione di giorni. A Napoli, dove la smorfia e la cabala fanno parte del lessico familiare tanto quanto il caffè, quella vicenda viene ancora citata come esempio di come il caso sappia sfuggire a qualsiasi calcolo affettivo, e le stesse convinzioni che accompagnano il Lotto finiscono spesso per trasferirsi davanti al cilindro della roulette, un gioco con regole matematiche molto diverse.

La smorfia napoletana nasce per il Lotto, e i suoi novanta numeri associati a sogni, eventi e figure della vita quotidiana (il 90 come la paura, il 33 come gli anni di Cristo, il 17 come la disgrazia) appartengono a un sistema di interpretazione simbolica, non a un metodo di previsione. Applicata alla roulette, la cabala incontra subito un ostacolo strutturale, perché il cilindro della versione europea contiene soltanto trentasette caselle, dallo zero al trentasei, e oltre metà dei numeri della smorfia non trova alcun corrispettivo sul tappeto verde. Molti giocatori aggirano il problema con riduzioni e somme di cifre, trasformando per esempio un 77 in un 14, ma ogni passaggio aggiunge soltanto un livello di arbitrarietà, senza alcun effetto sulla probabilità che la pallina si fermi su una casella piuttosto che su un’altra.

Il confronto tra i due approcci è netto. La cabala attribuisce ai numeri un significato, mentre la roulette assegna a ciascuno la stessa identica probabilità, pari a una su trentasette, indipendentemente dal sogno della notte precedente o dalla data di un anniversario.

La caccia ai ritardatari è forse la convinzione più radicata, e si basa sull’idea che un numero assente da molto tempo debba prima o poi “recuperare”. Il ragionamento ha un fascino intuitivo, ma la matematica lo smentisce da più di un secolo, perché ogni lancio della pallina è un evento indipendente, privo di memoria rispetto ai precedenti. La storia della roulette conserva il caso più famoso, avvenuto al Casinò di Monte Carlo il 18 agosto 1913, quando il nero uscì per ventisei volte consecutive e i giocatori persero cifre enormi puntando sul rosso, certi che la serie dovesse spezzarsi a ogni giro.

Gli statistici chiamano l’errore fallacia del giocatore, e il 53 di Venezia ne è la versione italiana. Nel lungo periodo le frequenze di ciascun numero tendono ad avvicinarsi alla media teorica, ma il riequilibrio avviene per diluizione su migliaia di estrazioni e non attraverso una “compensazione” a breve termine, come dimostra il fatto che il 53, una volta uscito, non abbia avuto alcun obbligo di ripresentarsi più spesso degli altri.

Accanto alla cabala si collocano i sistemi di progressione, metodi che regolano l’importo delle giocate in base agli esiti precedenti. La Martingala prevede di raddoppiare la puntata dopo ogni sconfitta sulle chances semplici, così che la prima vittoria copra tutte le perdite accumulate, mentre il sistema D’Alembert aumenta e riduce la posta di un’unità alla volta, con oscillazioni più contenute. Entrambi modificano la distribuzione delle vincite e delle perdite nel tempo, ma non toccano il dato che conta, cioè il vantaggio del banco, che nella roulette europea resta fisso al 2,7% su qualsiasi tipo di puntata, dal numero pieno pagato 35 a 1 fino al rosso o nero pagato alla pari.

La Martingala, in particolare, si scontra con i limiti massimi del tavolo, perché otto sconfitte consecutive con una puntata iniziale di 5 euro portano la nona giocata a 1.280 euro, una soglia che molti tavoli non accettano.

Se cabala e sistemi lasciano intatte le probabilità, la scelta della variante di roulette le modifica in modo concreto. La versione americana aggiunge al cilindro il doppio zero, con trentotto caselle complessive, e il margine della casa sale al 5,26%, quasi il doppio rispetto alla versione europea. La roulette francese prevede invece in molti casi la regola della partage, in base alla quale l’uscita dello zero restituisce metà della puntata sulle chances semplici, dimezzando il vantaggio del banco all’1,35% su quel tipo di giocata.

La conoscenza delle regole vale dunque più di qualsiasi numero sognato la notte prima, e le schede informative del gioco della roulette indicano per ogni tavolo la variante in uso, la tabella dei pagamenti e l’eventuale applicazione della partage, dati da leggere prima di puntare con lo stesso scrupolo con cui un napoletano consulta la smorfia, ma con la consapevolezza che a decidere sarà soltanto la pallina.

#2209. Cosa sta cercando il Milan per gennaio: una priorità e le riflessioni sul 9

Nuova linfa, nuovo spirito. Il Milan ha vinto il derby contro l'Inter e anche Gerry Cardinale, già prima della partita, è stato chiaro. Il club a gennaio è pronto a investire. Cosa vuol fare la società rossonera nel calciomercato invernale? L'idea centrale è un difensore centrale ma attenzione anche ai movimenti avanzati.

Strahinja Pavlovic sta giocando una stagione da leader del reparto arretrato, l'evoluzione di Koni de Winter lo sta portando a diventare uno dei giocatori di maggior affidabilità nel ruolo e figuriamoci Mario Gila. Però c'è sempre la questione Fikayo Tomori aperta, l'inglese è in scadenza e resta sempre tra i possibili partenti. Per questo, stante anche l'infortunio di Matteo Gabbia, e l'intenzione di far giocare De Winter più largo in difesa da terzino destro, il club cerca un giocatore 'Tier 1' per la retroguardia. Il nome più caldo? Goncalo Inacio dello Sporting CP che, ironia della sorte, sarà allenato da Paulo Fonseca fresco nuovo allenatore del club di Lisbona, pare il primo nome. Ma non è il solo.

C'è poi la questione aperta del vice Goncalo Ramos. L'idea del Milan è chiara. Un top, secondo i suoi parametri, e un giovane alle sue spalle che possa diventarlo. Ma lo è, adesso, Francesco Camarda? O forse per lui è meglio un prestito e dentro un calciatore di maggior esperienza e pronto subito all'uso, rimandando il progetto Camarda alla prossima stagione?

#2208. Kieran McKenna on West Ham’s three-man managerial shortlist as Nuno doubts grow

West Ham slipped to 8th in the Championship after defeat against West Brom on Saturday. WHUFC are currently in the play-off positions, but back-to-back losses to fellow promotion hopefuls have brought concerns.

Now, reporter Alan Nixon states that the Hammers have a three-man shortlist of potential targets if they decide to part ways with the under-fire Nuno Espirito Santo. Nixon says that Kieran McKenna, Rob Edwards and Scott Parker are all on the radar at the London Stadium.

All of the names mentioned are currently available, but it remains to be seen if the interest develops into anything concrete.

West Ham have some favourable fixtures coming up, with Cardiff City, Blackburn Rovers, Preston North End and Portsmouth all to play before the end of November. This run could be crucial for Nuno as pressure on his position grows.

Unlike Championship rivals Burnley, who have recently appointed Fabio Celestini, it appears West Ham are looking for experience in the division as they weigh up potential Nuno replacements.

It may be hard to persuade McKenna to return to the second tier, however, Parker and Edwards may be tempted by the opportunity.

Parker has gained promotion from the Championship with Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley. He operated with possession-based football and defensive organisation within his ranks. However, his time at each club ended on a sour note in the Premier League with relegation campaigns.

Edwards has also gained promotion from the division with Luton Town, whilst showing positive signs at the likes of Middlesbrough. He deploys his sides with a compact, high-energy system, putting an emphasis on pressing and attacking width.

McKenna meanwhile has only managed Ipswich Town, taking them from League One to the Premier League. He left the club earlier this year, but the Tractor Boys would still be owed a sizeable compensation fee.

Although Parker has multiple promotions on his CV, a move for the Englishman may be a risk. He might take West Ham out of the Championship, but his spells at other clubs has indicated that he may not be able to keep them in the Premier League if they return.

McKenna would be a very exciting appointment for West Ham, however it would be a surprise to see him drop to the Championship again. He is the most attractive target of the three, but the most unlikely.

Edwards, may be a more feasible appointment though. He’s proven his promotion pedigree in the Championship and takes pride two things WHUFC are currently lacking: defensive organisation and battling spirit.

Time will tell if Nuno can turn the tide, but the Hammers are seemingly prepared if they do opt for change.

#2207. James Penrice hit with former referee verdict on 'instant red card' vs Aberdeen

James Penrice should have been "instantly" sent off for Rangers in their Premier Sports Cup semi-final against Aberdeen on Saturday evening.

That's the view of former FIFA referee Keith Hackett after he watched the defender catch Dons' Afeez Aremu high in a clash at Hampden.

Gers saw off their foes to reach the showpiece finale next month after Ryan Naderi found the net in his side's narrow 1-0 victory. But it could have been different had Penrice been shown a red card by referee Ryan Lee.

Penrice clearly caught Aremu on the hip with his studs and the debate raged on whether or not the force was enough to see Penrice given his marching orders. But after the whistler did not even produce a yellow for the challenge, VAR official John Beaton refused to intervene and the player continued.

Then he helped tee up Naderi for the winner.

Hackett had his say on Football Insider and insisted the former Hearts ace was lucky to avoid punishment. In fact the retired official could hardly believe the outcome.

He said: "I have to ask how James Penrice was allowed to stay on the field of play, when his high boot was in contact with the chest of his opponent.

"That was clearly serious foul play, and should have seen a red card produced instantly. The fact that no action was taken comes as a surprise. Why was there no intervention by VAR?"

Rangers will now face the winner of the Edinburgh Derby in the first cup final of the campaign.

#2206. Erling Haaland cuts off his trademark blond hair

Erling Haaland has unveiled a dramatic new look after cutting off his trademark blond locks.

The Manchester City striker revealed his new buzzcut hairstyle on Sunday morning ahead of his side’s Premier League opener at home to Bournemouth later in the day.

Later in the episode, Haaland called a host of famous faces, including Oasis singer Noel Gallagher and former City manager Pep Guardiola, to get their opinions on his transformation.

Pep Guardiola's reaction to Erling Haaland's new haircut. 😭😂📲 Watch: https://t.co/4KvxC9e5mx pic.twitter.com/QQBCKKpGkP

Haaland, 26, has not sported short hair since his time at Borussia Dortmund, where he played three seasons before joining City in 2022.

Haaland removed his hairband during a 4-1 win over Arsenal in 2023 on a raucous night at the Etihad as City beat their title rivals to move one step closer to winning the league. There will be no need for one now, though, with a close-cut look to mark a new campaign.

It is a new-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.

Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.

So far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.

“I’ll try to find a new Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager said. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many important things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

“When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

“When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”

Maresca added: “Hopefully we can do the things that we need to do. It doesn’t help that there are players that for different reasons want to leave, this is for sure.

“But we need to adapt and we don’t want to keep players here that don’t want to stay.

“The normal thing in transfer windows is that you have to wait because all the clubs try to keep players until the last week and then sell for more money.

“It’s normal, I’m not worried about that. When the transfer window closes and we have all the squad there, for sure it will be different.”

#2205. Effetto Palladino, Bologna da secondo posto: soltanto la Lazio ha fatto meglio

Tredici punti in sei giornate. Un rendimento che, se si isolasse il campionato disputato dal momento dell'arrivo di Raffaele Palladino sulla panchina rossoblù, proietterebbe il Bologna al secondo posto in classifica, alle spalle della sola Lazio. Un dato che racconta meglio di qualsiasi dichiarazione l'impatto del nuovo allenatore e la trasformazione vissuta dalla squadra nelle ultime settimane.

Da quando Palladino ha raccolto l'eredità di Domenico Tedesco, il Bologna ha cambiato passo, trovando continuità di risultati e soprattutto una nuova capacità di raccogliere punti. Sei partite sono ancora un campione limitato per trarre conclusioni definitive, ma sono sufficienti per fotografare una crescita evidente. I 13 punti conquistati rappresentano una media di oltre due a partita: un ritmo da zona altissima della classifica, che nel confronto con il rendimento delle altre squadre avrebbe portato i rossoblù immediatamente alle spalle della formazione biancoceleste.

Il confronto con le altre squadre del campionato assume così un significato particolare: nel periodo preso in esame, soltanto la Lazio avrebbe tenuto un passo superiore. Non si tratta di una semplice fiammata, ma di una progressione accompagnata da prestazioni convincenti e da vittorie pesanti. Basti pensare al successo di San Siro contro il Milan (unica sconfitta in Serie A fin qui per i rossoneri), arrivato con un roboante 4-2, e alla rimonta completata sabato sera contro il Monza, che ha permesso anche di spezzare il digiuno casalingo.

C'è poi un altro aspetto da considerare: Palladino è riuscito a restituire fiducia a un gruppo che, nella prima parte di stagione, aveva faticato a trovare una propria identità. Il pareggio all'esordio contro il Torino e la sconfitta con l'Inter non avevano ancora prodotto una svolta immediata, ma da Lecce in avanti il Bologna ha infilato una serie di risultati che ha cambiato completamente il volto della sua stagione. Quattro vittorie e un pareggio nelle successive cinque gare, con tre successi consecutivi nelle ultime uscite. La media è di 2,16 punti a partita, un rendimento che proiettato sull'intero campionato significherebbe quota 82 punti. Naturalmente si tratta di una proiezione teorica, che non tiene conto delle difficoltà che inevitabilmente arriveranno nel corso della stagione, ma è comunque un indicatore significativo del ritmo imposto dal nuovo allenatore.

Palladino, insomma, non ha soltanto rimesso in carreggiata il Bologna: ne ha cambiato le prospettive. La classifica reale dice ancora che c'è strada da fare per raggiungere le posizioni europee, ma quella virtuale delle ultime sei giornate racconta una squadra che, per rendimento, ha già dimostrato di poter stare ai piani alti della Serie A. E adesso la sfida sarà una sola: trasformare questa rincorsa in una nuova normalità, evitando che l'entusiasmo di queste settimane rimanga soltanto una parentesi.

#2204. Martin O'Neill explains Jota omission before Falkirk clash

Martin O'Neill has explained his decision to leave Jota out of Celtic's matchday squad against Falkirk.

The Portuguese winger has only recently returned from long-term injury with an ACL problem and he has made four appearances since his comeback against Motherwell last month.

He was not named in the squad at all by the manager for this afternoon's test against the Bairns who are sitting sixth in the Scottish Premiership and in decent form of their own.

O'Neill, though, put all worries about a potential setback to bed as he revealed the playmaker has been left out due to the fact that Falkirk play their games on an astroturf pitch.

Asked on Sky Sports why the wide man is not involved and whether that may be something for punters to worry about, the Northern Irishman calmed those fears.

"No, he's just back from the injury and I think in terms of the pitch, we felt it's best with the type of injury he's recovering from, to leave him," he said.

Celtic found themselves a goal down to Ethan Ross' finish within the first three minutes of action. At the time of writing they remain 1-0 behind.

#2203. Middlesbrough should be optimistic about 21-year-old’s future amid bright loan stint for struggling League One side

Middlesbrough have built a squad that is readily challenging for promotion to the Premier League. Boro currently sit top of the Championship and have responded well to their play-off final defeat last season.

As a result of their big spending in the summer, several loans were sanctioned for players whose game time would be questionable. Out of the three departing for the campaign, Finley Munroe is the player for Kim Hellberg to monitor closely.

Middlesbrough signed the 21-year-old from Aston Villa in January 2026 after impressing on loan at Swindon Town. Now with his move to Blackpool almost three months in, Boro’s prospect is finding some success at Bloomfield Road.

Munroe has made a step-up this season despite being sent out on loan by Middlesbrough. Last campaign, the 21-year-old was playing in League Two and now he is playing in the third tier.

Despite just five starts in the league for Blackpool so far, the left-back has made a good account of himself. The youngster has made eight successful dribbles and won 57 duels. He has just featured at left-back in League One action, and his tenacity is evident with 31 tackles made.

He has been on the bench for the Tangerines’ last three outings, but he has done well to compete with Ilmari Niskanen for a starting XI spot. Munroe’s best display for his loan club came in a 2-2 draw with Bromley back in September.

The 21-year-old grabbed an assist and won 86% of his ground duels. While the Middlesbrough prospect may not have featured as much as they would’ve liked, there has certainly been many positives to take from his stint away from the Riverside.

Middlesbrough currently have two senior left-backs at the club with Neto Borges and Alex Bangura. The former has been Hellberg’s go-to option as the Brazilian has appeared in all 13 league games this season.

His performances have been quality too, with 131 line-breaking passes made and 16 chances created. Defensively, the 30-year-old has been astute too. He has made 50 recoveries and blocked seven shots.

Munroe’s first-team chances are slimmer next season if Borges remains and certainly so if they achieve promotion to the Premier League. That being said, the Brazilian could be a perfect role model for the 21-year-old to learn from, and a position off the bench could be necessary for the youngster.

With the youngster’s ability to play further forward on the left wing too, it does improve his chances of breaking into the first team. However, for his development’s sake, Boro must identify his natural position and work on strengthening him in that specific area.

#2202. Peggiorano le condizioni di Jesus de Miguel: l'aggiornamento del Tenerife è preoccupante

Cresce la preoccupazione in Spagna per le condizioni di Jesus de Miguel. Il Tenerife, club militante nella Segunda División, ha comunicato poco fa un peggioramento del quadro clinico dell'attaccante 30enne, ricoverato dopo il violentissimo scontro di gioco con il portiere dell'Andorra, Jesus Owono, avvenuto durante la sfida di campionato.

Con un breve comunicato pubblicato sui propri canali ufficiali, il club canario ha aggiornato sulle condizioni del giocatore: "Lo stato di salute di Jesus de Miguel è peggiorato dal punto di vista neurologico. Forniremo ulteriori informazioni nelle prossime ore". L'incidente si è verificato nei minuti di recupero, quando il risultato era fermo sul 2-2. Lanciato in profondità, De Miguel è stato travolto da Owono, uscito in ritardo nel tentativo di intercettare il pallone. L'impatto è stato violentissimo e il portiere dell'Andorra è stato immediatamente espulso, mentre i giocatori di entrambe le squadre hanno richiamato con urgenza i soccorsi, resisi conto della gravità della situazione.

Secondo le prime ricostruzioni, l'attaccante avrebbe riportato un arresto cardiorespiratorio direttamente sul terreno di gioco. L'incontro è stato sospeso definitivamente al 108', consentendo ai sanitari di intervenire e trasportare il calciatore in ambulanza all'ospedale universitario Nuestra Señora de Candelaria. Il primo bollettino medico aveva riferito che De Miguel aveva ripreso conoscenza grazie alle manovre di rianimazione cardiopolmonare praticate dal personale sanitario durante il trasporto, pur rimanendo privo di coscienza. In serata il Tenerife aveva parlato di condizioni "stabili ma gravi" e del ricovero in terapia intensiva. L'ultimo aggiornamento, però, desta grande preoccupazione.

Nelle ore successive all'incidente, numerosi compagni di squadra si sono recati in ospedale per stargli vicino. Anche l'Andorra, club presieduto da Gerard Piqué, ha espresso la propria vicinanza con un messaggio sui social: "L'FC Andorra esprime tutto il suo sostegno e i migliori auguri a Jesus de Miguel dopo il grave incidente avvenuto durante la partita. Gli auguriamo una pronta guarigione. I nostri pensieri sono rivolti al giocatore, alla sua famiglia e al CD Tenerife".

#2201. Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win

Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur

“It’s the perfect day to be honest,” Maresca said, although he may wish to set his expectations slightly higher. The East Stand which faces the dugouts at the Etihad unfurled a banner before the game welcoming him back to Manchester after his spell as Guardiola’s assistant. “I was very pleased when the game started, to watch the banner at the other side, and I was pleased at the end because we gave them the joy of the three points.”

His team made a fluid and furious start to Premier League football, suffused with a desire to prove the Community Shield is just a jumped-up friendly. A newly streamlined short-haired Erling Haaland ran with impatience, Elliot Anderson was a sinewy presence in midfield, Foden pulled off a gorgeous flick which led to a shot by Rico Lewis, well saved by Djordje Petrovic.

Maresca’s selection was surprising, with six defenders in his XI, some deployed unexpectedly. Guéhi partnered Anderson in defensive midfield, while their England team-mate O’Reilly was often just behind Haaland in a No 10 role. There was an air of destiny about one O’Reilly run down the left flank in the first half, cruising to the byline and crossing presentably. Haaland was well positioned in the middle, but utterly fluffed his lines. Samson similes on standby, although perhaps he too was short of full match fitness during his early-season visit from the Philistines?

Momentum shifted after Haaland’s miss, and Bournemouth took the lead when an innocuous high ball flummoxed Abdukodir Khusanov and Rúben Dias. They both pursued it, neither could make decisive contact and it left Evanilson on the ball with space to manufacture an unmissable cross for Marcus Tavernier.

Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc

Marco Rose, their new manager, is facing a similarly daunting task to Maresca in living up to a predecessor who led Bournemouth to their highest-ever league finish and European football. “How the game went, it was quite unlucky to lose,” he said. “We had two situations, one corner kick and one attacking when we defended too passive, and that’s why we lost.”

His team showed an appealing coiled-spring quality after weathering the early City onslaught. They have players of class with the ever lively Tavernier, new signing António Silva seamlessly replacing Marcos Senesi at centre-back and silky Alex Scott, the Guernsey Grealish, whose current standing has now overtaken the man who gave him his nickname.

They could not hang on here though, with Guéhi atoning for a free header planted wide with his day-saving equaliser. Cherki’s corner was nodded in from around the six-yard line then, with the game in the balance, the Frenchman provided another, thanks in part to the semi-automated gods smiling on Gvardiol and his new manager.

"That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP

No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6

City will need more, especially in midfield. Anderson at his best can cover the ground and roles of two men, which is just as well as City await reinforcements. The incoming Ayyoub Bouaddi will help, but it is a big ask for an 18-year-old to fill a spot vacated by a Ballon d’Or winner. Maresca was asked after the match about finding a “new Rodri” and deadpanned “Marc Guéhi”, who played acceptably, but is probably not a long-term solution.

There was a jadedness at times from City, which is not a great way to start the season, although they will surely improve with a bolstered squad and fitness levels. Maresca said “four or five” of his players who returned late from the World Cup are still effectively in pre-season training, including Haaland and Anderson.

Of course City are not the finished article, what team are one game into a new season? While there is a vast gap from this performance to their best, it was still impressive to smuggle three points from zero with six minutes left to play. Guardiola’s influence will be hard to shake, but that need not be a negative.

Marc Guéhi: Central Midfield Edition pic.twitter.com/ViBZqOroB2

The Maresca era begins with the most dramatic of wins. City were trailing 1-0 at 84 minutes, but somehow managed to turn it around.

Emery doesn’t hang around. I’m not convinced he shook Hurzeler’s hand.

Manchester City 2 Bournemouth 1 (Gvardiol) Oh my, Gvardiol has the ball in the back of the net but his “winner” is ruled out by the linesman instantly. Cherki had wriggled this way and that on the edge of the box before sliding in the Croatian who dispatched the ball with aplomb.

BUT, replays show that Hill’s back foot played Gvardiol onside ...so the late, late goal is GIVEN!

Maresca jumps for joy, the Etihad erupts. But that is heartbreaking for Bournemouth...

Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur

Guehi saves the day for City, scoring a harder header than the sitter he missed early in this half. Nice corner from Cherki was powererd in from close to the penalty spot. Crowd smells blood with five minutes left but Bournemouth look to still have a bit in the tank.

Incidentally, Jack Grealish is on for City with the ‘Guernsey Grealish’ Alex Scott still out there for Bournemouth, who is presumably worth about double in today’s transfer market? Can’t be often that a player shares pitch with his nickname-giver as their careers head in opposite direction. Wonder if Lionel Messi was ever described as “the new Roman Riquelme?” and played against him?

Bournemouth have responded well to getting pegged back, playing through City, who are desperate for a shot at three points. Gannon-Doak stands up a cross but finds the gloves of Donnarumma.

City attempt to break down the left but Grealish just runs out of road.

Manchester City 1 Bournemouth 1 (Guehi) He might have missed a sitter earlier on, but when presented with a similar opportunity from a corner - this time via Cherki from the right - Guehi makes no mistake, planting his header beyond Petrovic.

No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6

Haaland threatens to break free down Bournemouth’s right but Truffert just about recovers and clears his lines.

Grealish replaces Foden, who slopes straight down the tunnel.

Jebbison calls Donnarumma - who has been a spectator for the past 20 minutes - into action with a sharp header. There is a delay in the taking of the subsequent corner as Adams and Jebbison jostle for position with the City goalkeeper, but it’s all for nothing as the delivery is dealt with.

Foden goes into the book for a foul on substitute Jebbison. A tad harsh, perhaps. Looks like he semi-slipped into that contact.

Ayari attempts an bicycle kick but cannot beat Bizot. That would have been a goal of the month contender had it found the back of the net.

Guehi combines with Foden down the right and hits the by-line before a digging out a cross to Haaland. The ball is behind him and his right-footed effort does not have the requisite power to beat Petrovic, who has been immense today.

Bit better from City, Foden curls just wide, Semenyo has a shot well saved by Petrovic. Meres presence of Cherki seems to have injected some urgency to their attacks and fear to Bournemouth’s defence. Not sure City look quite ready for this season. Obviously there will be further incomings but they are leggier and more haphazard than Bournemouth.

Chance! Foden, Nunes and Cherki work the ball from right to left on the edge of Bournemouth’s box, eventually falling to Haaland who scoops the ball over with his usually lethal left boot. The visitors had plenty of men between ball and goal and that caused the Norwegian to snatch at his effort.

Villa started last season with no win in their first five games and just three points. They then rallied strongly after that. This one feels different as the rebuild is so significant. Second half has been very flat so far.

City are asking questions now. Cherki combines with Foden down the right and the Englishman shifts the ball on to his favoured left boot and his curled effort deflects off Silva and out for a corner which comes to nothing.

Semenyo breaks free down the left channel and fires the ball across the keeper towards the far post, but Petrovic gets a strong hand to it and pulls off a good save.

Kostoulas thinks he’s made it five having followed in a fizzed-in Costinha effort that had struck the post. But the strike is scrubbed off immediately and replays back up the linesman’s decision.

Little sign of City finding the composure to take control of this match. Passing is getting ever-sloppier and Guehi put a free header painfully wide. Maresca’s team are dominating possession but would be no surprise if the next goal was another Bournemouth sucker-punch. Kovacic and Cherki about to come on, the latter should improve the picture.

Anderson receives treatment on the pitch and is subsequently replaced by Kovacic. The Englishman stretches out his right leg as he leaves the field of play and keeps it elevated as he takes his position on the bench.

Dunk creates some chaos in Villa’s box, spinning in a lofted through-ball which Bizot palms away under duress. Rutter then pulls an effort wide off the resulting corner.

Nunes makes an instant impact, beating Scott easily down the right before standing up a cross to the far post where Haaland is waiting. Two Bournemouth defenders mirror the forward’s leap and do enough to disrupt his flow - and Semenyo’s - the Ghanaian also misses the ball.

Shows how few options Emery has - he has not made a change at half-time. Villa have been a little brighter going forward. A good run from Hemmings to play in Maatsen, and then the Villa teenager misjudging a cross when McGinn put him in down the right. But Brighton will feel there are more goals for them.

Maresca looks to his bench and brings on Nunes for Lewis.

Brighton are still going for this. Gross’ corner from the left reaches Vuskovic at the back post, but he cannot poke the ball past Bizot.

You’ll do well to see a worse miss all season! Guehi is afforded the freedom of Manchester inside the box from an inswinging corner but he somehow glances the ball wide.

"That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP

De Cuyper tees up another corner from the right. His punched-in delivery picks out Ayari perfectly on the edge of the box but the Swede’s volley flies just wide. A touch ball to hit first time.

Villa have opted to sit in and hope they can see this out without further damage. The Sky Sports cameras pan to a now sparse away end where some are still cheering their side on. Fair play.

Play has resumed at the Etihad and immediately City begin circulating the ball in front of Bournemouth’s first line of pressure. It’s all very slow still and they are unable to penetrate their opponents’ robust mid-black.

Boos at half time as City leave the field, although will charitably assume they are more for referee Jared Gillet for his late non-award of a penalty. Rico Lewis went down in the box but it looked soft. Another early test for Maresca, Bournemouth are lively in attack and defending capably. City all pace and intent but not playing with much patience or finesse.

Pretty horrifying first half from Villa. It was a strange team to start with – factoring in the four big summer sales and then the two absentees, Watkins and Emi Martinez. But this has been even worse than expected. Many of the team has just crumbled under the first sign of pressure. Pau Torres has been terrible. Joao Gomes picked up a yellow and then a red card on his debut. Villa started with Buendia as a centre-forward and now - with ten men - are just trying to play without any striker at all. Emery’s options are limited. Funny to think they started really well and should have taken the lead through Buendia on five minutes.

There’s a shout for a penalty as Haaland knocks down a header at the back post for Lewis, who gets shoved to the ground clumsily by Scott. Nothing going though, and that’s the half.

There’s a coming together on the halfway line at the Etihad. Haaland and Silva tangle, which sets off a chain reaction as Kluivert comes steaming in, first towards Haaland and then Guehi. Evanilson is next on the scene and he gets a firm shove off Gvardiol.

City now looking shaky at the back. Cross-field balls in their half zipping past half a dozen in sky blue without intervention, shots from range going just wide, Donnarumma needing to save well to prevent a second.

Has stopped clicking up front as well, something isn’t going to plan when you have Haaland in your team but most of the high balls are heading towards Foden and O’Reilly.

CARTÃO VERMELHO! Gomes is sent off. Disaster for Villa. It was a kick at Rutter borne of frustration. McGinn was already walking Gomes away from referee Peter Bankes before the decision came. A clear kick to the chest after Rutter knocked him over. Gomes has been nowhere near the level required. He will never forget his Villa debut.

Ooof, Tavernier goes close with a lovely curled effort from 25 yards out. Just wide, however.

Kluivert gets a sight at goal moments later but is denied by Donnarumma who gets down to his left sharply to keep the ball out.

Haaland looks to breathe life into City’s rather drab performance by chasing down Petrovic.

Moments later, he directs a glancing header towards goal and forces the Bournemouth keeper into a smart stop. Foden’s subsequent corner is not up to much.

VAR is looking at an incident on the halfway line. Rutter barges into Gomes and the midfielder kicks out at the Brighton front man. The referee is sent to the screen and a red card correctly follows. A dreadful performance from Gomes.

Villa have really struggled under pressure at the back. Going forward they still look have enough creative players that they are not embarrassed. But Brighton are dominating them with the press in the Villa half. There are not many options for Emery to change at half-time. Mings? Garnacho?

Some very untidy defending for the opening goal here which comes against the run of play, if not drastically so. Khusanov was bamboozled by an  innocuous high ball, couldn’t make decisive contact and left space for it to reach Evanlison on the right, whose cross was hard for Tavernier to miss.

A few groans and grumbles already from the home fans, Guehi getting some flak for squandering a decent position near the Bournemouth area and giving away the ball. Not really his job to be on the ball and making stuff happen near the opposition box though, is it?

This is looking very bad for Villa. Two Brighton goals in one minute for Jack Hinshelwood and it is 4-0 with 31 mins played. The first was a very well-worked goal – Ayari cross nodded down by Gomez for Hinshelwood to head in. The second was just another mistake by Villa – Ayari stealing the ball from Joao Gomes to create a critical turnover. Villa started well but they look completely outgunned physically. Brighton are really pressing home their advantage in the duels. Lots of pressure on the likes of young George Hemmings and Gomes.

"Absolutely INCREDIBLE!"Jack Hinshelwood scores two in a matter of minutes and Brighton are ripping Aston Villa apart! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/tvS5qMJJ8C

Brighton 4 Aston Villa 0 (Hinshelwood) That’s two in a matter of seconds. Again, Villa try to play out from the back and again they get caught out. Ayari telescopes in a leg to take the ball away from Gomes on the edge of Villa’s box and Hinshelwood is there to tuck it home.

Brighton 3 Aston Villa 0 (Hinshelwood) A cross from the left is nodded back across goal by Gomez and Hinshelwood is there to finish.

Manchester City 0 Bournemouth 1 (Tavernier) Bournemouth carve City open with ease. A long ball from Smith is not dealt with and Rayan works the ball out to Evanilson who needs just a brief look up before picking out Tavernier, who finishes at the back post.

Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc

City have not yet reached the intensity levels they usually show when in full swing. Semenyo tries to inject some energy with a burst down the left but Rayan does well to track back and cut it out.

Villa’s defence is floundering. This time a corner delivered from the right sails over everyone, including Bizot, but the back-post nod-down evades everyone and Villa clear their lines.

Bright start from City, but momentum has diminished since an odd miss from Haaland, whose limbs looked unusually muddled after O’Reilly soared down the left wing and crossed presentably. Move had an air of inevitability to it, was unexpected not to see the Norwegian score. Prepare the Samson similes.

The second goal from Brighton, and it’s direct. Georginio Rutter played through with a very straight ball, and Rutter had Pau Torres on the proverbial toast. De Cuyper kept up with his team-mate and ran onto the cross. Villa have not been bad. Torres, however, is having a dreadful afternoon.

Brighton 2 Aston Villa 0 (De Cuyper) Rutter does brilliantly to latch on to a ball over the top from well inside his half. He bursts down the left channel before lashing a fierce ball across the face of goal which De Cuyper turns in. Villa in all sorts of problems here.

What a start for Brighton!Maxim De Cuyper doubles their advantage! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/3WbyZlEhMV

Chance! O’Reilly bursts past Smith out on the left and picks out Haaland, who appears to be in two minds as to whether he wants to head or volley the ball. Instead he does neither and the chance goes begging.

Gomes leaves one on Ayari, which is risky given he has already picked up a booking. A red card at this point would be hugely damaging.

Brighton take the lead with an own goal from Victor Lindelof. An unfortunate one for the Swede who was trying to get Maxim De Cuyper’s shot off the line. It hit the post and ricocheted in off Lindelof. The fault lay with Pau Torres who gave the ball away needlessly. Very good turn from De Cuyper to make the room for the shot. Up until then, Villa - even with this unusual understrength side - were much the better.

Lewis is in fact playing right-back, with Guehi into defensive midfield alongside Anderson. O’Reilly advanced of both, with Gvardiol at left-back. All quite fluid, though, as you would expect from modern City.

Brighton 1 Aston Villa 0 (OG Lindelof) A disaster at the back for Villa. Pau Torres looks to play out from near the by-line but instead picks out De Cuyper inside Villa’s box. The wide man does well to steady himself before getting a shot away, which ricochets off the post, back on to Lindelof and into the net.

City have started brightly. Here Haaland slips in Lewis, who is unmissable with his new bleached hair, but Petrovic pulls off a smart save.

Chance! Ayari gets his pocket picked inside his own half by a buzzing Barkley. Buendia has a sight of goal but he slides the ball inches wide.

He’s at it again moments later, but he sends a third effort at goal over the bar.

Villa have started the brighter of the two sides. McGinn spins a deep free-kick into the box, which is cleared out to Buendia on the edge of the box but his shot sails over.

A warm minute’s applause for the former Manchester City manager.

Brighton are in their customary blue and white home kits shooting left to right, with Villa in black.

That’s a “Welcome Back Enzo” banner slowly cascading down the East stand. Feel that the tifo department has missed a trick, because it would have been very amusing to use a picture of Pep Guardiola, and see if anyone noticed. That could actually be Guardiola for all I know, my facial recognition is dreadful. Getting all of the trite “don’t they look similar!” observations out of my system ahead of the September cut-off point.

The teams have emerged from the tunnel at the Amex and the Etihad...

When asked by Sky Sports whether Ollie Watkins’ omission from the match-day squad was a sign that his Villa career was over, Emery pursed his lips and stared back at the reporter for a few seconds before saying: “Silence.”

After being pressed on the subject, he added: “No, no, no. We are playing today here. It’s OK. We are not speaking about [Ollie].”

"Silence" 🤫An unusual response from Unai Emery 😅 pic.twitter.com/kWNZtQu3PA

On taking charge of his first match as City head coach, Enzo Maresca told Sky Sports: “It’s big emotion. It’s a very nice feeling, the first game at home in front of our fans, so hopefully we can give them the three points.”

When asked about Elliot Anderson and the void left by Rodri, he added: “I think Elliot [Anderson] has to be himself; a good player, he’s going to be even better, but he has to be himself. Again, for me, there are no players that they are the same player, they are all different.

“We are happy with Elliot, but for sure, as we know, Rodri is a big player but he’s already gone. So now the focus is on the ones that are here with us and the ones that will probably arrive.”

Brighton and Hove Albion Verbruggen; Wieffer, Vuskovic, Boscagli, Dunk; Gross, Ayari; Gomez, Hinshelwood, De Cuyper; Rutter

Subs Steele, Strujik, Costinha, Svoboda, Osman, Yalcouye, David, Kostoulas, Yohanna

Aston Villa Bizot; Cash, Torres, Lindelof, Maatsen; Barkley, Kamara; McGinn, Gomes, Hemmings; Buendia

Subs Suzuki, Mings, Ruggeri, Bogarde, Alysson, Rowe, Burrowes, Garnacho, Lynch

Manchester City Donnarumma; Khusanov, Dias, Guehi, Gvardiol; Anderson, Lewis; Semenyo, Foden, O’Reilly; Haaland

Subs Rulli, Ait-Nouri, Nunes, Reis, Kovacic, Cherki, Gonzalez, Grealish, Marmoush

Bournemouth Petrovic; Smith, Silva, Hill, Truffert; Cook, Scott; Rayan, Kluivert, Tavernier; Evanilson

Subs Dennis, Diakite, Gannon-Doak, Toth, Sanchez, Brooks, Adams, Rodriguez, Jebbison

Brighton have spent around £100m this summer but of those only the Croatian centre-back, Luka Vušković, is in the starting XI to face Aston Villa. He cost £46m from Spurs. Brighton have, as ever, sold players with Jan-Paul Van Hecke the biggest price. The expectation is that Carlos Baleba will leave for Manchester United. He is not in the squad. The injured Yankuba Minteh would not have been involved today - but he is another likely departure. Player of the year Ferdi Kadioglu is missing with injury.

Pep Guardiola’s successor assessed the breadth of the challenge before him and offered a candid appraisal of how to replace the irreplaceable. “It would be silly to try and change it,” he said of Guardiola’s grand design.

Tito Vilanova was addressing the world’s media in Camp Nou. For Barcelona in 2012, read Manchester in 2026. Enzo Maresca would be wise to study the manual for standing on the shoulder of a giant.

Charged with maintaining the standards of a two-time Champions League-winning team many still consider the best ever, Vilanova’s big idea was effectively to leave the existing one alone, mastering the art of the subtle tweak.

Describing the transition as seamless barely does justice to the changeover; Vilanova’s Barcelona side won 23 of their first 25 La Liga matches, snatching back the title lost to Real Madrid in Guardiola’s farewell campaign. Tragically, the promise of further honours to build on sturdy foundations was realised by others as Vilanova died from cancer in 2014.

After a brief stint by Gerardo Martino, Luis Enrique gave the dream team of Lionel Messi, Andrés Iniesta and Sergio Busquets further La Liga titles and another Champions League win.

The so-called “impossible job” of being bound by the weight of the preceding genius, therefore, was no such thing.

The Villa team is missing six of the players who started the Europa League final against Freiburg on May 20. Four of them have left (Ezri Konsa, Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne, Youri Tielemans) and Emi Martinez and Ollie Watkins might be leaving too - they are absent today. Belgian goalkeeper Marco Bizot starts and there is also a place for teenager George Hemmings. Emi Buendia in what looks like the central striker role. It is certainly a bracing opening day to the season for Unai Emery.

No sign of Watkins in what is an objectively underpowered Aston Villa line-up. There’s also no start for new signing Suzuki, with Emery preferring Bizot between the sticks. Academy graduate Hemmings makes his first Premier League start.

Representing Aston Villa 👊 pic.twitter.com/JjqgYhBzwb

TEAM NEWS! 🚨 Here's how we start 🆚 Villa! 👊 pic.twitter.com/nnFj5swsdg

Some eyebrows raised at the inclusion of Rico Lewis in City’s starting XI, presumably as a defensive midfielder given the presence of Dias, Guehi, O’Reilly and Khusanov on the team-sheet. He did not have a pleasant afternoon in Cardiff last weekend, although that could be said for several City players. Some lingering doubts about his physicality, in a Premier League becoming ever more hands-on, but Enzo Maresca knows him from his time as an assistant here and clearly rates him. Wonder whether that sentiment will endure if (when) City buy some new midfielders in the coming weeks.

🔵 TEAM NEWS🍒The first #afcb team of the new Premier League season 👊 pic.twitter.com/uJhTI01Jld

Haaland will make his 200th appearance for City this afternoon. Either Lewis or O’Reilly could be deployed alongside Anderson in central midfield.

Our first XI of the season! 🩵XI | Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias (C), Guéhi, Gvardiol, Lewis, Anderson, O'Reilly, Semenyo, Foden, HaalandSUBS | Rulli, Marmoush, Kovačić, Cherki, Nico, Grealish, Aït-Nouri, Reis, Nunes🤝 @etihad pic.twitter.com/6wSBoP8jon

Welcome to live coverage of Sunday afternoon’s 2pm Premier League kick-offs. Enzo Maresca faces the unenviable task of following Pep Guardiola’s decade of dominance at Manchester City and his reign begins in earnest with a visit from Bournemouth, who themselves are ushering in a new era after Marco Rose succeeded Andoni Iraola. A bruising 3-0 defeat in the Community Shield last weekend does not bode well for City’s hopes of closing the gap to Arsenal, but Maresca will be telling his charges that this afternoon is a fresh start: a new week and a new competition, plus Erling Haaland has a new haircut…

The Italian’s squad has been shorn of World Cup winner Rodri, who departed for Barcelona this week, and the spotlight will turn to £116m club-record signing Elliot Anderson who is expected to make his Premier League debut with City. Jérémy Doku is out for two to three weeks after suffering a calf injury, which could open the door for Jack Grealish, with City bereft of wide options. City will have their work cut out as Bournemouth, fresh off a historic sixth-place finish last season, look to extend their 18-match unbeaten run from the end of last season. The Cherries won three of their five pre-season matches, which included an eye-catching 10-1 victory over Serie A side Genoa.

Brighton and Hove Albion welcome Aston Villa to the Amex for their 2026-27 season opener having travelled 220 miles north of the Arctic Circle to play Norwegian side Tromso in their Europa Conference league play-off on Thursday. Fabian Hurzeler’s side face the defending Europa League champions without Carlos Baleba, who is on the brink of joining Manchester United, as well as injured wingers Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh. While Unai Emery has lost key players in Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa and Lucas Digne, the funds raised has gone towards seven signings, with Zion Suzuki, the Japan goalkeeper, in line to make his first start for Villa.

#2200. Celtic face key fixture shunting thanks to Rangers as precedent set

Celtic could be forced into a fixture reshuffle after Rangers booked their place in the Premier Sports Cup Final with victory over Aberdeen.

There is already a precedent for such a move. Last season, Rangers had to switch an Ibrox clash with Hibernian after Celtic's Hampden showdown with St Mirren was scheduled for the same day. The match was pushed back to the Monday evening, with Emmanuel Fernandez scoring the winner for the Gers.

A similar scenario is now looming for Martin O'Neill's side, who are due to host Hibs at Parkhead on Sunday, December 13, the same day as this season's Hampden showpiece.

While Hibs could still reach the final themselves if they beat Edinburgh rivals Hearts in the second semi-final, their Premiership trip to Glasgow looks almost certain to be moved should they fall short.

The SPFL and Police Scotland are traditionally reluctant to have Celtic and Rangers playing separate matches in Glasgow on the same afternoon, making a change the most likely outcome.

Celtic are unable to simply bring the fixture forward by 24 hours. The champions are in Europa League action away to Omonia Nicosia on the Thursday night before the scheduled league encounter.

That leaves Monday evening as one potential solution, mirroring the arrangement made for Rangers and Hibs last season.

However, officials could also decide to move the match to an entirely different date depending on fixture congestion and broadcast requirements.

For now, Celtic's schedule remains unchanged, but Rangers' victory over Aberdeen has left a major question mark hanging over Hibs' planned visit to Parkhead.

#2199. How Dave Challinor’s strongest Sheffield Wednesday XI will look as new boss gets to work

Sheffield Wednesday confirmed Dave Challinor’s appointment as first-team manager over the weekend, and after watching the 1-1 draw with Blackpool from the stands, he starts his work now.

The former Stockport County boss is tasked with leading SWFC back to the Championship as they rebuild after relegation and administration. He has a strong squad at his disposal, and the pressure is on to succeed where the departed Henrik Pedersen failed.

One of the first challenges Challinor faces is to identify his strongest and favoured starting XI. His squad is brimming with talent and boasts depth in all areas, so there is strong competition for a place in the plans of the new manager.

Lumley; Bernard, Cooper, Weaver; Valery, Mitchell, Slattery, M. Lowe; Barry, Keillor-Dunn; Burstow

The Owls’ summer rebuild means they have good squad depth across the board, so Challinor will be able to tinker with his setup as he works out the best XI. However, there will be a familiar feel to the setup, as the 51-year-old’s preferred formation has been 3-4-2-1 over the course of his career.

This setup was Pedersen’s go-to last season, although he occasionally switched to a 3-1-4-2 or 3-5-2 at times. Danny Rohl also used a 3-4-2-1 during his tenure, but like Pedersen, he switched to a 4-2-3-1 – which Challinor has deployed too – later in his reign.

As for the personnel, Joe Lumley will be backed to reclaim his starting spot from Ashley Maynard-Brewer when fit.

The centre-back positions will be a point of contention, with all of Di’Shon Bernard, Liam Cooper, Ernie Weaver, Ricardo Santos, Sil Swinkels, Gabriel Otegbayo and the versatile Max Lowe to pick from. All of those players could feasibly start, but Bernard has been a Championship standout at his best, Cooper provides leadership, experience and a left-footed presence for balance, and Weaver has the highest ceiling of the lot.

Yan Valery seems a shoo-in for Challinor’s right wing-back spot, and Lowe should be favoured on the left.

In the middle, Callum Slattery could emerge as Billy Mitchell’s regular partner with Barry Bannan enduring a tricky start to the campaign. This is another area where competition is strong, with all of Bannan, Jaden Heskey and Jarvis Thornton up for consideration while Tyler Onyango recovers from his ACL injury.

In the two roles behind the striker, Davis Keillor-Dunn is emerging as an influential player, and Louie Barry will be backed to land a key role when fit given his past success under Challinor. Slattery could also play in one of these advanced roles.

Up top, Mason Burstow could get the nod over top scorer Jamal Lowe. Again, there is strong depth here with Harry Gray, Ali Al-Hamadi, Will Grainger and Keillor-Dunn all capable of playing at striker.

The 3-4-2-1 has been Challinor’s go-to, but a 3-5-2 at Sheffield Wednesday could see Barry start as a striker with a midfield three of Mitchell, Slattery and Heskey or Bannan.

A 4-2-3-1 would facilitate a similar midfield, while a centre-back drops out. The depth in the SWFC squad means Challinor is spoiled for choice as he works out his best lineup.

Challinor has plenty of experience now, but this is a new task for him. With the greatest respect to his previous jobs, Sheffield Wednesday are a different beast in terms of club stature and expectation.

At Stockport County and AFC Fylde, he built them into teams that were truly his, and they grew over time. At Hillsborough, he faces the task of getting the most out of a group with big names and personalities. It will be a test of his abilities as both a coach and man manager.

Challinor’s record is excellent, but this is the biggest challenge he has faced in his managerial career to date.

#2198. Chris Sutton skewers 'pathetic' Celtic star as big money signing called out

Unimpressed Chris Sutton branded Haissem Hassan's defending "pathetic" after the Premiership champions fell apart in a 2-0 defeat to Falkirk.

The Parkhead icon has long been a supporter of the Egypt international's attacking threat, but he could not hide his frustration at the winger's lack of effort tracking back.

Hassan, bought for £6m in a deal which includes £3m in add-ons, was hooked in the 84th minute after an afternoon full of near misses. Goals from Ethan Ross and Scott Tanser in the first half secured a famous victory for the Bairns over the Premiership champions.

The latest setback means Martin O'Neill's struggling side have managed just three wins from their last 10 games.

Read more: Celtic face key fixture shunting thanks to Rangers as precedent set

And it was Hassan who found himself firmly in Sutton's firing line, with the former Celtic striker making his feelings clear while on commentary duty for Sky Sports. O'Neill admitted on Friday that Hassan's defensive game needed added work.

Sutton said: "Absolutely pathetic from Hassan on a couple of occasions. He doesn't want to defend.

"You thought Celtic would come out in the second half and play with purpose, but they're being bullied by Falkirk."

#2197. Julien Stephan confirms ‘long-term injury’ for QPR forward ahead of Burnley clash

QPR were beaten 4-1 by Southampton on Saturday, and the result wasn’t the only dampener on a tough day at the office for the Hoops. After being introduced as a second-half substitute, forward Alfie Lloyd hobbled off through injury.

Now, speaking to West London Sport ahead of Tuesday’s tie against Burnley, R’s boss Julien Stephan revealed the 23-year-old looks set for an extended spell on the sidelines. Lloyd is set to be out for two months, likely keeping him sidelined until 2027.

“It’s a long-term injury,” Stephan said. “It will probably be difficult for him to come back before the end of the year.”

Jake Clarke-Salter is also expected to miss the Burnley tie, though his issue is undisclosed at present. Nicolas Madsen, Rumarn Burrell and Tariq Lamptey are on course for returns right after the November international break, and Ilias Chair is set to be eased back in with more substitute appearances after his return on Saturday.

Stephan does not have the biggest of squads at QPR, but he has good depth in all positions. That has been put to the test in the first quarter of the campaign, especially in attack.

Lloyd offers his services across the front three, and his versatility has helped deal with a shortage of options. Up top, all of Richard Kone, Justin Obikwu, Burrell and now Lloyd have had time on the sidelines, while Rayan Kolli was omitted too.

On the wings, Karamoko Dembele is still working back to full fitness after his ACL injury. Chair and Koki Saito, have had their issues as well, so it has been a heavily impacted area.

Stephan’s options have replenished over recent weeks, but Lloyd now drops out to leave the boss without a flexible forward and a strong physical profile. It will be hoped he can recover swiftly to return as soon and as safely as possible.

Lloyd’s long-term absence serves as a blow, but QPR do have the players to deal with the blow.

Stephan could recall one of Leon Scarlett or Justin Obikwu to the bench to cover. Kone will be backed to hold onto his starting berth having netted again in the Southampton loss.

Burnley have conceded 25 times in 13 games this season, and that record is something the Hoops will be ready to target. They have scored nine goals in their last two matches at Loftus Road, and they have the attacking style and talent to find a similar level of success against the Clarets.

#2196. Celtic fall to Falkirk defeat as Scott Bain shines for Bairns

Celtic paid the price for a sloppy start and a superb display from former goalkeeper Scott Bain as they fell to a 2-0 defeat at Falkirk.

Ethan Ross netted in the third minute after a mistake by Cameron Carter-Vickers and Scott Tanser put Falkirk two ahead in the 38th minute.

Bain made 10 saves as Martin O’Neill’s side endured an afternoon of frustration and suffered a sixth defeat in 10 matches.

The champions remain four points clear at the top of the William Hill Premiership but have now played a game more than second-placed Rangers.

Falkirk moved up to fourth in the table after their fourth consecutive victory and their first over Celtic since 2007.

Read more: Celtic face key fixture shunting thanks to Rangers as precedent set

Carter-Vickers returned to the starting line-up after injury, while Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain was handed his first start in two months. Winger Haissem Hassan was recalled.

Kasper Hogh might have fancied himself to end his barren run on Falkirk’s synthetic pitch given most of his career goals have come on artificial surfaces, but the former Bodo/Glimt striker was dropped as Camilo Duran led the line.

The Danish striker came on for the final 25 minutes but was barely involved as he went 14 games without a goal.

Falkirk got an early lift after the Celtic central defence failed to deal with a long ball.

The hosts worked the ball out to Ryan Strain, whose cross was knocked into the path of Ross by Carter-Vickers. The wide player lapped up the chance.

The goal came at a cost as Strain injured himself while crossing. Jack McMillan was a natural replacement at right-back.

Both sides made opportunities in the first half.

On-loan Derby winger Owen Eames was a hive of creativity on Falkirk’s left wing and helped set up two half chances for Jacob Murrell, who could not make the most of them.

The 19-year-old wide player set up the second goal as left-back Tanser ran on to his infield pass before slotting past Sam Johnstone.

Duran hit a post after getting in behind and Celtic were kept out by a string of excellent first-half stops from Bain, who denied the Colombian three times and also foiled Hassan with a diving save.

Falkirk were almost out of sight early in the second half when Murrell bundled the ball over the line after Celtic failed to deal with a long throw, but the ball had hit the American’s hand when it bounced off a post before going in off the striker’s waist and the goal was disallowed by VAR.

O’Neill had brought on James Forrest for Callum Osmand at half-time and the winger forced Bain’s first save of the half before Callum McGregor, Kieran Tierney and Hassan missed the target from inside the box.

O’Neill turned to Hogh and Benjamin Nygren as Duran and Oxlade-Chamberlain made way.

But Bain quickly pulled off a brilliant double save from Forrest and Nygren to spark chants of ‘Scotland’s number one’.

The former Celtic goalkeeper soon denied Forrest again before Nygren was thwarted by a diving block from Finn Yeats.

It grew increasingly clear that Celtic were never going to score as Liam Scales headed over and Bain saved long-range efforts from Nygren and Mika Baur.
