#2195. Tony Mowbray confirms early Blackburn Rovers winter transfer hope with key position targeted

Blackburn Rovers have had a strong first quarter of the 2026/27 campaign, despite a challenging summer. Many at Ewood Park felt more was needed in the transfer window as only three new players signed, and now eyes are already on January.

Speaking to the Lancashire Telegraph, Tony Mowbray has confirmed one position he wants to strengthen is central midfield. He said: “We’ve talked about positional stuff and I think that’s very much an area where we can create competition for places. I’m sure we’ve got a department looking and I think within the next week or so I’ll be shown some players.”

Sam Morsy was signed on a free transfer and has made a positive impact at Ewood Park, but depth is limited and at 35, the Egyptian isn’t a long-term fix. Kristi Montgomery, Moussa Baradji and Jake Garrett are the other midfield options at present with Adam Forshaw out through a hip issue.

The Blackburn Rovers hierarchy have not got a great reputation. A dismal year of recruitment left them in relegation danger last season, and there have been justified concerns over their fate this term given just how few new arrivals there were in the summer.

Mowbray has made a good start to his latest Rovers stint as he gets a tune out of the group at his disposal, but they can not afford to rest on their laurels. If they do not strengthen in January, the Lancashire outfit are certainly at risk of a slide down the table.

It means Blackburn have to do business in the winter, and the midfield is a good place to start. Identifying targets now will allow them to make their moves early in the next transfer window, rather than scrambling for late additions like they have in recent times.

A new midfielder is clearly a priority. However, goalkeeper is another position of focus for Rovers amid doubts over Balazs Toth’s future as his deal runs down.

Morsy provides experience, leadership and pedigree in the middle of the park for Blackburn Rovers. Someone of a similar profile to him could be ideal, but perhaps a few years younger.

Montgomery is developing well and Baradji is settling into Championship football too, and they will both benefit from an experienced player alongside them. Targeting another central midfielder who has played plenty of football at a similar or higher level will be wise – someone who can guide their partner through the match and offer a bit of bite out of possession.

Forshaw and Morsy have proven to be players of value for Rovers, but at 35, the club will be aware that they are not long-term options. Perhaps a signing like the 2023 swoop for Sondre Tronstad would be ideal to keep the balance of youthful exuberance and experience in the middle.

#2194. VIP pundits rip Celtic to shreds as major next manager claim goes public

Celtic's shock defeat to Falkirk has sparked a blistering backlash from some of Scottish football's biggest names, with Martin O'Neill's leadership, team selection and transfer planning all coming under fierce scrutiny. Kris Boyd insists serious questions now have to be asked of the under-pressure boss and even fears the Parkhead hierarchy lack a clear succession plan should they decide to make a change. Chris Sutton has branded Celtic's current set-up a mess, from goalkeeping concerns to midfield shortcomings, while claiming O'Neill's starting XI has become impossible to predict. Pat Bonner also voiced concerns over whether every member of the squad is capable of meeting the demands expected at Celtic.

"The midfield is really vulnerable, but it's not just in the midfield.

"The goalkeeping situation is a mess. Sam Johnstone doesn't really excite and inspire me, and I think he's going to be safe.

"You've got Liam Scales dribbling out from the back thinking he's Baresi - he's not. The lack in midfield athletically and physically.

"Then you sign two strikers, but you can't play them together. Why not? Because you can't play 4-4-2 because the midfielders aren't athletic enough to do that and he doesn't want to play a back three.

"Martin needs to be forthright in how he wants to play and stick to one thing. It's a lottery waiting for the Celtic team, who knows what team Martin is going to pick?"

"Overall if you look at Celtic right now, where are they going? If you're operating as a top football club, you should already have a list of who your next managers are.

"Celtic haven't a clue what they're doing... the hierarchy will say, 'we're still successful, we're still winning', but eventually it catches up with you if you don't have a plan in place."

"Celtic have got a team that if they're all functioning - as we saw against Hearts - they can still cause problems for every team in the league. But they're not functioning properly.

"There are other managers under severe pressure. There has to be serious questions asked about Martin [O'Neill] now. Last season is over now... and right now, for Celtic to have lost six in the last ten in all competitions still isn't good enough. They're miles off it."

"It was a terrific display from Falkirk defensively. They had much more penetration than Celtic, who just go from side to side. Scott Bain was unbelievable. Absolutely unbelievable. I counted eight saves he made.

"Falkirk deserve it. They've got a terrific young team. John McGlynn has done a great job with them. But there are big question marks over whether or not these players are good enough for Celtic."

#2193. Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan

It had to end that way, didn’t it? A last-minute goal, a sense of what might have been and a helter-skelter contest that will take days to decipher.

Newcastle versus Liverpool became the Premier League’s most dramatic fixture when Kevin Keegan was manager here and, on the afternoon they flocked to the “cathedral on the hill” to pay tribute to the late, great superstar, we were treated to a contest that was in keeping with his narrative.

Liverpool operating with the discipline of a basketball team undoubtedly helped, and we can examine those gaping chasms soon enough, but the poignancy of seeing Matthias Jaissle looking as bereft as Keegan at Anfield 30 years ago at the final whistle was impossible to ignore.

Really, the German’s first match in charge of Newcastle should have ended with three points. His team are a work in progress – rich in youthful exuberance though prone to lapses – but how they fought, ran and worked to give the locals the result they wanted.

They were almost at the finish line, seconds away from beating Liverpool here for the first time since December 2015, but then Lewis Hall ran into Victor Muñoz, sending the Spanish substitute sprawling, and Stuart Attwell pointed to the penalty spot. Dominik Szoboszlai inflicted maximum damage.

Dominik Szoboszlai equalises from the spot in the 99th minute! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/0Ag9WitqHt

“I have clear thoughts,” Jaissle said quietly, as he was asked to reflect on the day-wrecking decision. “I guess you call it a soft penalty here. If you give it, you need to give a lot during this match and a lot during the season. I don’t know if it that is good for football.”

Here was the third time in four seasons Liverpool had scored in injury time in front of the Leazes Stand, after Darwin Núñez (2023) and Rio Ngumoha (2025), and their eighth goal beyond the 90th minute in collisions with Newcastle is a Premier League record against the same opponents.

No wonder he was stunned. Jaissle had spent idle moments in the build-up thinking about what might happen if Newcastle scored an early goal and, much to his delight, fantasy became reality in the most thrilling fashion. On this emotional afternoon, it was fitting the hosts scored first.

One of Keegan’s great early wins as Newcastle manager was in November 1993, when his team blew away Liverpool in the snow and Andy Cole scored a first-half hat-trick. His first goal that day came after five minutes and, by happy coincidence, the clock stopped at that moment for Anthony Elanga, too.

How Liverpool went from having a chance of their own to conceding 20 seconds later is something Andoni Iraola will have to address quickly, but that is what happened: Ryan Gravenberch should have shot, instead he passed and Amar Dedic intervened, his interception finding Will Osula.

Off Osula galloped, Liverpool’s defenders looking leaden-footed as they gave pursuit, and he ushered Elanga into open space. Once he was in the clear, he was not for catching and his shot was perfectly placed beyond Alisson Becker.

An electric start! Anthony Elanga gives Newcastle the lead inside 5 minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/8DYYFJ9i6F

As Elanga was mobbed, the recriminations started. Fingers pointed at each other, Iraola spun around in dismay. Liverpool were easy to play against last season – Iraola’s Bournemouth had scored two identical goals against them on the opening day 12 months ago – and old habits die hard.

“We should finish the play,” Iraola conceded. “We created a great chance. We are on the edge of the box and have a clear opening to shoot and we decide not to. We don’t finish it properly and then you have to give credit to Elanga, who wins the race.”

What could Liverpool offer in response? The answer before the interval was nothing, other than a shot from Florian Wirtz that was well saved by Lukas Hornicek. The first half was wretched and it was difficult to see what had changed from the final throes of Arne Slot.

This, to be clear, is no criticism of Iraola, more a spotlight on players who need to step up. They did that momentarily in the second period, when Cody Gakpo equalised. He was afforded too much time by Newcastle’s defence but, still, his finish from 20 yards was super, zipping beyond Hornicek.

Cody Gakpo with a fine finish to equalise for Liverpool! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/cfDQWbES2v

But parity was secured for less than two minutes before Newcastle scored a near-carbon-copy second goal, another counter-attack – this was one led by the outstanding Yoane Wissa – ending with substitute Joe Willock finding a corner of Alisson’s net. Again the inquests followed.

"Wow!"Joe Willock restores Newcastle's advantage almost instantly with an exceptional finish! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/8IKPUgqapK

“We had the numbers to defend it better,” Iraola said. “It’s not like they caught us by surprise, but we didn’t defend it properly. We should compete for the first ball and probably make a foul, be a little more aggressive as we had the numbers to defend it.

“You don’t want to concede transitions and we’d been preparing them in the week for transitions.”

Why they didn’t follow the plan that had been set is something that Iraola must address, but he will be relieved that the days spent this week are not dissecting a defeat, as Wissa should have wrapped up the contest, only for Alisson to make a brilliant save to thwart the Congolese striker.

Those missed chances should not have mattered but in the final throes, Hall misjudged the angle Muñoz attacked him from, he got his challenge wrong and, after a pause, Attwell pointed to the spot. Given the agony Liverpool have inflicted, the outcome was as clear as black and white.

“We scored at the end, so you have a better taste,” Iraola said. “Before the game, we wouldn’t have signed for this result. It’s a reward. It’s only a point, but at least it’s something that’s deserved.”

Plenty would contest his conclusion. Liverpool got away with it – and Iraola is about to find the hard work is only just beginning.

A really soft one, if you give that, they’ll be more in the future, I’m not a fan of that.

Their heads are a little down but we know we had many challenges, we’re in a huge transition phase at the moment.

It’s a brave project but I like the challenge, working with young lads, they were tired. Lewis Miley just came back from an injury but they did an amazing job and it’s just about getting adapted to the league.

The crowd here is unbelievable and the quality. Every change can be decisive and it’s something I really enjoy. We’re clear in our approach and you can adjust in the game if you plan ahead.

It’s not the result you want, but scoring in the last minute gives us a better feeling. I value that the players never gave up. I’m sure we had more chances, it’s unfair they’re winning very early and overall, I think we’ve had the better chances.

What a special club, what a special man, that’s why we gave him a big credit. The fans were unbelievable today. I think we gave them so much back today and that’s what we need to give them all season.

We know we needed to give the fans something after this period so that’s why we tried to start fast. The fans pushed us until the end.

More than 50,000 fans in the stadium against you. You can’t hear your own voice. That’s why I love football and that’s why I am doing it.

To come here is always tough. Everybody knows the [Newcastle] fans are unbelievable. They have a great team and a manager - new but he has proven himself in many other clubs. But we were prepared and we needed to be closer to each other under a new manager as well. We needed to know what was going on in the game. It’s a good thing coming back into the game after 2-1 down.

If I am honest, we should have won. But that’s football. You don’t win easy in the Premier League - doesn’t matter who you play against. We have to be aware of that and we need to take care in the next game.

Alexander Isak is going to be in for the sort of hostile afternoon unseen in English football for years.

Not since Michael Owen has a player left Newcastle and been so universally despised. Owen was accused of ducking out of a relegation battle to ensure he secured a lucrative free transfer move after an injury-ravaged spell in the North East.

If anything, Isak was even worse, He went on strike, refusing to play for the club again, despite having three years left on his contract, in order to force a move to Liverpool. It felt like the ultimate betrayal and crossed a line with Geordies. They will love you and worship players as good as Isak, but if you behave like the Sweden international did you become the ultimate villain.

Isak was a superb player in black and white stripes, arguably their best since the takeover by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund in 2021. He was top goalscorer two years running and was the focal point of Eddie Hower’s attack as they qualified for the Champions League twice and won the Carabao Cup.

He could have been a Geordie legend, but he left in such an ugly and acrimonious fashion. Isak forced Newcastle to buckle from their not for sale stance, rejecting a pay rise and a new contract, insisting he would never play for the club again even if they refused to sell him, that he will be tarnished forever.

It is sad in many ways and shows the ugly side of the game. I’m told he does regret the manner of his exit, especially his falling out with Howe. They have not spoken since. It has weighed heavily on him since his move to Anfield.

Looks like Rio Ngumoha will play on the right flank with Cody Gakpo left, Wirtz in the No 10 role behind Isak.

Sir Kenny Dalglish and Bobby Moncur are the representatives of both clubs with wreaths, and Shola Ameobi is behind Dalglish. Ian Rush is also in attendance, who spent one season on Tyneside in the twilight of his career when Dalglish was the manager.

There will be a powerful expression of unity between Newcastle United and Liverpool supporters in memory of their shared icon, Kevin Keegan, before this afternoon’s game.

A man who meant so much to both clubs: a phenomenal player for Liverpool and a force of nature who transformed Newcastle as both a player and a manager.

The cooperation between the two to ensure St James’ Park can deliver a special tribute to a remarkable figure in English football has been heartwarming.

The sale of Curtis Jones to Inter Milan means that for the first time since Liverpool came into existence in 1892, the prospect of them going through the season without fielding a player who was born in the city for a game is real. That will surely sting Liverpool fans more than most, given the city’s strong sense of regional identity. You can read more on the subject in this article by Dominic King. Trent on loan in January, anyone?

He has also not sugar-coated anything. Jaissle knows he is up against it. Time is the enemy, given how late he arrived in pre-season and he understands the size of the task ahead.

These are early days, but the energy and purpose he has brought to the job have impressed everyone at all levels of the club. Clear communication is at the heart of everything. He explains what he expects, what he needs and what has to be done, no matter who the conversation is with.

It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

This fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with new managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

It has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

Liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Much will depend on how 21-year-old central defender Jérémy Jacquet fares alongside Vigin van Dijk but he impressed in pre-season.Full team news on the way shortly.

#2192. Wolves and Swansea City handed major boost involving Peixoto & Matos

Wolverhampton Wanderers and Swansea City have received a major managerial boost after their respective head coaches were linked with the vacancy at Liga Portugal side, Sporting CP, across the weekend.

Indeed, it has been widely reported that Sporting are nearing an agreement with Olympique Lyonnais boss, Paulo Fonseca, which increases the likelihood of Cesar Peixoto and Vitor Matos staying put.

Both clubs enjoyed emphatic victories on Saturday and are well-placed inside the Championship's early-season promotion picture as a result.

Wolves made it two home victories in the space of a week by seeing off Cardiff City 3-0 at Molineux, whilst Swansea responded to successive losses with a 4-0 thumping of Blackburn Rovers.

As such, the aforementioned managerial news will be the latest lift for both sets of supporters and the respective squads in WV1 and SA1.

It was reported on Saturday that the two Championship managers had emerged on the radar of Sporting, who have terminated Rui Borges' contract after just under two years in charge.

Peixoto's move to Molineux in the summer was his first managerial role outside Portugal, having finished sixth in the top-flight last season with Gil Vicente, whilst Matos also enjoyed a brief spell with Maritimo after coaching at Liverpool and RB Salzburg.

Fonseca was also namedropped in said report, and it has since been claimed by RMC Sport that the 53-year-old has said his goodbyes to his squad at the Groupama Stadium, with Lyon currently sat third in Ligue 1 after nine matches.

Sporting are also third in the Portuguese top-flight at present, but are already nine points behind leaders Porto, with Borges' final match in charge being a 2-0 away win against Casa Pia on Friday.

There are a number of young coaches in charge of Championship clubs right now - but who are the youngest?

It is, of course, a positive and a hindrance to clubs if their head coach is being eyed by clubs of a greater stature in terms of history or current divisional status.

Since taking charge 12 months ago, Matos has won 22 of his first 45 Swansea matches across all competitions, giving his side a strong platform to build from after a strong end to last season.

As well as being linked with the Sporting vacancy, which is set to be filled by Fonseca, the 38-year-old recently emerged as a potential target for UEFA Conference League holders, Crystal Palace, who have endured an underwhelming start to Pierre Sage's reign as they sit inside the Premier League's bottom three.

Five players, five careers. Name them from the clubs they played for.

Each day there are five current or former EFL players to identify. For each one you’ll see their senior clubs in the order they played for them. Loan spells are left out.

You get four guesses per player. Every wrong guess unlocks a clue: first their position, then their nationality, then their initials.

Get it first time for 4 points, then 3, 2 and 1. The best possible score is 20. A new set of players arrives at midnight.

Just a matter of weeks ago, Peixoto was in the firing line from sections of the Wolves fanbase after a disappointing run of form post-international break, but his team have since taken 10 points from 12 and are now just one place behind the Swans after 13 games.

Given the strength-in-depth at both his and Matos' disposal, both clubs will hope for stability in both the short and long-term to give themselves the best possible chance of success.

Wolves and Swansea fans, what is your reaction to this news? Comment below!

With another international break looming, they also have the chance to build on their weekend victories on Tuesday and Wednesday against Portsmouth and Bristol City respectively.

#2191. 6 Steve Evans replacements Bristol Rovers must consider as sack calls grow

After a nightmare few weeks, it is fair to say that pressure is increasing on Bristol Rovers manager Steve Evans.

Evans took over at the Memorial Stadium in December with Bristol Rovers sitting in the League Two relegation zone, but the 64-year-old led his side to a 14th-placed finish last season after a stunning second half of the campaign that included a run of eight consecutive victories.

The Gas' momentum continued into this season as they won four of their opening five games to top the table in early September, and as Evans' impressive work started to attract attention from elsewhere, he was said to have been on the radar of Scottish Premiership side Hibernian.

However, since a 1-0 win over Rotherham United on 5th September, Rovers have won just one of their last nine league games, and they slumped to a seventh defeat during that run as they were beaten 3-1 by Fleetwood Town at Highbury Stadium on Saturday.

As they continue to slide down the table, the Gas currently sit 17th, but while they are just four points clear of the relegation zone, they are also the same distance from the play-off places in what is an incredibly congested division.

After their latest defeat at Fleetwood over the weekend, growing numbers of Rovers fans are calling for Evans to be sacked, and we have looked at some of the potential replacements the club should consider if they decide to make a managerial change.

Stuart Maynard has been out of work since his shock departure from York City in July, just three weeks before the start of the season.

Maynard led the Minstermen to the National League title last season with an incredible total of 108 points, but owner Matt Uggla made the surprise call to part company with the 46-year-old over the summer, much to the dismay of the fanbase.

While Maynard's last managerial role was in the fifth tier, he previously had an 18-month spell in charge of Notts County in League Two, guiding the Magpies to a sixth-placed finish in the 2024-25 season before being dismissed following defeat to AFC Wimbledon in the play-off semi-finals.

It was reported that Maynard rejected an approach from National League side Hartlepool United in September, which suggests he may be eyeing up an EFL job, and he should be high on Bristol Rovers' wish list if they were to sack Evans.

If Bristol Rovers feel that Maynard is too much of a gamble, they could go for a manager with more recent experience of the division in former Salford City boss Karl Robinson.

Robinson led the Ammies to a fourth-placed finish in League Two last season, only missing out on the automatic promotion spots by a single point, but he was sacked in June after a 3-0 defeat to Notts County in the play-off final at Wembley.

The 46-year-old has achieved one promotion during his managerial career, having guided MK Dons to the Championship in 2016, while he also oversaw two play-off finishes in League One during his five-year spell in charge of Oxford United.

Robinson held talks with Peterborough United in September prior to the appointment of Robbie Savage, so he may be keen to hold out for a League One job, but the Gas would surely have a strong chance of tempting him back to the fourth tier.

Another manager with an excellent recent record at League Two level is ex-Bromley boss Andy Woodman.

Woodman took over at then National League side Bromley in March 2021, and after leading the Ravens to promotion to the EFL for the first time in their history in 2024, he defied the odds once again as he inspired his side to the League Two title last season.

However, after a tough start to life in League One that included a number of heavy defeats, Bromley parted company with Woodman last month, and the 55-year-old broke his silence on Monday to express his disappointment at his exit from the CopperJax Community Stadium.

Given that he has only just departed Bromley, Woodman may wish to take a break before returning to the dugout, particularly with emotions still running high about the way he was treated by his former employers, but he may find it difficult to turn down a club the size of Bristol Rovers.

Like Woodman, former Peterborough United boss Luke Williams is another manager to have been sacked by a League One club this season.

Williams saved Posh from relegation last season after taking over at the Weston Homes Stadium last October, but after an underwhelming summer transfer window, his side made a slow start to the new campaign, resulting in his departure in September.

While Williams' time at Peterborough did not go to plan, the 46-year-old led Notts County to promotion from the National League in 2023, and he steered Swansea City to a 14th-placed finish in the Championship in the 2023-24 campaign before being dismissed midway through the following season.

Williams' career is at something of a crossroads after his exit from Posh, which could mean that he may have to consider taking a job at a lower level than he would ideally like, but Bristol Rovers could be the perfect place for him to rebuild his reputation.

Although his stock has not fallen quite as low as Williams, it has been a tough few years for ex-Luton Town and Oxford manager Matt Bloomfield.

After taking his first steps into management with Colchester United, Bloomfield then made the move to Wycombe Wanderers, where he spent much of his playing career, and his side emerged as serious automatic promotion contenders in League One in the 2024-25 season.

Despite the Chairboys sitting second in the table at the time, Bloomfield opted to depart Adams Park to take over at Luton in January 2025, but he was unable to prevent their relegation from the Championship, and he was dismissed last October after an inconsistent start to life back in League One.

Bloomfield was handed another opportunity in the Championship by Oxford in January, but he suffered his second consecutive relegation after failing to save the U's from the drop, and he was sacked in June after just over five months in charge at the Kassam Stadium.

The 42-year-old's recent record does not make for good reading, but it could be argued that he was rather unfortunate in each of his last two managerial roles, and he would certainly arrive at Bristol Rovers with a point to prove.

Should Bristol Rovers sack Steve Evans or does he deserve more time at the Memorial Stadium? Tell us in the comments below!

Many of the above candidates are on the market, but if Bristol Rovers are willing to poach a manager who is currently employed, Worthing's Adam Hinshelwood could be an exciting option.

After a successful first spell at Worthing, Hinshelwood took over at then National League side York in February 2024, and after keeping the Minstermen in the division in his first season, he led them to a second-placed finish in the 2024-25 campaign before losing to Oldham Athletic in the play-off semi-finals.

Despite making an unbeaten start, Hinshelwood was sacked by York just four games into last season, and after making a surprise return to Worthing just over a month later, he guided the Rebels to the fifth tier for the first time in their history after winning the National League South title.

Hinshelwood's managerial reputation has continued to flourish this season, with Worthing currently sitting sixth in the table after an outstanding start to the campaign, and the Gas should consider swooping for the 42-year-old.

#2190. Alfred Johansson hails returning stars as Motherwell end seven-game wait for victory

Motherwell boss Alfred Johansson insists welcoming back a host of first-team regulars was the icing on the cake in their William Hill Premiership victory over St Mirren.

The Fir Park boss was delighted to break a seven-game winless run and he believes an easing injury list is another cause for celebration.

He said: “It was so good to be manager of Motherwell for this game and being able to put that quality onto the pitch in the second half. Wow, that makes a massive difference. Regan Charles-Cook came on and was involved in the penalty situation.

“Oscar Priestman had a huge influence as did Eythor Bjorgolfsson and Callum Hendry, so that is a big joy and also something we will be able to build on.

“There was a lot of joy and happiness in the locker room after the game. After the draw in midweek at St Johnstone there was a lot of anger, fire and frustration, so the emotions were different and we are delighted to get the win.

“Even more than relief I felt there was determination and this group have been doing very well recently. To get four points from our last two games brings only praise to the players.

“The most important thing was we never gave up anything, we were very solid defensively and we pressed well.

“The solidity is something we need to build on and offensively we need to create even more from the advantages we have.

“There were spells when we were going too direct at times and making the game a bit more 50-50. In the second half we had to focus on the things we needed to take care of to win this game.”

Saints boss Craig McLeish admits his side will get back on the training ground in a bid to rediscover their early-season form and regain some belief.

He said: “There is a lack of belief and we will get back in on Monday and work hard on regaining that freedom of play which marked our performances at the start of the season

“We didn’t do enough to test Motherwell, I don’t think their goalkeeper had a save to make.

“We got into some promising areas but lacked a bit of quality in the final third. There were some really promising periods and we got into promising areas but didn’t manage to take advantage of them.

“Motherwell are a good side and will maybe feel a bit aggrieved that they didn’t take more of their chances.”

#2187. How Hibernian made Hampden history against Hearts and booked final date with Rangers

Hibernian made a little piece of Hampden history this afternoon when they came from behind to beat Hearts in the second Premier Sports Cup semi-final.

The Easter Road club had lost all four of their previous meetings with their age-old Edinburgh adversaries at the Mount Florida venue before today.

When Claudio Braga put the Tynecastle men ahead in just the fourth minute it looked like they might be heading for another defeat.

But first-half goals from Martin Boyle and Jamie McGrath gave Hibs a deserved lead and they held on to book a place in the final against Rangers next month.

Marink Reedijk, who had failed to win any of his first four games as manager, savoured the victory as much as any supporter.

Here are five talking points from the last four meeting.

Stragglers were still taking their seats inside the packed stadium when Hearts broke the deadlock.

Braga got in between Jason Kerr and Marko Ivezic and on the end of a Calvin Miller cross in the Hibs six yard box and headed beyond Raphael Sallinger from a few yards out.

The Portuguese forward was mobbed by his team-mates on the touchline as the maroon half of the stadium celebrated wildly.

But there was not much more for them to shout about after they had edged ahead.

Hibs recovered superbly from the early setback. Felix Passlack, their captain, was unfortunate not to restore parity just a few minutes later after being sent through on goal by Joe Newell. Beau Reus just managed to keep his deflected attempt out.

Owen Elding also should have done better after being supplied by Adam Mayor. The striker shelled over when he only had the keeper to beat. But he atoned for his miss soon afterwards by teeing up the leveller.

He controlled a pass from Newell and then scooped a chip over the heads of the opposition defence to Boyle who turned a shot in off of Reus and the inside of the left post.

The Hearts players and fans appealed for offside but linesman Douglas Ross kept his flag down.

VAR officials Andrew Dallas and Nick Walsh had a long look back at the replay over at Clydesdale House and found that there colleague had made the correct call. Jordi Altena had played the winger on.

Jamie McGrath put his side in front with an opportunistic strike at a Boyle corner three minutes before half-time.

The ball broke to Newell, who had just skimmed the top of the crossbar from distance, and he burst forward and then unleashed a powerful shot which was blocked by Malachi Fagan-Walcott. McGrath was perfectly positioned to net the rebound.

Hibs fans had high hopes of seeing their struggling heroes produce some Total Football when Dutchman Reedijk replaced David Gray as manager at Easter Road last month.

There has, though, been little evidence of that in the former Ajax youth coach’s opening games.

His charges produced some nice passages of play after falling behind at Hampden and deserved to go in front. They dominated long spells of the encounter with their capital rivals. But they did so by winning their battles and bullying their opponents.

Josh Mulligan and Kerr were booked by referee David Dickinson for fouls on Stephen Kinglsey and Dhanda respectively. The players in green and white shirts were hungrier and far more physical.

Miller going off injured – he was replaced by Sabri Guendouz shortly after the half hour mark and was later seen hobbling about on crutches – did nothing to help Hearts’ cause. He had set up the opener and posed a threat whenever he got on the ball.

Still, they could have no complaints about the scoreline when they returned to their dressing room. Braga had headed a Josh McPake cross well wide after his side had fallen behind. But if he had found the target and levelled it would have flattered them.

Hearts, doubtless after a few choice words from their manager Vrancken, played with far greater purpose when the action resumed in the second half. Sallinger had to produce fine saves from both Braga and Guendouz to keep the Leith men in front.

McPake, who should be named in the Scotland squad for the Nations League games against North Macedonia and Switzerland on Tuesday, was a real handful throughout.

However, Hibs looked dangerous on the counter too. Reus had to deny Boyle and Ivezic and Kingsley slid in a denied Passlack on two occasions as well. It was, to use an old football cliché, real end-to-end stuff.

The meeting between Aberdeen and Rangers on Saturday evening had been a tense affair that was devoid of chances as well as a difficult watch for the neutral observer. This was the perfect antidote. Everyone in the 41,673-strong crowd was royally entertained.

This has been another wretched season for Hibs fans and they travelled along the M8 in hope rather than expectation.

The Leith men last won a William Hill Premiership game back in August and are in bottom spot in the top flight table.

But Passlack and his team-mates buried the memory of the Scottish Cup defeats that Hibs they had suffered against Hearts at Hampden in 2006, 2012 and 2022 and the League Cup loss they were on the receiving end of on the South Side of Glasgow in 1955.

There were tears in the eyes of their longsuffering followers during the rendition of Sunshine on Leith which they belted out following the final whistle.

If Hibernian perform as well in the final against Rangers next month then their fans may have more reason to party.

#2186. 'Nonsense!' - Ex-QPR & Southampton star Charlie Austin launches rant on social media

Former Southampton and QPR striker Charlie Austin has criticised coaches preying on gullible parents of young children trying to make it in the world of football.

The former forward has posted a message on social media in which he complained about coaches advertising the importance of ball mastery by the age of 10 or 12.

The 37-year-old’s playing career saw him reach the Premier League with the likes of QPR, the Saints and West Brom.

He also competed at a Championship level with the likes of Burnley, before moving to Australia in 2022 with Brisbane Roar.

Austin has since returned to British football, and he continues to compete at a non-league level.

However, he has also become a prominent voice in expressing his football opinions online, and this includes on his personal social media pages.

Austin has attacked the coaches that advertise their business by claiming that kids have to master certain skills with the ball by certain ages, suggesting that those claims are utter nonsense.

He believes that they are preying on gullible parents who won’t know any better, and that this is taking advantage of kids trying to fulfill their dream of making it as a professional footballer.

Pick any two players. Send the code, and your mate enters it here to play the same pair.

“I keep seeing coaches, etc. on Instagram talking about ‘oh, you’ve got to master these ball mastery skills by the age of 10. Oh you’ve got to do this by the age of five. Oh you’ve got to do this by the age of 12’. No you don’t,” said Austin, via Instagram.

Harry Redknapp has opened up on the reaction he received from Portsmouth fans when he took over at Southampton

“Just go about your business, and I certainly get you’re advertising your business, which is great, which is absolutely fine.

“But to come up with nonsense, spout nonsense to gullible parents — and there is plenty of gullible parents that want their kid to live the dream.

“And I get you want to charge £35 an hour, or £20 an hour to make a few quid because you don’t want to work, you don’t want to do the occasional nine to five job, or whatever, totally understand that.

“It’s all about growing your business, but seriously stop talking rubbish, stop hassling parents with nonsense.”

Austin originally started his career in the Reading academy system, but was released at the age of 15.

The striker took an unconventional career path from there, working his way through a number of non-league sides before earning an opportunity with Swindon Town at the age of 20.

He made 54 league appearances for the Robins after being given a place in the first team squad, which led to him signing for Burnley in 2011.

But it was at QPR where he first received a taste of Premier League football, helping the Hoops earn promotion from the Championship in 2013/14.

Austin scored an impressive 18 times in 2014/15, but it wasn’t enough to keep QPR in the top flight, with the club succumbing to relegation with a 20th place finish.

But the striker earned another shot at top flight football with a move to Southampton in 2015/16.

Injuries hampered his time at St. Mary’s, but he still contributed 16 goals and three assists in the division for the Hampshire outfit across four campaigns.

Austin went on to help West Brom earn Premier League promotion in 2019/20, but he played just five more times in the top flight in the remainder of his career.

Austin is clearly thinking about his own path to playing in the Premier League when going on this rant about kids needing to master certain skills by certain ages.

His opportunity to make it at the top level looked to be over as a teenager, but he was able to continue working on his own skills to eventually make it when he was in his 20s.

So it’s not too surprising that he is taking an issue with this kind of framing when it comes to underage player development, as he is an example that there is no perfect path to becoming a professional player.

Perhaps Austin should try his own hand at coaching in the future, as his experience could be quite a valuable asset for young kids to learn from.

#2185. Why Jeff Stelling will have one eye on Sheffield Wednesday this season

Sheffield Wednesday have confirmed Dave Challinor as their new manager, and with that appointment will come plenty of intrigue from League One fans and Jeff Stelling over how they'll cope with him in charge during the remainder of their campaign.

It seemed inevitable that, as soon as Simon Wilson left Stockport County to become Sheffield Wednesday's new Sporting Director, the ex-Hatters boss would be following suit.

Both departed Edgeley Park in the summer, having been key parts of their rise from the National League to the brink of the Championship after back-to-back third-placed finishes in League One. Now, they'll be looking to get to the second tier together in South Yorkshire.

Pick any two players. Send the code, and your mate enters it here to play the same pair.

The Wednesday job is a big one, but it's one that a lot of people agree Challinor deserves to take on, having experienced success everywhere he's been, from the Northern Premier League to the EFL, including at Hartlepool United, of which Stelling is an Honorary President.

Jeff Stelling is an iconic football television and radio presenter, and his voice has been associated with his boyhood club, Hartlepool United, for many years.

The 71-year-old has been an Honorary President at the club for over a decade now, having originally been appointed in 2015, before resigning in protest of then-owner Raj Singh in May 2025 and being re-appointed by new owner Landon Smith back in February.

It's been a real up-and-down 10 years at Victoria Park. Back in the 2016/17 campaign, the Monkey Hangers were relegated out of the Football League for the first time in their history. The man to take them back four years later was Dave Challinor.

Hartlepool had finished no higher than 12th in their first three seasons in the National League. But in his first full campaign at the club, Challinor led them to a play-off position (as he's become known to do in full seasons) and beat Torquay United on penalties in the final to return to the EFL.

It allowed Challinor to coach in the Football League for the first time, but just three months into the 2021/22 campaign, he'd leave for Stockport, whom they'd beaten in the play-off semi-final the year prior. Either way, the 51-year-old provided Stelling with plenty of great memories, and the two are still close five years on.

Ultimately, there was no bad blood from Stelling's perspective, as showcased by the fact that he has named one of his cats after the new Sheffield Wednesday manager.

In a story back in January 2021, while Challinor was still Hartlepool boss, it was revealed that the cat was welcomed into the Stelling home and named after him after he turned up on their doorstep.

Who are the biggest wind-up specialists in the EFL Championship right now? Football League World takes a deep dive...

And even despite the 51-year-old moving on, the cat hasn't had their name changed. Speaking on his talkSPORT breakfast show on Monday morning, Stelling spoke of Challinor's appointment at Hillsborough, predicting that he'd do a good job at his new club.

"Sheffield Wednesday have a new manager — my mate, Dave Challinor, and not Dave Challinor the cat; Dave Challinor the manager, obviously. I do have a cat called Dave Challinor," he joked.

"A terrific appointment, and one I feel will do a brilliant job there, because he’s done a brilliant job wherever he has been."

Challinor has a lot of credentials. He has a win percentage over 50% and has finished no lower than a play-off place in all 15 of his full seasons in management.

The 51-year-old has done a good job taking clubs up the footballing pyramid, which is exactly what Sheffield Wednesday want to do. You get the feeling, though, that this job will come with different pressures compared to his other roles.

We've already seen Wednesday fans turn on Henrik Pedersen quickly as soon as results started to fade. Even with four wins from five to begin the campaign, that performance in defeat against Bradford City was fixated on by a percentage of the fanbase.

Stockport were well backed over Challinor's tenure at Edgeley Park, but a lot of fans in the stands were content with being competitive and enjoying the ride they were on from the sixth tier to the third in the space of a decade.

Do you think Dave Challinor will be a success at Sheffield Wednesday? Let us know in the comments.

That romance won't be there at Hillsborough. This is a club and a fanbase that are demanding immediate success, and it'll be a real test of Challinor's managerial credentials in front of 30,000 loud Wednesday fans and sold-out away ends each week.

But there's a lot of confidence that he'll be able to thrive in this environment, and not just from Jeff Stelling. If he can lead Wednesday back to the Championship and maybe even beyond, perhaps there'll be a few more cats called Dave Challinor in South Yorkshire.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#2184. Manchester United confirmed lineup: Amad & Yoro return to starting lineup

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur return from the international break with plenty to prove when they meet at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Michael Carrick’s side have won just once in their last four domestic matches since beating Ipswich 5-2. A Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton was followed by a loss to 10-man Manchester City, before Manchester United drew with Everton and Fulham. Matheus Cunha’s late equaliser at Fulham rescued a point, but Manchester United still sit 12th.

Roberto De Zerbi’s side are bottom of the Premier League with only two points from their opening five games. Spurs have failed to score in four of those matches, while defeats against Aston Villa and Newcastle have added to the pressure.

Michael Carrick has named his starting eleven for the clash at Old Trafford, with Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans partnering in midfield as United look to get their season back on track.

Senne Lammens starts in goal, with Leny Yoro, Lisandro Martinez, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw forming the back four. Carrick has opted for Mainoo and Tielemans in the middle, with Amad Diallo, Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha tasked with supporting Bryan Mbeumo up front.

Leny Yoro had a brilliant international break where he made his debut for France. His performance on debut was enough for Zidane to praise the debutant.

Amad, after missing the start of the season with an injury, returns straightaway to the team.

Carlos Baleba starts on the bench and is expected to make his debut today. Marcus Rashford is also on the bench alongside Shea Lacey.

Lammens; Yoro, Martinez, Maguire, Shaw; Mainoo, Tielemans; Amad, Bruno Fernandes, Mbeumo; Cunha.

Mbeumo gets his place through the middle, while Amad and Cunha start on the wing after scoring the late equaliser against Fulham. Fernandes will be expected to start producing the numbers from last season after a lackluster start to the season, except against Ipswich, before the international break.

United need a response after a difficult run, but Tottenham arrive under pressure of their own. With both sides desperate for points, the starting lineups set the stage for an important afternoon at Old Trafford.

#2182. Palmer and Rogers show promise of star double act for Chelsea

The stirring of what might yet be a great partnership between Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, although it will need to be, given some of the chaos that endures at Chelsea.

This was a Premier League game played at a furious pace, and the two former Real Madrid team-mates in charge of the sides will not have seen much of the control all coaches seek. Xabi Alonso’s team eventually won with a goal from each of his attacking triumvirate of Rogers, Palmer and João Pedro – and at times it will have been painful for the new Chelsea manager.

That was chiefly the fault of Robert Sánchez, who was embraced afterwards by Alonso, having demonstrated just how damaging a shaky goalkeeper can be to any serious team. Álvaro Arbeloa’s Fulham had their moments – and the best ones were granted to them by Sánchez. At a club that is such a restless trader of footballers, it feels remarkable that Sánchez has endured for so long.

Alonso played down the significance of Sánchez’s errors, although he cannot seriously be considering sticking to his mantra of “relax and carry on”. That was, he said, his response to the first-half Sánchez mistake that let in Josh King’s shot for Fulham’s first goal. Sánchez could have done a lot better with Gonzalo García’s goal after the break.

Fulham have equalised against Chelsea thanks to Josh King's low strike 💥 pic.twitter.com/WCLKB7XqeE

Gonzalo Garcia has scored on his Premier League debut after Robert Sanchez spilled Castagne's shot 🤯 pic.twitter.com/BmP6eqwkuN

Chelsea have a lot of faith that Mike Penders, the 21-year-old Belgian on the bench for this game, will be their first-choice goalkeeper eventually. The situation seems rather more urgent and with Penders likely to feature against Luton Town on Thursday night in the Carabao Cup it would appear a big decision is looming for Alonso.

In terms of the Palmer-Rogers axis, this was very promising, although there was no doubting the senior figure in this. Palmer’s ball set João Pedro free in the first minute, the Brazilian lifting a well-judged nudge over Bernd Leno.

"A flying start under Xabi Alonso!" Chelsea lead against Fulham after just 31 seconds 🤯 pic.twitter.com/LrkYxOReFB

It was Palmer who was crucial to the second for Rogers, made by Maxence Lacroix on his debut. Palmer stroked in the third on 49 minutes with the easy confidence of a man in form.

A goal for Morgan Rogers on his Chelsea debut! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/hphe8y077v

"Cole Palmer back to his best!"Palmer has scored to double Chelsea's lead! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/zo6e0Vdcgq

“I am very happy for Cole,” Alonso said. “I have really enjoyed seeing him play with the dynamism and the freedom and the responsibility... when Cole feels this way we have a better team and a better Cole.”

Palmer makes it look very easy in this form, capable of switching the direction of play a beat before anyone else spots the opportunity. He and his old Manchester City academy friend Rogers came off before the end, Palmer having demonstrated some discomfort chasing a ball. Asked afterwards how ready he felt, Palmer responded in kind. “Did you not watch the game? I’m only joking, I’m ready... it was a difficult season with injuries and whatnot, but through the summer and since I’ve been back I’ve worked extra hard.”

If there was an attacker to compare with him on the other side it was King, who looks even better. The 19-year-old was way ahead of Arbeloa’s two young Real Madrid imports. García toiled away and took his chance, but César Palacios struggled for any impact in a position tucked in on the left. Oscar Bobb and King gave Fulham some edge but the concern, as ever, will be where Fulham get their goals.

Arbeloa pushed his full-backs high and encouraged Sander Berge to drop deep to get on the ball in the first passing phase. The Norwegian delayed too long in challenging João Pedro for Chelsea’s third – backing off and allowing Palmer to overlap to receive the pass.

Sánchez had not been the only concern for Chelsea. Back in the team, Levi Colwill misjudged a challenge on King in the first half and was relieved that the card was only yellow. Roméo Lavia took a wild swing at Calvin Bassey and was also booked. Moisés Caicedo was not fit to play. Enzo Fernández was on the bench and would come on in the second half to the kind of reception from opposition fans to which he will quickly become familiar.

There was a grin from the Argentine at those who berated him from the home stands when he returned at half-time. Fernández worked hard to transmit a general sense that the abuse did not land, although he will be relieved that the Chelsea fans were supportive. His future still feels very much in play.

It was Palmer’s subtle ball through that gave João Pedro the chance with 32 seconds of the game played. The ball came forward immediately from Lacroix’s firm header from defence. The Frenchman delivered a very accomplished assist for Rogers’s first-half goal. Before that King had equalised. There was an exchange with Timothy Castagne, and King looked up just inside the box and decided to have a swing at it. Sánchez was close enough to grasp the ball and somehow failed to do so.

Sánchez would later push a Castagne shot in the direction of García, who stooped and nodded the ball over the goalkeeper after Palmer had scored Chelsea’s third. This second error was unfortunate, but it is the kind of thing that happens to a goalkeeper as erratic as the one for whom Chelsea’s hierarchy seem to have such patience.

“We concede goals in the first minute, the end of the first half and the beginning of the second half and there are not worse moments to concede. But we showed character and personality and I am very proud of how my players responded. We deserved a little bit more but football is not about what you deserve, it is about what you take. If you lose against a team like Chelsea they [should] have to do a little bit more. For me, they are easy goals for them and mistakes we cannot make. We need to improve and be more ready in the first minute, that is for sure.

“We are on our way and we will keep improving. The first thing I want to see is a competitive team. We were tonight, we tried our best and tried to play our football against a team like Chelsea, which is not easy. I believe in them and I believe in young players. I think they have the energy and ambition I want and they fit in the way I play. Josh King is absolutely amazing. I am really happy with him. Gonzalo [Garcia] scored and Cesar [Palacios] did well. I think they need a bit more time but they are doing great and making an impact already.”

"Arsenal DON'T win the league if they have Ramsdale and not Raya" 🧤@Carra23 and @GNev2 think that upgrading the goalkeeper position could be the 'last piece' for Chelsea 🧩 pic.twitter.com/UBzMCFmxpp

The final whistle is blown at Craven Cottage and Chelsea hold on to win 3-2 to give Xabi Alonso a win in his first game in charge. Alvaro Arbeloa’s first game as Fulham boss ends in defeat. An absorbing west London derby.

Fulham fans think they are about to be awarded a free-kick right outside the box but instead the free-kick goes the other way. It was a clear dive from Bassey, who is rightly booked for simulation.

Double change for Fulham as Kevin and Sessegnon are brought on.

This is a very open, end-to-end game and you would fully expect more goals in this one. I would be very surprised if this one ended 3-2. Both defences are looking leaky.

Fulham are going to make their substitution of the night as Charles comes on for his debut having signed from Southampton, replacing Bobb.

Enzo is being booed a lot by the home fans every time he touches the ball.

There is a new rule being implemented. Hato takes far too long over a throw-in and Fulham are therefore awarded the throw-in instead.

When Palmer put Chelsea 3-1 up, the visitors looked in control of this match. Fast forward five minutes and the momentum has completely switched around. What an absorbing opening Monday night of the season!

There will be two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Both sides have been guilty of giving the ball away in dangerous areas and Fulham do so on this occasion. Palmer then curls an effort from the edge of the box but his shot goes just wide of the far post.

Fulham are on top at the moment and Chelsea are lucky shaky as they are under the cosh inside their own box. King is playing really well, finding pockets of space down Fulham’s right and looking a real threat.

Fernandez was booed by some Chelsea supporters in pre-season, but there were no loud jeers from the away end during the team announcements.

“During the week they had a few setbacks. With Moises [Caicedo], and with any [player], we do not want to take too much risk. They were not ready to play tonight. We need to go week-by-week but for tonight they were not ready.”

No more excuses. No more jam tomorrow. It is time for Chelsea to fight for the Premier League title this season. Anything else should be deemed a disappointment.

This is Chelsea version 3.0 under BlueCo, who bought the club four years ago. First there was Todd Boehly’s trolley dash, then came Behdad Eghbali’s youth club. This summer the focus has been on being Premier League-ready.

Off the pitch, the timing might be right for Boehly to be discussing the sale of his shares to Eghbali’s Clearlake Capital. But on it, Chelsea look better equipped to re-enter the title conversation than at any point in the BlueCo era.

Two former Liverpool, Real Madrid and Spain teammates go head-to-head in the dugouts at Craven Cottage as Fulham host Chelsea in a west London derby to round out the opening weekend of the new Premier League season. Alvaro Arbeloa and Xabi Alonso were teammates at Liverpool, Real Madrid and Spain and both had stints as Real Madrid manager last season but have new homes in London. Arbeloa has replaced Marco Silva, who is now at Benfica, whilst Alonso is Liam Rosenior’s permanent replacement. This is the first time a manager’s Premier League debut has come against someone he also played alongside in the competition.

“I know Alonso well because I have watched so many games of his teams,” Arbeloa said. “We have to be ready, and if we want to beat them we will have to play very well. I spoke to Xabi a few days ago. But not about football; both of our families are coming to London, and we are very good friends, until Monday night [tonight]. We will be there on the touchline, so close for 90 minutes, and we will give everything for our clubs. For those 90 minutes, we are not friends.”

Arbeloa has gone back to his former club to add a couple of players in the shape of Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios. The opening weekend has not served Fulham well of late; they have won just one of their last six Premier League opening weekend fixtures. They concluded their pre-season with a 1-0 win over Stuttgart.

Chelsea have been very active in the transfer market this summer, breaking the British transfer record to sign Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa as well as adding experience through the likes of Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck, whilst the likes of Marc Cucurella, Andrey Santos and Trevoh Chalobah have moved on. They finished off their pre-season with a 3-1 victory over Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge just over a week ago.

“We feel ready,” Alonso said. “We have prepared the whole pre-season with some players from the first day, other ones coming later, but the desire, the ambition, the hunger to start the Premier League is already in the building each training [session] and we are looking forward to it.”

Enzo Fernandez has been strongly linked with a move away this summer, with Manchester City’s interest well-known.

“Enzo is a Chelsea player,” Alonso added. “He is a top, top player. He is training really well since he started 10 days ago with the team, very integrated. We are happy with him and he is getting ready for Monday. He is training really well, good attitude and that is what we want. He is trying his best to prepare for the kick-off of the Premier League.”

These sides finished on the same number of points (52) last season, with Chelsea finishing ahead on goal difference. It was one win apiece for each club in the two Premier League meetings last season. Nearly a year ago, Chelsea won 2-0 at Stamford Bridge whilst Fulham won 2-1 in this fixture at Craven Cottage back in January. Chelsea have won six of the past eight Premier League meetings at Craven Cottage.

#2181. Michael Carrick reacts to Man Utd boos after Tottenham draw

Michael Carrick admitted Manchester United’s 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur was a painful result, after his side failed to protect the lead against 10-man Tottenham at Old Trafford.

Manchester United looked set to claim three points when Bryan Mbeumo scored in the second half off Cunha’s low cross, but Dominic Solanke’s late equaliser in injury time left Carrick facing more questions on United’s performance and his future.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, the United manager felt his players improved after the break but failed to handle the situation when victory was within reach.

“It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time,” Carrick said.

“But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position – we should see it through. We have to manage those situations.”

United have now conceded two late goals that have cost them valuable points, something Carrick believes has made their position look worse than it might have otherwise.

Asked whether a lack of confidence had contributed to United’s slow start, he disagreed but admitted matches can quickly slip away from his side.

The boos at half-time and full-time also clearly affected him.

“It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”

The Easter Road outfit saw off their Edinburgh rivals in the derby clash at Hampden on Sunday to seal their spot in the cup final against Rangers to be played on December 13.

#2179. Bryan Mbeumo reacts to Man Utd draw with Tottenham

Bryan Mbeumo admitted Manchester United have work to do after their frustrating 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur, despite scoring a superb second-half goal at Old Trafford.

The Cameroon international put Manchester United ahead in the 73rd minute, finishing in the far corner after Matheus Cunha created the opportunity from a low cross. However, Dominic Solanke’s stoppage-time equaliser denied Michael Carrick’s side a much-needed victory, even though Tottenham had been reduced to 10 men following Rodrigo Bentancur’s red card.

Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2).

3 – Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2). Disadvantage? pic.twitter.com/DuSpvymZfu

Speaking to Sky Sports after the game, Mbeumo acknowledged that United had taken too long to find their rhythm.

“We took time to get into the game, but we played well in the second half. In the first half, that wasn’t us, we had to change. We tried to get at them,” he said.

Mbeumo recognised the threat Tottenham posed and admitted the result was disappointing, particularly given United’s position in the game before Solanke’s late goal.

“We know Spurs have good players who can be dangerous. It’s a bit disappointing, we need to work on things.”

United have struggled for consistency in the opening weeks of the season, and dropping points after taking the lead will do little to ease the pressure on Carrick. Mbeumo, however, insisted the team must look ahead rather than dwell on the setback.

“We need to keep going forward, as we have a lot of games.”

Michael Carrick was pleased with Mbeumo’s contribution, highlighting both the quality of his finish and the different roles he has played since joining United.

“Bryan’s done great. It was a fantastic finish again; he’s obviously played different roles for us but we know what he offers,” the United manager said.

“He’s got good quality and obviously the more goals he scores, the better. He’s doing really well for us.”

Mbeumo’s goal was one of the few bright moments in another difficult afternoon for United. Carrick’s team must now find a way to turn things around from here after just six points from six games.

#2178. Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp tear into Man Utd after Tottenham draw

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United have come under fresh criticism after their disappointing 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur, with Sky Sports pundits Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp questioning the team’s performance and the challenges facing Michael Carrick.

Manchester United looked on course for a much-needed victory at Old Trafford after Bryan Mbeumo put them ahead in the second half. However, despite Tottenham being reduced to 10 men, Dominic Solanke’s late equaliser denied Carrick’s side all three points.

Gary Neville felt Tottenham deserved the points, pointing to Solanke’s late goal and his impact as Tottenham captain.

“Tottenham deserved a point. That was a really important moment for Solanke. He’d missed some big chances and was captain for the first time,” Neville said on Sky Sports.

“They were the better team by far. If they’d left without a point, it would have been terrible for them.”

The former United defender also expressed concern about what the result means for Carrick, who faces increasing pressure to improve performances and results.

“Michael Carrick is left with a lot to think about. It was a worrying day in terms of the level of performance and a big week ahead.”

Manchester United spent massively in the summer to overhaul their midfield. However, Jamie Redknapp was critical of the performance he saw on the pitch.

“I do not see enough connections in that midfield, and they look devoid of any confidence, ideas, or patterns of play, playing out the back,” Redknapp said.

“Tottenham were just much better than them in every department, but that is a theme this season.”

The former Liverpool midfielder also questioned United’s energy and attacking organization, suggesting the squad is not strong enough to meet the demands placed upon it.

“Their energy levels are not good enough, and they look loose going forward; there was no real structure.”

Redknapp added that Carrick cannot fix every issue alone, insisting the manager needs backing to improve the squad.

“The squad is not good or strong enough, and Michael [Carrick] needs help in that respect.”

#2177. 13 players set to miss QPR vs Burnley ft £20m striker

It's an action-packed week in the Championship before the November international break, with a full slate of midweek games on the horizon.

It's been a real feast-or-famine month for QPR since the return from the last break. After a 1-1 draw against West Ham United in their first game back, Julien Stephan's side have alternated between big wins and defeats in their last four, all by at least a three-goal margin.

After a 4-1 defeat at Southampton on Saturday, they return to Loftus Road to hopefully continue that pattern against a struggling Burnley side.

The Clarets year-long wait for a win at home continued against Portsmouth in Fabio Celestini's first game in charge following the sacking of Nicky Hayen, but it was a promising performance which arguably warranted all three points and at least saw them keep a clean sheet.

Now they're on the hunt to climb out of the bottom three, but against an unpredictable QPR side, grabbing just their second win of the season may be quite difficult.

Nevertheless, it promises to be an exciting matchup in the capital, but these 13 players won't be available for it.

Once again, QPR were forced to end the game at Southampton with ten men due to injury, as Alfie Lloyd, who had just come on 14 minutes earlier, came off with what seemed to be a hamstring issue.

The 23-year-old had just returned from a couple of games on the sidelines, too, which must be incredibly difficult to take. It's unknown how long this fresh setback will keep him out for.

QPR boss Julien Stephan revealed in late October that a trio of key players will be out until after the international break. One of whom is Nicolas Madsen, who has been one of their more impressive players since the Frenchman took over ahead of last season.

The Danish midfielder picked up his first three goal involvements of the campaign against West Ham and Derby County, but after being unused from the bench in the defeat at Birmingham City, it was revealed he'll be on the sidelines for a few weeks.

Injury issues are the main reason why someone with the quality of Tariq Lamptey has found himself playing in the second tier this season. The former Chelsea and Brighton and Hove Albion man signed for QPR off the back of an ACL injury picked up at Fiorentina.

The 26-year-old returned from an ankle problem against West Ham, but managed to re-injure it in his 21-minute cameo off the bench. He will also be out of action until after the international break.

Striker Rumarn Burrell has battled injury issues throughout 2026, clouding what was a brilliant start to his life at Loftus Road last season. His ten league goals came in 26 games before he went down in January.

Now, an issue picked up during the last international break with Jamaica will see him out of action until the following break. Richard Kone has done a good enough job stepping up in his absence, with four goals in that time.

Amadou Mbengue will miss the remainder of the 2026/27 campaign after he was forced off early in their win over Derby with a devastating ACL injury.

The right-back started seven of the opening ten games this season, and will be a big miss over the coming year at Loftus Road.

Dastan Satpaev has had a really frustrating loan spell at Burnley so far. The 18-year-old arrived with plenty of promise from Chelsea and has looked exciting, but hasn't been able to stay fit for lengthy periods.

New Clarets boss Fabio Celestini confirmed that he faces yet another spell on the sidelines with a hamstring issue, after he missed the goalless draw with Portsmouth.

Armando Broja hasn't enjoyed the best of stints at Burnley since arriving from Chelsea, either. The Albanian international was bought for up to £20 million by the Clarets ahead of their Premier League return last summer, but has scored just one goal.

He's yet to find the net this season, and that wait looks set to continue, as he faces time out with a groin injury he picked up in Nicky Hayen's final game at Lincoln City.

Celestini admitted he doesn't know how long Broja will be on the sidelines for, but it will be a few weeks at least.

In what is currently an injury crisis in the forward areas, Zeki Amdouni's absence due to an ankle injury he picked up midway through October is the biggest frustration at Turf Moor.

The Swissman had finally started to find his feet in a Burnley shirt after a stint which has so far seen him sent out on loan the last time they were in the Championship, only to pick up an ACL injury upon his return last summer.

But after three goals in four games, he's been out and will remain out until later this month.

Jacob Bruun Larsen saw his momentum halted last month, too, after coming back from the international break with a bit more purpose. He scored two and assisted one in three games, adding to the two assists he picked up earlier in the year.

The Danish wideman suffered a stress fracture in their defeat against Wolves, and won't be seen until the New Year.

Mike Tresor's disastrous spell at Burnley has continued into this season.

After his initial loan spell was made permanent for £15.4 million following their relegation from the Premier League in 2024, the 27-year-old has played just 13 times in over two years.

The two-time Belgian international made the first four matchday squads of the Championship season, but has been sidelined since that 1-1 draw with Middlesbrough two months ago.

#2176. ‘Embarrassing themselves!’ Jamie Carragher hits back at Rio Ferdinand over Cristiano Ronaldo defence

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Jamie Carragher has taken aim at Rio Ferdinand for defending Cristiano Ronaldo following the Portuguese forward’s latest controversy with his national team.

Ronaldo has found himself at the centre of a growing dispute after abruptly leaving Portugal’s national team camp following a reported disagreement with head coach Jorge Jesus. The incident has prompted strong reactions from former teammates and pundits, with Ferdinand firmly siding with the Al-Nassr star.

Jamie Carragher, however, believes Ronaldo’s reputation should not shield him from criticism when his behaviour becomes difficult to defend.

Rio Ferdinand, who played alongside Cristiano Ronaldo at Manchester United between 2003 and 2009, criticised Jorge Jesus for the way he handled the situation.

Speaking on his Rio Presents podcast, the former United captain criticised Jesus for not showing respect to Cristiano Ronaldo.

“Cristiano Ronaldo was put in a very bad situation and was treated in an inappropriate way. He has an enormous history in football. Jorge Jesus did not deal with Ronaldo well and chose to treat him in that way, but I cannot find any explanation for it,” Ferdinand said.

Despite Jesus being Portugal’s manager, Ferdinand questioned his standing, comparing him with the likes of Sir Alex Ferguson and Pep Guardiola. To say the least, Ferdinand only embarrassed himself doing that.

Jamie Carragher saw the argument very differently and rightfully so.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, the former Liverpool defender suggested that Ferdinand’s friendship with Ronaldo was influencing his reaction to the incident.

“People think it’s good to be close to people in the game, but this is where it becomes a problem,” Carragher explained.

He then called out both Ferdinand and broadcaster Piers Morgan, who has also been vocal in his support of Ronaldo.

“People like Piers Morgan and Rio Ferdinand, who are big people in the media whether you like them or not, are embarrassing themselves with the nonsense that they’re coming out with because they know Ronaldo. You can know someone and try to look after them, but you cannot defend the indefensible.”

Carragher believes Ronaldo’s achievements should not put the forward beyond criticism, particularly when his actions involve his national team and its management.

Gary Neville, who also played with Cristiano Ronaldo, has questioned Ronaldo’s handling of the situation, despite his longstanding affection for his former Manchester United teammate.

Neville argued that Ronaldo’s public response had made matters worse and the forward needed to accept criticism rather than expect others to defend him.

“With Cristiano, it’s difficult because I love him, but I can’t watch what happened at United in his second period and then see him make a statement like that without saying something. He has to be pulled up on that and told that it isn’t acceptable,” Neville said.

He also suggested Ronaldo’s extraordinary success, wealth and influence could have contributed to a sense that he was beyond challenge.

“When you have a billion pounds in the bank, the achievements he has had and the power he has, you feel you’re unbreakable, you feel you’re unstoppable,” Neville added.

Despite his criticism, Neville does not believe the episode will define Ronaldo’s legacy permanently. He expects the attention to fade once the forward retires, allowing his achievements on the pitch to take centre stage again.
