#2089. If West Ham Cannot Sack Nuno – Then He Must Make These Immediate Changes

Calls for West Ham United manager Nuno Espírito Santo to be sacked are growing louder following consecutive home defeats against Southampton and West Bromwich Albion. The Hammers have dropped to eighth in the Championship, and supporters are understandably questioning whether the Portuguese coach is capable of leading the club back to the Premier League.

I certainly fall squarely into the camp of people who don’t believe Nuno can either motivate his players or outsmart many of his rival Championship managers. The football has become stale, the team looks disjointed and there is precious little evidence of a manager getting the best out of what should be a very competitive squad.

But if we’re absolutely honest with ourselves, I suspect most West Ham supporters would acknowledge that Nuno is nowhere near being sacked. So rather than simply demanding his removal, perhaps the more useful question is what he can actually change to get this team playing better.

There are several reasons why I suspect Espírito Santo will remain in charge for the foreseeable future.

Firstly, West Ham are still in a state of flux regarding the club’s ownership structure. Until the proposed changes involving Vanessa Gold’s shareholding are completed and the i’s are dotted and t’s crossed, there remains uncertainty about precisely who will be making the biggest decisions.

Secondly, despite bringing in the best part of £200million through summer player sales, there are questions about how much money the club actually has available. Whether West Ham would be willing or able to fund another managerial dismissal and appointment is unclear.

And thirdly, if Daniel Křetínský is indeed calling the shots, Nuno is very much the manager he backed to lead the club through this Championship campaign.

Which leaves us with a rather uncomfortable situation. A manager whose football is becoming increasingly difficult to defend, but who may nevertheless be extremely secure in his job.

The first thing I’d change is the defence.

Nuno needs to abandon the experiment of playing Morato at left-back and select a proper full-back in that position.

I appreciate that Morato has performed reasonably well at times, and his versatility has been useful. But ultimately he’s a central defender, and I don’t believe the arrangement is helping West Ham develop a balanced team.

Whether Nuno selects Adama Boiro or Ollie Scarles doesn’t particularly matter to me at this stage.

We need better balance, more natural movement down the left and defenders playing in positions they understand.

As I’ve said previously, Arne Engels appears to be guaranteed a game irrespective of how he performs. Meanwhile, Nuno seems to believe he can win the Championship without consistently selecting a recognised defensive midfielder.

West Ham have a wealth of options in central midfield, yet we repeatedly find ourselves overrun, unable to retain possession and exposed whenever opponents break forward.

For that reason, I think it’s probably time to change the midfield completely.

I’d be tempted to give Lewis Orford another opportunity alongside either Edson Álvarez or Soungoutou Magassa.

Both Álvarez and Magassa offer the possibility of greater defensive protection, something West Ham have been desperately lacking.

And with a more secure base behind him, Divine Mukasa could finally be deployed in his best position as a number ten.

He’s a wonderfully gifted young footballer, but we’re wasting too much of his ability by asking him to drop deep and collect possession from the centre-backs.

Get him further up the pitch, give him some protection behind him and let him start opening up opposition defences.

Between the sticks, Mads Hermansen hasn’t exactly covered himself in glory.

I’m not suggesting every goal West Ham concede is his fault, because the defending in front of him has frequently been dreadful.

But when a team is struggling this badly, nobody should be guaranteed their place simply because they’ve been selected regularly.

Nuno has an ex PCG goalkeeper in Alphonse Areola at his disposal… surely it’s worth a try?

Which brings us to the striking department.

Leading up to the Southampton game, plenty of people were keen to repeat the fallacy that West Ham couldn’t win football matches without Pablo.

It’s worth remembering that Pablo didn’t start the Hammers’ 6-0 victory against Wrexham, which I consider our most convincing performance of the season.

And following back-to-back defeats in which the £23million striker started both matches, I suspect that particular myth has been exposed to all but his most vociferous supporters.

I don’t question Pablo’s effort. He works hard, puts himself about and certainly isn’t afraid of making a tackle.

Unfortunately, those qualities alone don’t make somebody an effective Championship striker.

For that reason, I’d be inclined to give Joël Piroe, our only proven Championship goalscorer among the recognised centre-forwards, a proper opportunity to establish himself.

He hasn’t been given anything resembling a consistent run in the side, and I struggle to understand how Nuno can properly assess his options without giving him one.

I’m not suggesting Piroe is guaranteed to solve our problems.

Of course, all these changes will count for very little unless Nuno can find a way to motivate his players.

I have little doubt that West Ham possess a number of talented footballers, many of whom I suspect would look considerably better under different coaches.

Once the players cross that white line, tactics, organisation and selection become equally important.

And that is where Nuno continues to let himself down.

Whether any of my suggestions would make a significant difference, I genuinely don’t know.

But I do know that repeating the same errors time and again isn’t going to get West Ham back into contention for automatic promotion.

The players who have consistently underperformed need to be dropped, and those who haven’t had much of an opportunity deserve a chance.

We have enough players in this squad to try something different.

And frankly, that’s probably the best we can hope for at the moment.

Because as much as some West Ham supporters might wish for Nuno Espírito Santo’s removal, I suspect he’s currently extremely secure in his job.

Which means if West Ham are going to improve, the manager who created many of these problems is probably going to have to be the one who solves them.

Kris Gonzo (commonly known to the West Ham community as Gonzo) is the co-founder of Hammers Chat (established 2014) and the lead video content creator and columnist for Claret and Hugh.

A lifelong Hammer since the legendary 10-0 victory over Bury, when he isn't providing daily match analysis on the Hammers Chat YouTube Channel or broadcasting on X (@GONZObignose), he can be found walking his dog and restoring classic pinball machines.

#2088. What Celtic are 'ruing' amid poor form and just three wins in last 10

Celtic have been left "ruing" the hierachy's failure to equip Martin O'Neill with the transfers he sought early on in the summer.

That's the view of Alex Rae who believes the Hoops are struggling with poor results and performances as a result of a lack of planning and signings early doors.

Celts spent big on the likes of Camilo Duran, Kasper Hogh and Mika Baur before a late flurry in the window to bring in loan players while being unable to strengthen to replace Arne Engels with a defensive minded midfielder.

That has come back to bite the league leaders and they have won just three of their last 10 fixtures in all competitions.

Rae reckons, after their most recent 2-0 defeat to Falkirk, that the Glasgow giants might regret their business or lack thereof in the signing stakes. And the higher-ups will know it.

"I think John McGlynn's done an incredible job but I'd imagine a lot of the calls will be about Celtic and their current form," Rae said on Superscoreboard.

"It's been very indifferent to say the least and there's been people clamouring for the hierarchy to support the manager a lot quicker than the window just closing.

"It didn't quite happen and now they're ruing that because they're not getting the performances on the pitch."

#2087. Newcastle United v Everton preview ahead of tonight’s St James’ Park match

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Welcome to the Newcastle United v Everton preview.

Newcastle look for revenge against the Toffees on Monday night as the two clubs face-off for the second time in just five days.

The blues got the better of United first time around when dumping the 2025 champions out of the League Cup and the Toon will be desperate to get their season back on track following such disappointment.

Three points for either side would have them in the top seven of the Premier League. The match will once again take place on live TV and a global audience will be waiting to see if the Toon can build on their win over Crystal Palace last weekend, as we look to put together a run of form ahead of the busy Christmas period that can make or break a season.

Newcastle have won two, drawn one and lost three of their last six league matches. Wins have come against Hull City and Crystal Palace whilst we’ve drawn with Bournemouth despite going 2-0 down. Defeats away to Leeds and Coventry saw the Toon get battered 4-1 on both occasions whereas Villa also took three points from St James Park in our last home match. The Toon have scored eight goals in these six matches but conceded a whopping twelve. The seven points gained has us twelfth in the league but a win would see us in seventh place.

Everton have only won one of their last six matches and have lost their last two in a row, drawing the other three. They beat Ipswich 1-0, drew with Tottenham, Man United and Hull and lost to both Chelsea and Arsenal. They’ve scored five goals in these six matches and conceded eight. A win on Monday would see them leapfrog the Toon and rocket seven places up the league. The Toffees were unbeaten in all competitions before the last two league matches so will be determined to alleviate this slump before it sees them slide towards a relegation scrap.

A quirk of the fixture list saw the two sides play each other in their last match having been drawn together at the Hill Dickinson stadium in the League Cup. Despite a promising start for United, this was ultimately a night to forget. Everton survived some early pressure before taking a two-goal lead into halftime. A number of substitutions saw the Toon attempt to wrest some momentum back from the Toffees. Any romantic notion of a famous comeback however was dispelled in the sixty-ninth minute when Everton scored again to take a three-goal advantage. There was still time for Dan Burn to net a late consolation but it was too little, too late as Everton dashed out Wembley dreams.

Newcastle haven’t beaten Everton in their last three visits to St James’ Park.

The Toon have lost only once in five home matches in all competitions this season.

NUFC have scored thirteen goals in their past eight home matches against Everton.

The 2007/08 season had very few highlights under Sam Allardyce who was thankfully shown the door in January. Big Sam had overseen only seven Premier League victories in twenty-one matches at the Toon. The Toffees visited St James’ Park in early October and the two sides played out a quite incredible five-goal thriller. Newcastle were the better team in the first half but were wasteful in front of goal as misses from Martins, N’Zogbia and Geremi looked to ensure that the teams were to go into the half-time break goalless. Thankfully Nicky Butt volleyed home at the Leazes End just before the interval to give the Toon the initiative. Anyone thinking this would mean NUFC would have things all their own way however were to have another thing coming when Johnson equalised just a few minutes into the second half to place the tie on a knife edge. An end-to-end second forty-five saw both sides push for a winner without really looking like they believed it possible until late substitutes were to make the difference. With just five minutes left, Emre picked up the ball outside of the area and unleashed an absolute rocket into the bottom corner from fully twenty-five yards out. A few minutes later, the Turkish midfielder turned provider when floating a freekick into the danger zone for Michael Owen to nod a header in off the bar and seal the destination of the points. There was still time for a wicked deflection to completely bamboozle Shay Given and end up in the back of the net but this was followed by the final whistle as United were able to celebrate three memorable points. Newcastle 3-2 Everton.

Antony Gordon came through the youth system at Everton having joined their academy at eleven years old. He made his debut in the Europa League aged just sixteen and spent six years at the Toffees. He played sixty-five league matches and scored seven goals over a six year period. He joined Newcastle in January 2023 under difficult circumstances following a well-publicised incident where he was harassed by supporters when leaving the stadium following a 0-0 draw with Southampton. He’d go on to enjoy an eventful three and half years at St James Park as NUFC qualified twice for the Champions League and he helped United to Wembley for the 2025 League Cup final, finally breaking a long-standing trophy duck in 2025. The 2025 League Cup would show both the good and bad of Anthony Gordon, scoring crucial goals in both legs of a semi-final success but being suspended for the final for a needless sending off just a few weeks later, meaning he missed out on playing in the greatest game of our recent history. He signed for Barcelona for over sixty-nine million pounds a few months back having scored twenty-four league goals in one-hundred-and-eleven appearances.

Paul Gascoigne was arguably one of the most naturally talented players to have ever come out of our country. Born in Gateshead, he made his debut for the Toon in 1985 and scored twenty-five goals in one-hundred appearances before signing for Tottenham in 1988. A million words could be written about ‘Gazza’ both on and off the pitch, books can and have been written about such an enigmatic figure. His story is eventful, intriguing, funny and tragic in equal measure. He played for Everton from 2000-2002 and scored a single goal in thirty-two league matches.

David Ginola was perhaps one of the most exciting players ever to represent NUFC in the Premier League era. Highlights of his two years on Tyneside include superb goals against Sheffield Wednesday, Man United and Ferencvaros, whilst equally memorable was his ability to whip the ball into the box loading the bullets for Sir Les and then Shearer to fire home. Tragically sold to Spurs by Kenny Dalglish in the same summer that Ferdinand also went to White Hart Lane, Ginola became something of a pantomime villain when playing against NUFC for the remainder of his career. Thankfully his retirement has seen a thawing in relations and he’s rightly remembered by Toon fans as a modern day legend. He played for Everton in 2002 but made only five league appearances for the Toffees.

Matthias Jaissle after a 3-1 defeat away at Everton in the League Cup: “Shocking and frustrating but if you just see the bigger picture, we did well in many aspects of the game. We of course are disappointed with the result, it’s also a bit shocking at the moment because overall the game was not that bad, but it’s the story of the season so far, that in situations where it really counts we lack the clinical approach to solve the situations. Just thinking about the first goal, it’s no risk zone, we clear the ball and nothing happens, and a couple of seconds later we concede a goal out of nothing. The second one is also frustrating in my point of view, we deserved to have a penalty then we miss in a transition to defend our own box which again is difficult to accept. We have clear rules then how to behave. We need to learn quickly. For me it’s about being mature in the situations, more clinical to solve the situations and not allowing almost a gift for the opposition to score. It feels like the opposition is not giving us these gifts at the moment so we need to avoid that.”

David Moyes after a 3-1 win against Newcastle United: “I thought it was a tough game. Newcastle had moments in the game but I think the Premier League is a bit like this at the moment. I think the games are quite close. You could be defending for twenty minutes and then you might be better for another twenty minutes. I think the games are very tight. Obviously we got the goals at good times, certainly the third goal sort of killed the game off at that time when Newcastle were probably better at the start of the second half.”

Newcastle United fans food bank will once again be collecting opposite the Gallowgate end and gratefully receiving food, money and toiletries for those in need. Of particular interest are non-perishable food and drink items (such as noodles, pasta, rice, canned food, soup, cereal, cordial, long life milk etc) as well as toiletries such as shower gel, shampoo, toothpaste and sanitary products. Please give whatever you can, any donation is very much appreciated.

For further info and/or to donate online go to Newcastle Foodbank

Thursday night was hugely disappointing for everyone concerned with NUFC for a number of reasons. The carrot of a match against League Two Fleetwood Town for a place in the cup semi-final was carelessly tossed away. That’s gone now and it’s important we build up a head of steam in the Premier League having got things back on track last weekend with a win over Crystal Palace. Newcastle need revenge against Everton and I fancy us to get it with two early goals putting the match to bed in the first half. Newcastle 2-0 Everton.

#2085. “One of the best nights of my life” – Bologna duo react after comeback win vs. Milan

Samuel Mbangula labelled scoring a hat-trick against AC Milan as ‘one of the best nights’ of his life, as he fired Bologna to victory.

It was a rollercoaster night at San Siro, one in which Milan trailed early on, then came back to lead, before a complete collapse in the second half that left sections of the fans jeering as the final few minutes played out.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Milan trailed early to a goal from Samuel Mbangula, but they went into half-time 2-1 up thanks to Alphadjo Cisse’s brace. The second half was a disaster though as an own-goal and two more from Mbangula allowed Bologna to inflict a first league defeat of the season on the Rossoneri.

Mbangula spoke to DAZN after the full-time whistle to give his thoughts on what was a very memorable evening for him, as he opened his account for his new club after the summer move.

“It’s one of the best nights of my life. First hat-trick of my career, I hope it’s not the last. It was a beautiful victory. The coach has great confidence, everyone is strong and can play. We are united, today is a team victory,” he said (via MilanNews).

Alongside the match-winner, Bologna goalkeeper Lukasz Skorupski spoke to DAZN about the victory as well, praising the strength of the team’s reaction.

“Perhaps the best thing was the team’s reaction. We were down 2-1, but in the end we won 4-2. We’ll enjoy it tonight, then we’ll immediately think about Saturday, where we have another match. Mbangula’s hat-trick? I told him he has to take us out to dinner next week.”

#2083. West Ham v Cardiff City | The numbers that shout loud and clear for one particular change in Nuno’s line-up

This week should never have become a narrative of two tough away fixtures becoming ‘must win’, but with West Ham United kissing goodbye to six points at London Stadium in the last seven days, there’s now an urgency to try and claw them back.

Cardiff City on Wednesday and Blackburn Rovers on Saturday will offer stern tests once again, with opponents now emboldened and egged on by the Hammers’ very well known first half frailties.

Both teams will more than likely launch a Millwall-style opening half hour storm which the Irons will have to withstand. They cannot say they haven’t been warned.

Matthias Jaissle has issued a statement of intent ahead of the Everton match tonight..

Newcastle United looking to bounce back from Thursday’s Carabao Cup defeat at Everton.

Though at the same time follow up their last Premier League game, a 2-0 win at Crystal Palace.

Ahead of this Everton challenge tonight, Matthias Jaissle declaring: “”I must acknowledge the disappointment we all felt following Thursday night’s Carabao Cup game at Everton, especially with such an incredible away following of nearly 8,000 supporters. There is no time to feel sorry for ourselves and make excuses – we have to learn quickly, understand what went wrong and where we need to be better, and then make sure we put it into action with a response on the pitch tonight.”

Newcastle United will go seventh top if winning against Everton.

The German Head Coach telling Newcastle United fans: “We showed our intent with the number of chances created and, after making a really promising start to the game on Thursday, I felt like we were in a strong position to build on the win at Crystal Palace. That is the nature of football at this level and over the weekend at the training ground we have been really focused on identifying and working on the areas we need to improve.”

Matthias Jaissle stating: “I have said many times already that we are going through a period of transition and we fully expect to experience ups and downs this season, as the last week has shown. What’s vital after nights like Thursday is that we all stick together, in the same way that we all celebrate together and enjoy the moment after wins like Crystal Palace. I admit that sometimes it is easier said than done, but it is important that we don’t get too high after a win and we don’t get too low after a defeat. #2077. Nuno’s West Ham Future Under Threat As Board Concerns Grow

Nuno Espírito Santo’s position as West Ham United manager is under increasing threat, according to a new report from The Guardian. With the Hammers slipping to eighth in the Championship following consecutive home defeats, patience is reportedly wearing thin among key figures at the London Stadium.

Writing for The Guardian, Hammers fan Jacob Steinberg reports that although Nuno is expected to be given more time to turn things around, influential figures at West Ham are becoming increasingly impatient with the club’s disappointing start to the season.

The report comes just two days after the 3-1 defeat against West Bromwich Albion, a result which prompted further questions about Nuno’s tactics and his ability to get the best out of a squad assembled with the intention of securing an immediate return to the Premier League.

According to The Guardian, any decision regarding Nuno’s future would be taken collectively by the West Ham board, rather than by one shareholder acting alone.

Interim chief executive Karim Virani and recruitment director Nils Koppen are among those expected to have input.

The report also revisits the decision to retain Nuno following relegation, explaining that David Sullivan had wanted a change of manager while Daniel Křetínský favoured continuity.

However, that previous support does not necessarily mean the manager’s position is secure indefinitely.

West Ham have won just twice in their last six Championship matches, and the upcoming fixtures against Cardiff City and Blackburn Rovers could become increasingly important ahead of the November international break.

The Guardian also highlights concerns about Nuno’s inability to settle on his strongest starting eleven, the lack of balance in midfield and the failure of the club’s strikers to provide sufficient goals.

The report states that West Ham’s three recognised centre-forwards, Joël Piroe, Pablo Felipe and Taty Castellanos, have scored just five league goals between them this season.

Meanwhile, Jarrod Bowen has scored seven, leaving the Hammers heavily dependent on our captain.

The continued absence of recognised defensive midfielders Soungoutou Magassa and Edson Álvarez from Nuno’s preferred selections is another issue raised.

These concerns will sound familiar to Claret & Hugh readers. Following the West Brom defeat, I questioned whether Nuno’s entire West Ham project was becoming fundamentally flawed, particularly given the lack of cohesion and the manager’s constant tactical changes.

And while I appreciate that managers need time, I struggle to see how West Ham can continue performing so poorly with a squad that should be capable of competing for automatic promotion.

Perhaps the most important aspect of The Guardian’s report is the suggestion that Nuno will face difficult questions if performances fail to improve before the international break.

There is no suggestion that a dismissal has already been agreed, and the report specifically indicates that West Ham still hope the manager can turn things around.

Nevertheless, it appears the pressure is no longer coming exclusively from frustrated supporters.

The next two matches now offer Nuno an opportunity to demonstrate that he can produce a convincing response.

Because as I’ve argued previously, West Ham’s problems haven’t suddenly appeared over the last fortnight. The warning signs have been there for considerably longer.

And if the manager cannot begin addressing them, it is becoming increasingly difficult to see how the club can justify continuing with the same approach.

#2076. This is where the match was lost as it ends Newcastle 0 Everton 1

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Newcastle 0 Everton 1 – Monday 2 November 2026 8pm

Everton seemed to have at least one extra player nearly all evening.

They used the ball better and with accurate finishing would have scored twice before half-time.

Newcastle, perhaps nervous of throwing men forward after being exposed last Thursday, rarely threatened. Our midfield and defence still looked scarily open, however.

Hall and Dedic were apparently being expected to play simultaneously in defence and attack, with predictable results when possession was turned over.

The first save either keeper had to make fell to Lukas Hornicek just after the interval. He let a routine shot slide under his body. Barry couldn’t miss and the officials did the rest, deciding a dubious challenge on Schar in the build-up was legal.

Hornicek prevented Dewsbury-Hall from doubling the lead, then did well to block a Branthwaite header.

On 64 minutes, Steur and Wissa replaced Gonzalez and Willock. Within two minutes we nearly levelled but Elanga’s point-blank shot rolled along the line before being cleared.

As the game became spread, Schar stopped a second Barry tap-in with a great but risky challenge. Murphy and Ramsey replaced Elanga and Joelinton with 15 minutes left. Ramsey was a yard wide from hitting the jackpot on 79 minutes but still Pickford had not been extended.

The save he made from a weak 20-yarder by Wissa was as easy as Everton made their victory look. Conversely, United struggled to do much right.

Pickford finally earned his wage by kicking clear a Wissa snap shot after good work down the left by Toure, the last sub.

Deep into stoppage time, Ramsey was shown two yellow cards in quick succession, the second for an ugly tackle.

The bumps on the road are becoming bigger and more frequent.

Going on the presumption that a 6 out of 10 is a passing grade (as the Italian papers do it), there were only four players in the starting line-up that managed to achieve that. The substitutes were a mixed bag too, with Sankhoun Diawara’ 4.6 and Francesco Camarda’s 4.8 the worst, but even Luka Modric and Christian Pulisic (5.6s) didn’t get a pass this time.

#2073. 'Ticking bomb': Ex-striker's brutal Celtic warning as tensions threaten to explode

Former Hibernian striker Brian Graham has branded Celtic a "ticking bomb" amid growing unrest at Parkhead.

Graham believes pressure is mounting on the club, with supporters unhappy with the board, performances below expectations and questions surrounding the team's direction. It comes after the Hoops' latest 2-0 defeat to the Bairns as they've now won just three games from their last 10.

Speaking on Superscoreboard, Graham also defended Martin O'Neill against potential calls for his head, insisting the Celtic boss deserves credit for last season's title success.

"If it wasn't for Martin Celtic wouldn't have won the league last year," Graham said.

He suggested O'Neill may have been frustrated by the club's transfer business, adding that supporters are unaware of exactly what has been happening behind the scenes at Lennoxtown.

Graham admitted Celtic's European campaign had been a "disaster" and questioned the circumstances surrounding Cameron Carter-Vickers' recent absence.

But his strongest criticism was reserved for the club as a whole.

"As us and as fans, we don't know what's going on in the background at Celtic Football Club. Martin might've wanted X, Y and Z in the transfer window and didn't get it. Clearly with a couple of his comments he wasn't particularly happy with how it ended," he added.

"It's not been a fantastic start for Celtic in terms of their standards and how they're playing at the moment but rightly so they're top of the league. Europe has been a disaster, we have to be honest with that one, so there's unrest within the camp, it's clear to see.

"When Carter-Vickers comes out and he doesn't play the next couple of games which was alarming for me and the so-called 'injury'. Was there? We don't know. Then he's back in, makes a mistake for the goal.

"Celtic on the whole as a club right now is a ticking bomb. They're ready to just go off and it's been like that for the last six months, there needs to be some sort of resolve.

"There's been a lot of fans not happy with the board and that's been the case for a long time. Something has to give. Surely."

#2072. ‘It’s not easy to explain as it looked so good during the week…’ Matthias Jaissle after Everton defeat

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Matthias Jaissle watched on as his team lost to Everton, again.

This Premier League loss to the Toffees coming only four days after Everton also knocked Newcastle United out of the Carabao Cup.

The goal shortly after half-time and a combination of a comedy of errors when it came to Newcastle United’s defending and what looked dubious decision making from the referee.

Newcastle United then lacking the quality and penetration to get much joy out of a solid Everton defence.

Matthias Jaissle speaking to BBC Sport: “Today we didn’t play well. It’s not enough against Everton to get a good result, that’s something we need to do better. The performance today, you didn’t see our playing style and that can’t happen.”

The Newcastle United boss going on to say: “It’s not easy to explain as it looked so good during the week [in training]. The lads looked committed and the confidence was there. Today from the start the confidence was missing. We need to improve really fast. We have to encourage them that they are able to do it, that they have the potential to play in that way.”

Matthias Jaissle on creating chances and the killer goal: “We should have created even more moments. It was not good enough. To concede a goal like that also was not good enough. It’s almost like a negative spiral [on the elements of the goal]. I’m not happy with the referee decision. For me it’s a clear foul on Fabian Schar. It’s a difficult period. We also know you can only overcome that as a unit.”

#2071. Black November arrives at Celtic as prosecution's case against Martin O'Neill grows

An audio clip appeared online this week of former Republic of Ireland winger James McClean winding back the clock to life as an international footballer under Martin O’Neill.

Promoting his new book, McClean offered the opinion that the current manager of Celtic was never terribly big on tactics.

The game, he believed, came down to eleven versus eleven and good players were expected to take the initiative and solve any problems on the pitch.

Sending the likes of Henrik Larsson, Chris Sutton, Alan Thompson and Bobo Balde in to the trenches, the strategy seemed to work like a dream. Steve Walford and John Robertson ran the training and the set piece drills at Barrowfield and results spoke for themselves.

The issue with the Ireland O’Neill managed 10 years ago was a squad full of young English Championship players who expected to be coached on everything.

Their world, said McClean, revolved around tactics, tactics, tactics. Some struggled to get their heads around O’Neill’s old school ways or cope with the administration of a few truths.

A damning indictment on the modern footballer, Celtic fans seized on McClean’s pearls of wisdom, piecing them together with recent clues gleaned from the Parkhead dressing room.

Defender Cameron Carter-Vickers suggested that the tactics were all a ‘bit too random’. Callum McGregor offered the view that players with the wrong profile were being shoe horned into the unfamiliar positions.

Carter-Vickers could make a more constructive contribution if he could stay fit for five minutes and stop gifting goals to Falkirk in the opening minutes of games. The captain might also explain why Scott Tanser was allowed to gift through the midfield for Falkirk’s second yesterday or how he managed to miss a real chance to get his team back into the game at 2-0.

Putting that stuff to one side, supporters are compiling a case for the prosecution of Martin O’Neill. They no longer care what he did for Celtic 20 years ago or even last season.

Where their frustration is usually aimed in the direction of the board of directors more and more is now being channelled towards their 74-year-old manager.

Many accuse him of being a Dermot Desmond appointee who picks the wrong teams and leans on coaches who failed to cut the mustard at clubs like Wigan and Huddersfield.

While older diehards are uncomfortable with criticising the man who gave them some of their greatest days, the young crew are unencumbered by sentiment or history.

They would rather that O’Neill had sailed off into retirement after steering the team to a league and cup double in the summer. And there must be times when the man himself wonders if they have a point.

Everything Martin O'Neill said about Celtic's performance after defeat to Falkirk

The Martin O'Neill explanation that Celtic support won't accept after Falkirk

Martin O'Neill explains Jota omission before Falkirk clash

Had Scott Bain played for Celtic the way he did against his old club yesterday the Falkirk keeper would still be earning the big bucks at Parkhead.

After the man’s best performance in living memory it feels harsh to rain on his parade, but none of Bainarumma’s stops fell into the world class variety. As a team Celtic have become easy to play against and the attacking blueprint seems to consist of getting the ball into wide areas, throwing in a cross and hoping for the best.

When Camilo Duran is on form there is always a chance that might work. Yesterday the Colombian missed some glaring opportunities - thwarted by Bain - and, while O’Neill can’t legislate for the individual errors of strikers or experienced defenders like Carter-Vickers, he knows fine how football works.

After four wins in 10 games many now think he is a man out of his time and the trust and faith of the fans who once adored him is draining. Few buy the notion he pushed after the game that the Falkirk defeat was just one of those days. A pattern is emerging.

Between now and the end of December Celtic play 12 games. While games against Besiktas, Kilmarnock and St Mirren offer some home comfort, away trips to Dundee, Hearts, Toreense, Omonia Nicosia, Dundee United and Rangers must hold all the appeal of a one-day cruise through the Strait of Hormuz.

Come the January window the plan is to sign a physical, mobile central midfielder. They might even shore up a porous defence.

Regardless of how much they spend the most recent window - and plenty others before -  make it hard to harbour for fans to harbour much faith that they will spend the money well.

The £11million record signing, Kasper Hogh can’t buy a goal. Egyptian winger Haissem Hassan remains a talented enigma wrapped in a conundrum. They ended the January window scrambling around to bring in Joel van der Berg, Jordan Lotomba, Oliver Sorensen, Shim Mheuka and Landon Emanelo and they barely see a minute of first team action

Uniquely amongst modern football clubs Celtic see no need to hire a qualified Sporting Director capable of getting a handle on recruitment. A year since Head of Football Operations Paul Tisdale left the club they have yet to replace him. So much for aspiring to be world class in everything they do.

Before Falkirk O’Neill spoke of the need to give summer signings time to adapt to a new club.

While the demands and expectations at Celtic are on a different level, Falkirk made 17 new signings of their own. And, after a ropey start, John McGlynn has now secured his first ever victory over his old employer and won four league games in a row. Some new signings clearly settle in a little faster than others.

McGlynn’s restoration of Falkirk is a testament to the power of a good coach. Taking the  job in May 2022 the Bairns were a basket case. A League One club in the third tier of Scottish football they were losing money hand over fist.

There is nothing flashy or showy about the way he does things. Mention his name for the Celtic job and the very idea would be ridiculed because he is, essentially, a modest, working class man from Wallyford.

Yet those who say he’s not Celtic class should probably ask themselves a question now. What is Celtic class these days? What do the club aspire to be? Is being one point clear of Rangers the height of their ambition or do they want more? If so how do they plan to get there?

As a plc Celtic are duty bound to convene an Annual General Meeting before the end of December. This year all of these questions - over recruitment, ambition, the lack of communication and the strategy - deserve to be asked and​ answered

Martin O’Neill is one of the issues facing Celtic now. He is by no means the only one.

#2070. Cherki magic helping Maresca to step out of Guardiola shadow

Rumours of Manchester City’s supposed demise without Pep Guardiola appear to be much exaggerated.

They swept past Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park with a style of play under new manager Enzo Maresca that was just as swashbuckling as under his predecessor, with Rayan Cherki playing the role of chief architect. The Frenchman’s two goals included a captivating mazy dribble, which will long be remembered by those who had the fortune to see it.

City created enough space for themselves through clever movement. With Cherki zigging one way and Phil Foden zagging the other, they created even more by dribbling past a mesmerised Palace back three that became a back five at times and still could not cope.

Erling Haaland also scored twice. Even with the creative and unpredictable talents of those behind in a four-man attacking City midfield, Haaland remains irreplaceable with his ability to convert chances.

However, this night belonged to Cherki. Guardiola chided him publicly after he set up a City goal with a “rabona” cross last season. The thrust of Guardiola’s comments were that Cherki was not Lionel Messi. Of course not, but he possesses a genius all of his own, which Maresca would surely be foolish to rein in.

The jaw-dropping splendour of Cherki’s first goal drew a collective intake of breath at Selhurst Park.

Collecting a Foden pass, he attacked the Palace area on a diagonal path, slaloming between Jaydee Canvot, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chris Richards, before having the spatial awareness and technique to flick his left foot at the ball to send it rolling on a perpendicular trajectory past Dean Henderson.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv

An insight into Cherki’s mindset came after the match.

He said: “My performance is s---. In the first half, we didn’t find the space, I played bad. I need to show them that I want to play, I want to score. Next time I want to give the ball around more.”

Forget the words, Maresca cannot ignore the actions of a player he left on the bench against Bournemouth.

Sterner tests will come for City than against a Palace side missing key players who may or may not leave south London in the remaining days of the transfer window.

Whether Maresca will trust his forward players to express themselves as freely against their rivals for the Premier League title remains to be seen, but with Elliot Anderson providing a one-man shield behind them, City could not be stopped.

Maresca said: “For sure Rayan is happy tonight. His performance was very good and not just for his two goals. He has to press off the ball and he was in charge of [marking] Adam Wharton, so it was a complete game by him.”

Only for the first three minutes did Palace hint at a different outcome but, after shots from Eddie Nketiah and Daichi Kamada were diverted away for corners, City took control.

They took the lead in the 17th minute when the otherwise quiet Antoine Semenyo flighted a cross over the heads of everyone except the shorn locks of Haaland, whose determined header looped over Henderson and dropped in the far corner.

The only negative of Foden’s performance came in front of goal, with a ballooned shot and a mistimed header.

After Cherki’s solo masterpiece had made it 2-0, Yeremy Pino seized the next moment for his own with a stunning free-kick that flicked the crossbar, then the back of City keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma before finally dropping over the line.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp

Whatever hope that mustered was snatched away again when Cherki scored his second goal and the third goal of a breathless five minutes.

His shot at the end of a darting run flicked the ankle of Tomiyasu to send it just out of Henderson’s reach.

Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r

Morocco teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi had little time to show why City have paid Lille £85.6m for him with a late entry as a substitute, but they didn’t need him on this occasion.

Foden then set off on a swerving run that set up Haaland to lash home his second goal of the game and make it 4-1.

Erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF

The fear for Palace is that they cannot keep selling their best players and expecting to replicate the success on the pitch that has brought them three trophies in the past 15 months.

Leicester City offer a shuddering example of that. From Premier League champions to League One in 10 seasons.

Pierre Sage, the new Palace manager, will welcome the certainty that the closure of the transfer window will bring, particularly over the futures of forwards Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta, as well as wing-back Daniel Muñoz.

The one player he cannot afford to lose is Wharton, who matched the City midfield on his own at times in the first half.

Sage said: “I think the score is heavy. We stayed in the game for 65 minutes and created some chances. We know we are in for a tough season, but we have created a lot of opportunities in the first two games.

“I could speak about the transfer window, but I don’t want to find an excuse. We just have to be sure that in four days’ time, the team will be better than today.”

“It has been a short pre-season. Rayan [Cherki], five weeks ago was at the World Cup. Game by game, we will be back, just need a few games. We played well, it is a new manager but we have been playing together, with the addition of a few new players. We know what to do and have to trust the system.”

“We have to keep on playing together, find out where we are best and how to play. We have so many good players and we have to fit everyone in. He has to keep going because we know how good Phil is, it is about showing it week in week out. This is the right step forward for everyone. We have to build on this.”

"I'm just trying to play my football" 💪Elliot Anderson is excited about the future at Manchester City after his summer transfer 🔥 pic.twitter.com/huGv4Li3GZ

"Say what you actually mean!" 🤣Erling Haaland takes over Rayan Cherki's post-match interview! pic.twitter.com/adW6IU8DzQ

2 + 2 - Rayan Cherki is the third player to have a game with multiple goals and another game with multiple assists across a team's first two matches of a Premier League campaign, after Thierry Henry in 2004-05 and Didier Drogba in 2010-11.Polymath. pic.twitter.com/4cRV0xMIFa

September 5: Fulham vs Crystal PalaceSeptember 12: Crystal Palace vs IpswichSeptember 19: Leeds vs Crystal PalaceOctober 11: Crystal Palace vs Nottingham ForestOctober 18: Brighton vs Crystal Palace

Pierre Sage’s side will host Middlesbrough in the League Cup third round next month and will also begin their Europa League campaign in September.

The directions of these teams will be diverging this season. City were wonderful, free-flowing, expressive and fun to watch. Palace not so much. It will take Pierre Sage a while to impose his style of play. It will certainly take another week before he knows his final squad for the first half of the season.

It was noticeable at the final whistle that many Palace fans stayed around to applaud Daniel Munoz, an unused substitute on the night, as he made his way to the tunnel, probably for the final time as a Palace player if Nottingham Forest’s interest in him becomes a transfer by the end of the window.

"Cherki was the difference" 🪄"He is a genius" 🧠Jamie Redknapp reacts to Crystal Palace 1-4 Man City 🔊 pic.twitter.com/UjSarMngDR

Manchester City will take on Norwich in the League Cup third round in September and will also have their first Champions League match next month.

Possession: Crystal Palace 28%-72% Manchester CityShots: 9-18Shots on target: 1-9Corners: 2-6Touches in the opposition box: 13-33

Pretty comprehensive in Manchester City’s favour, which is reflected in the scoreline.

The final whistle is blown at Selhurst Park and Manchester City have cruised to a 4-1 win thanks to doubles from Cherki and Haaland. Enzo Maresca’s side make it two wins from two whereas it is two defeats from two for Pierre Sage.

Manchester City, with the three points already in the bag, are just stroking the ball around with ease and are in complete control. Palace can barely get a foot on it.

A late double substitution for Manchester City as Reis and Braithwaite come on. Enzo Maresca’s side are cruising to victory to make it two wins from two.

Cherki has two goals to his name and now Haaland does as Manchester City are romping to victory in south London. Guehi wins possession for City inside the Palace half and the ball comes to Foden, who dribbles towards the Palace penalty area. He lays it off to his left to Haaland who, from a narrow angle, finds the root of the net.

Erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF

Nearly an instant impact from McAidoo as the 18-year-old drives through the Palace half and curls a shot from the edge of the box that goes just wide.

When Manchester City were making those substitutions, the Crystal Palace fans were making sure they let the officials know how long the Manchester City players were taking to get off.

There is going to be a debut for the Premier League’s most expensive teenager ever as Bouaddi comes on for Manchester City. McAidoo is also coming on, with Cherki and Anderson going off.

Mingueza eventually comes on but not after having to wait until the ball goes out of play again as Khalaili was adjudged to have taken too long to have got off the pitch. Safe to say the Palace fans are not too impressed with that new rule. It will probably be a pub question in the years ahead. That change does mean that Palace have used all five substitutions, which means Munoz will not come on. He is being linked with a reunion with Oliver Glasner at Nottingham Forest in the final days of this window.

Crystal Palace make another double change and it will be two debuts as Disasi and Mingueza come on.

Enzo Maresca turns to his bench for the first time tonight as Kovacic comes on.

Khalaili brings down Semenyo and is booked for that challenge.

Palace are going to make a double substitution as McNeil and Gozo replace Nketiah and Pino. 19-year-old Gozo is on for his Palace debut.

That was a chance for Palace. Guessand finds Pino, who drives into the Manchester City penalty area on the right. Pino has Nketiah at the far post but there is too much on the cross.

Guessand, back at Palace, is going to come on to replace Strand Larsen, who has been pretty quiet up top for the home side tonight.

Sometimes you feel blessed to witness an extraordinary moment of footballing genius. Selhurst Park has just seen two in the space of three minutes. Yeremy Pino’s free-kick which flicked off the back of Gianluigi Donnarumma was stunning, but even that could not truly compare to the slalom run of Rayan Cherki that drew a collective intake of breath from all those present. The Frenchman has just followed it with a scorching shot. It couldn’t compare with his first, though.

Three goals come in quick succession and Cherki restores Manchester City’s two-goal advantage with his second of the night. The Frenchman receives it on the turn from around 30 yards out and drives towards the Palace penalty area. He then shoots and a kind deflection off Richards takes it over Henderson’s diving effort and into the Palace net.

Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r

Just as the hosts appeared to maybe out of this one, they get a goal back. Pino’s fantastic free-kick strikes the bar, hits Donnarumma on the back before going into the net off the post. That hit the frame of the goal twice and Palace have a crucial goal, minutes after going 2-0 down.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp

Anderson brings down Pino not far outside the Manchester City penalty area and is booked.

The next goal in this game felt crucial and the visitors have it. Foden drives towards the Palace penalty area before playing a pass forward into the path of Cherki. The Frenchman has numerous defenders around but he shows neat footwork to skip past a few, holds off Richards before slotting home with his left foot.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv

No-one has had fewer touches on the pitch tonight than Haaland up until this point but the Norwegian’s goal is the difference. His number of touches (14) is the joint fewest with his compatriot Strand Larsen.

That was a good chance for Nketiah. He plays the ball to the underlapping Mitchell, who from the byline cuts it back into the path of Nketiah. The former Arsenal man should so so much better with his opportunity from the edge of the six-yard box but fires a long way wide.

Semenyo wins Manchester City an early corner in this second half off Canvot. Anderson’s delivery beyond the back post picks out O’Reilly, who in space heads back across goal but Pino heads away.

We are back under way at Selhurst Park, with Manchester City carrying a 1-0 lead into this second half. As the players emerged from the tunnels for the second half, the DJ at Selhurst Park paid tribute to the late Dolly Parton and Kenny Rogers by playing Islands in the Stream. Nice touch! Get your favourite Dolly and Kenny tunes in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Possession: Crystal Palace 33%-67% Manchester CityShots: 7-11Shots on target: 1-6Corners: 2-2Touches in the opposition box: 10-18

The stats are certainly in Manchester City’s favour and they will feel they probably should have more than the one goal.

Cherki has a late chance for Manchester City but his shot is well saved by Henderson down to his right.

The first half at Selhurst Park is then brought to an end and Manchester City lead 1-0 at the break thanks to Haaland’s header.

There will be just one added minute at the end of this first half.

Palace started off with a nominal back three. That has become a back five far too often for Pierre Sage’s liking at times in this first half, yet still City are playing through them almost at will. The Palace fans whose deafening support accompanied Palace shots in the opening minutes are reduced to cheering battling midfield runs that win a free-kick now.

Pino delivers a free-kick into the Manchester City box and Richards gets to it first. It comes off his shoulder and rolls into the arms of Donnarumma.

Semenyo’s shot from the left side of the box takes a deflection off Richards, forcing Henderson into a decent save.

Palace now miss a big opportunity and should be on level terms. Wharton, who has probably been the best player on the pitch tonight, whips in a cross from the right and picks out Mitchell, who has a free header from eight yards out but somehow misses the target.

Strand Larsen comes close with a header from a Pino cross but he would have been offside anyway.

The first booking of the night goes the way of the visitors. Wharton drives forward into the Manchester City half and is cynically brought down by Cherki, who looked perplexed when the yellow card was shown but it was an obvious booking.

Foden wastes his second big chance of this first half. Manchester City break through O’Reilly, who carries it down the right. He waits for Cherki to make the overlapping run before passing to the Frenchman. Cherki’s cross picks out Foden inside the six-yard box and the latter should score but he gets a simple header all wrong.

Well, that was easy. So easy in fact – perfect Semenyo cross, perfect Haaland header - that it hushed Selhurst Park as the ball looped over Dean Henderson. Even the roar from the enclave of City fans took a moment to fill the south London air. You wouldn’t say that all the pre-match optimism among Palace fans has been punctured, but the home side need a moment if they aren’t to sink without trace to a City side bossing possession and territory now.

That is a huge miss from Foden. Anderson picks out his compatriot in acres of space on the right side of the box, with no Palace defender within five yards of him, but Foden blazes over the bar when he should have put Manchester City 2-0 up.

King Harald V of Norway has died in the last few days and over the last few hours two Norwegian cyclists claimed a one-two at the Vuelta a Espana and now Haaland has a goal.

He has barely touched the ball thus far but he puts the visitors ahead just past the quarter-of-an-hour mark. Semenyo is afforded too much space on the left just outside the penalty area and clips in a cross towards the far post. Haaland gets up highest, above Richards, and guides a superb header over Henderson into the Palace net.

Erling Haaland gets off the mark for the new Premier League season! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/5ZjQUVk6Zl

The England boss is in attendance tonight, perhaps keeping a close eye on that midfield battle between Anderson and Wharton.

Palace flirt with danger inside their own penalty area. After Haaland’s flick, Kamada should just belt the ball away but instead inexplicably leaves it. Henderson manages to mop up just as Foden was eyeing up the chance.

There is a mad scramble inside the Palace box but somehow the hosts escape without conceding. Initially, Anderson’s shot from range is saved by Henderson but Manchester City keep it alive in the penalty area. Palace frantically attempt to clear their lines and eventually they do after Haaland came close.

Quite a lot of the focus tonight will be on two English midfielders; one who has got a big-money move this summer and the other thus far has not. Anderson is directly up against Wharton and so far it is the latter who is winning the early battles, including dispossessing Anderson in midfield.

The first chance of the game goes the way of the hosts. It stems from a quite sensational first-time pass from Wharton from inside his own half into the left channel to pick out the run of Nketiah, whose shot from the left side of the box takes a deflection off Dias and is saved by Donnarumma.

Manchester City initially clear the corner but Palace keep it alive. Kamada’s shot from just inside the box appeared to be on target but it is headed over for another corner, which is easily caught by Donnarumma.

We are under way at Selhurst Park. Will Pierre Sage earn his first win as Palace boss or can Enzo Maresca and City make it two wins from two?

Both sides emerge from the tunnel in the corner of Selhurst Park to the customary sound of Glad All Over and we are moments away from kick-off in south London. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Crystal Palace: Henderson, Khalaili, Canvot, Richards, Tomiyasu, Mitchell, Wharton, Kamada, Pino, Strand Larsen, Nketiah.Substitutes: Benitez, Munoz, Disasi, Mingueza, Hughes, Lerma, Gozo, McNeil, Guessand.

Manchester City: Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol, O’Reilly, Anderson, Guehi, Cherki, Foden Semenyo, Haaland.Substitutes: Rulli, Kovacic, Ait-Nouri, Reis, Echeverri, Bouaddi, McAidoo, Braithwaite, Lewis.

Yes! It may have been fleeting but the boy in the Palace tracksuit top had his moment after all with Erling Haaland as City waited in line to enter the Selhurst Park pitch. And having done so, he fairly skipped up the steps back with his dad back to their seats. Whether the boy’s second wish of the evening, for a Palace victory, will come true is another question altogether.

The young Palace fan is still waiting for Haaland. Another determined walk back to the dressing room. It isn’t a simple task to attract an opposition player’s attention when you are leaning over a barrier a few feet higher than him – and in the home end. Haaland and his teammates have the look of a team that knows it must perform tonight to ease the concerns that they are a team in transition. The City fans will not entertain such thoughts, either.

Crystal Palace looked set to sign Club Brugge defender Joel Ordonez but that deal could be in doubt as there may be some problems with his medical. We await to see further updates on that situation.

“He is a genius. Make no mistake. Managers now want structure, they do not like players who are a bit loose out of possession. But I go to football matches to watch people like him play.

“That is what makes me smile. I do not like watching players pass it sideways, that is not why I go to football. I go to watch geniuses do their work. Some managers will not appreciate it. But last week he got his manager out of a hole because without him they would not have won that game.”

"He's irreplaceable" 💥Jamie Redknapp and Clinton Morrison sing the praises of Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton 🤝 pic.twitter.com/ZOpcZcItHY

Jack Grealish is not in the Manchester City squad tonight amid links with the likes of Everton and Sunderland. Will he still be at the club beyond the deadline? It would appear not.

Both Ismaila Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta are out of the Crystal Palace squad tonight with injury but could they be on the move before the window slams shut? Sarr has been linked with Galatasaray and Liverpool whilst the situation is complicated with Mateta as he claims the final year of his contract is void. How do those two situations resolve themselves? Daniel Munoz has been linked with a move to Nottingham Forest but is on the bench for Palace this evening.

Having waited patiently for the City players to emerge for their warm-up and being held by his dad as he leant over the stone wall to attract Haaland’s attention, he was left disappointed because the City striker was simply not looking as he and his teammates jogged past. Will the boy, who has on a Palace tracksuit top, get a photo with his hero when the striker returns to the Portakabin that hosts the away dressing room prior to kick-off? Stay tuned.

Was it really just a year ago when Crystal Palace fans flooded down the Holmesdale Road with not a care in the world having just won the Community Shield to add to their FA Cup triumph over tonight’s opponents Manchester City? Well, they are marching along the Holmesdale Road in the same numbers again this evening, bedecked in red and blue as always, yet there is uncertainty and worry in the air and on their faces. Will the player exodus continue? What should they make of new manager Pierre Sage? Will the good times fade from view as quickly as they did for Leicester City or can Sage build a new side to match the one which, under Oliver Glasner, added the Conference League to their list of trophies three months ago?

“We struggled to get into the game and win the battles,” a disappointed Carlo Ancelotti lamented.

At the World Cup, an industrious 18-year-old showed maturity beyond his years to dominate the midfield against Ancelotti’s Brazil on his competitive international debut, earning Morocco a draw. That was, in fact, the second time an Ancelotti side had been undone by precocious teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Ancelotti’s remarks about losing the midfield battle are from after a Champions League match in October 2024, when Lille shocked Real Madrid to end their 36-game unbeaten run. Bouaddi was at the heart of both statement results for his club and country.

The second weekend of the Premier League season kicks off under the lights in South London as Crystal Palace host Manchester City at Selhurst Park. Manchester City won both fixtures 3-0 last season and they are in fact unbeaten in their last 11 Premier league away games against Crystal Palace, who have won just two of the 22 top flight meetings.

Crystal Palace experienced defeat on the opening weekend, falling to a 2-0 loss at Everton last Saturday, meaning the Pierre Sage era started with a defeat. Tonight is Sage’s first home game in charge of the club.

“I think it will be a wonderful moment, but I prefer to have a wonderful moment with good news at the end of the game,” Sage said. “That is why I do not think about me in this situation. The most important thing is the team and the result for sure, because we prepare all the week for that, to make them [the fans] happy. They will be happy to see us, but I think they would prefer to see us win. I will give my life to make them happy. I cannot do more. When you are in this stadium [Selhurst Park], you feel the history. You feel that there is something heavy weighing on you. It is a great responsibility that I have been entrusted with. We cannot wait to see this stadium in action.”

Sage has confirmed that Ismaila Sarr, who has been linked with a move away from the club this summer, and Chadi Riad will miss out tonight due to injury, as will striker Jean-Philippe Mateta. Palace have confirmed the addition of Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea and the French defender could be involved tonight.

Manchester City appeared to be heading towards defeat in Enzo Maresca’s first league game in charge of the club last weekend. They were 1-0 down at home against Bournemouth in the closing stages before goals from Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol gave them a come-from-behind win.

It has been a busy week in the transfer window for Manchester City. Both Savio (formerly Savinho) and Omar Marmoush have left for Tottenham, joining a long list of departures from the Etihad this summer. Moroccan midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi has arrived in an £85m deal from Lille and has become the most expensive teenager in Premier League history. Maresca has confirmed that 18-year-old Bouaddi is ready to start.

“He [Bouaddi] is ready,” Maresca said. “He was working with his former club so he is fit. We will see how long he needs in terms of adaptation but he is ready to go. He is quite calm. He does not look 18, he already looks older, which is important. But in this case, we need to go slowly because he is very young, he has come from a different country so there is no rush for him. He is going to help us now and in the future. He is very mature for being 18.”

Team news from Selhurst Park to follow shortly.

#2069. Cardiff City v West Ham: Lineups And Predicted Teams For Huge Championship Clash

Cardiff City v West Ham United EFL Championship Cardiff City Stadium Wednesday 4 November 2026, 7.45pm GMT

West Ham United’s trip to Cardiff City is hugely important. Lose this one and I believe Nuno Espírito Santo will have a very real chance of losing his job following consecutive home defeats against Southampton and West Bromwich Albion.

Saturday’s 3-1 loss has already dropped the Hammers to eighth, occupying the final play-off position. Another defeat could see us unceremoniously dumped out of the top eight and further towards mid-table, which would be an extraordinary situation for a club widely expected to challenge for automatic promotion.

This is therefore about far more than collecting three points against a newly promoted team. Nuno needs a result to arrest West Ham’s decline, restore some belief among the players and demonstrate that he remains capable of rescuing a promotion campaign which is beginning to unravel.

The most concerning part of the 3-1 defeat against West Brom was the players’ apparent lack of motivation and the absence of any recognisable tactical plan.

West Ham do not seem capable of defending or attacking properly at the moment. The defence is repeatedly exposed by simple passages of play, while the attack remains heavily dependent on Jarrod Bowen producing something individually.

Nuno admitted afterwards that it was a poor performance and that West Ham conceded too easily. However, the same weaknesses have been visible for some time, and words will mean very little unless something changes on the pitch.

The team lacks cohesion, urgency and confidence. More worryingly, there is increasingly little evidence that the players understand precisely what the manager wants them to do.

Reports have already questioned whether West Ham’s players are still fighting for Nuno. Wednesday night should provide a fairly clear answer.

Nuno Espírito Santo needs to pull himself and his team together ahead of Wednesday

I believe Nuno is capable of turning this around in the immediate sense. West Ham have enough individual quality to beat Cardiff and Blackburn, even while playing considerably below the level expected of this squad.

What I am far less convinced about is whether he possesses the necessary man-management and tactical skills to turn West Ham into a team comfortably established inside the automatic promotion places.

Those are two different questions. Winning the next two matches may ease the pressure, but it would not automatically prove that Nuno has solved the underlying problems which have followed West Ham throughout the season.

I have already explained why I believe Nuno has had long enough and West Ham need a change. Nothing about the West Brom performance altered that conclusion.

My preferred formation would be a 4-1-4-1, accompanied by drastic changes in personnel.

Alphonse Areola would replace Mads Hermansen in goal. Nobody should be guaranteed a place during such a poor run, and Hermansen has not done enough to make himself untouchable.

Joël Veltman would start at right-back, with Airidas Golambeckis partnering Max Kilman in central defence if Konstantinos Mavropanos remains unavailable. Kyle Walker-Peters would move to left-back, assuming he recovers from the injury sustained against West Brom.

Soungoutou Magassa would operate as the holding midfielder. West Ham desperately need somebody to protect the defence, and the repeated decision to play without a natural defensive midfielder has contributed to the team’s lack of balance.

Lewis Orford and Divine Mukasa would play ahead of him, giving West Ham energy, creativity and players capable of retaining possession. Bowen and Edvin Austbø would provide the width, with Joël Piroe given a proper opportunity as the central striker.

These are broadly the immediate changes I believe Nuno needs to make. Repeating the same selections and expecting a different performance no longer makes any sense.

This is the team I would select at Cardiff, built around a recognised holding midfielder and players who deserve an opportunity. Walker-Peters is a fitness doubt, so his inclusion depends on him recovering in time.

Managers under pressure rarely make radical changes, which is why I expect Nuno’s selection to look rather different from mine.

I still believe he could replace Hermansen with Areola and retain Veltman at right-back. Golambeckis should continue alongside Kilman if Mavropanos remains unavailable, but I expect Morato to keep his place at left-back.

Mohamadou Kanté and Arne Engels are likely to form the central-midfield partnership, with Manor Solomon operating behind Piroe. Bowen and Austbø should provide the width in what looks like a 4-2-3-1.

Cardiff sit 17th after gaining promotion as League One runners-up last season. Their recent unbeaten run ended with a 3-0 defeat at Wolverhampton Wanderers on Saturday.

The Bluebirds have significant problems in defence. Gabriel Osho is suspended, while Dylan Lawlor and Calum Chambers have been sidelined through injury.

Manager Brian Barry-Murphy also revealed fresh concerns following the Wolves defeat, with Will Fish suffering a hamstring problem, Perry Ng struggling with fitness and Alex Robertson experiencing an Achilles issue. Krystian Bielik remains another doubt, although he has returned to training.

That leaves Cardiff facing the possibility of several important absences, although not every player mentioned has been ruled out of Wednesday’s match.

West Ham have their own concerns, with Mavropanos recovering from a knee problem and Walker-Peters doubtful following his injury against West Brom.

However, Nuno cannot reasonably claim he has been handed an impossible assignment.

Cardiff’s problems give West Ham an opportunity to stop the rot. If the Hammers cannot produce a convincing response against a newly promoted side with such significant defensive concerns, the pressure surrounding Nuno’s position will become increasingly difficult to ignore.

On paper, West Ham should win this match. We possess the stronger and more expensive squad, while Cardiff could be without a significant number of players.

Unfortunately, nothing about West Ham’s recent performances inspires confidence. The players look short of motivation, the defence is vulnerable and there is no obvious attacking plan beyond hoping Bowen creates something.

I believe Nuno is capable of winning the next two games, but I cannot predict it with any confidence. My expectation is that West Ham will stop the run of defeats without doing enough to claim the victory they desperately need.

Prediction: Cardiff City 1-1 West Ham United

Supporters travelling to the match can find ticket, parking and transport information in West Ham United’s official Cardiff travel guide.

#2066. Tactical change could revitalise Arne Engels if Nuno is ready to grasp the nettle | West Ham News

Arne Engels needs to be freed from the defensive duties with which he’s weighed down by West Ham’s current formation.

At least, that’s the gist of a report published last night suggesting that the Hammers need an old fashioned defensive midfielder at the heart of their side, to block off teams who at present appear to be able to play through their non-existent defensive shield owing to both Engels and Mukasa venturing too far forward too often.

As the 4thofficial suggested, there’s a remedy already at hand, a player largely ignored by Nuno yet one who could possibly could have a role to play in a more defensively solid West Ham United team, which is, frankly desperate to stop the early goals going in: Recalling defensive midfielder Edson Alvarez.

“From West Ham‘s perspective, reinstating Álvarez should come before abandoning the entire tactical framework. Engels has potential, but expecting the Belgian to provide attacking quality and defensive protection simultaneously places unnecessary pressure on an inexperienced midfield partnership.

Álvarez could give the centre-backs greater protection when attacking full-backs advance, while allowing Engels more freedom to distribute and move forward. That adjustment would address an immediate weakness without forcing another expensive recruitment exercise.”

Many have written off Alvarez as being too slow or too volatile in view of his disciplinary record – which other than an infamous red card against Liverpool – is perhaps not as bad as projected.

Report suggests the scrap- heap midfielder could do a job for Nuno.. if the West Ham manager is  big enough to mend bridges with El Machin

Many Claret and Hugh readers have commented that Nuno’s side needs the extra solidity of a ‘number six’ sitting in front of the back line to which, in truth, Engels doesn’t seem to be best suited.

Perhaps, indeed, rather than abandon the whole ‘tactical framework’ or trying to fit yet another square peg into a round hole, Nuno could grasp the nettle and re-integrate the tailor made defensive minded midfielder Alvarez into his line up.

There’s a down side of course. Dropping one of Mukasa or Kanté  would reduce West Ham’s creativity going forward. It could mean reverting Kanté to the bench blunderbuss role for the second half of games, exactly as he started the season so successfully.

It might make the Irons harder to score against in the first ’45 minutes anyway, Which at the moment couldn’t be such a bad thing. Is Nuno ready to grasp the nettle? Something has to give because right now, ‘hard work’ and ‘talking about it‘ isn’t fixing anything.
