#2064. AC Milan 2-4 Bologna: Five things we learned – the fatigue factor and striker struggles

AC Milan’s unbeaten start to the Serie A season is over, and it ended in worrying circumstances after a collapse against Bologna.

Things didn’t start well for Milan when Samuel Mbangula put the away side in front early on, but Alphadjo Cisse netted a quick fire brace to turn things back in the Rossoneri’s favour, meaning they led 2-1 at the break.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Bologna got themselves level again after an own-goal from a free-kic, and then they retook the lead one minute after that as Mbangula got his second of the night. The Belgian completed his hat-trick late on to make sure of the three points, continuing to Rossoblu’s upturn under Palladino.

San Siro was half-empty at full-time after what was a miserable evening, and certainly not the ideal way to go into Saturday’s derby, one which Inter will start already six points ahead. Ivan Stoev has five things we learned from the defeat.

Let’s get the obvious out of the way – this Milan side lacks the depth to play a game every three days, let alone play in the way that Amorim wants his sides to play.

This was a concern last season when Milan didn’t play in Europe and this past summer the management did not do enough to strengthen the squad, given they knew that the Europa League participation meant two games per week until at least January.

The desire to not buy in bulk is understandable, and bringing players that suit Amorim’s style is a specific requirement. However, the growing list of injuries has resulted in Milan being unable to be competitive as fatigue is setting in and rotation isn’t really an option given the players on the bench.

This is a very delicate moment where the management and the fans should not overreact and start blaming the players and the coach because you can only do so much with the limited resources.

Amorim was brought in to turn this side into a modern European club that plays attacking and attractive football. This unfortunately requires a lot of energy and that in itself means that player will be more likely to pick up an injury if they are not rotated properly.

Given how Milan fumbled the end of last season, the last thing that should go through the management’s head is yet another reset. Instead Amorim should be backed and reinforcements should be brought in as early as January if the Rossoneri want to keep up with the pack.

Extra reinforcements would also mean that – if things go their way – Milan could compete for the Europa League as well. The team have played some really good games and there is a platform to be built from. Let’s see if Gerry Cardinale feels the same.

It feels like we have a dedicated point to Pervis Estupinan every time the defender is on the pitch, but when the performances are so poor we can’t overlook it. We also can’t overlook the fact he keeps being willingly selected.

On the first goal it was unclear what the left-back was doing as he missed the run Zortea was making behind him. Before the goal he also made a mistake that nearly resulted in danger, and all night he tried passes that just were not there, often into dangerous areas.

Going forward the Ecuadorian was also underwhelming, meaning it’s pretty much impossible to find positives in Estupinan’s game. To bench Sankhoun Diawara and for that to be the response is alarming.

As we said, depth is an issue and with all the injuries Amorim does need to manage energy levels carefully. Hopefully the coach is starting to learn, though, that the former Brighton man just isn’t a good fit.

Goncalo Ramos got the nod to start up front and he looked very sluggish from start to finish. Amorim did talk about fatigue so that probably played a part given that the striker hasn’t been rested much recently.

The saving grace is that usually he combines well with his teampmates and his build-up play is quite solid, but the wasn’t the case against Bologna either as he struggled in all aspects of the game.

It doesn’t help that he drops deep all the time and whilst he’s probably doing this because of Amorim’s instructions it seems like the space he opens is not utilised by his team-mates which means he’s wasting energy for pretty much nothing.

Then if he does stay closer to goal, Milan lack the quality to provide him with any service and naturally the Portuguese struggles to take shots off.

It is not as black and white as saying Ramos does not have the quality but something needs to change in the way Amorim utilises him. He seems tired and listless, but without a proper back-up it’s difficult to see how the coach gets out of this situation.

Speaking of back-ups, Camarda also disappointed off bench. We obviously don’t want to criticise the 18-year-old too much year old a tonne as he’s not been getting a lot of minutes and it’s difficult to come on when your team are losing 3-2 and not playing well.

However, as the sample size grows we can also admit that the Italian eventually has to start taking some chances too. Camarda’s strength is supposed to be his instinct and finishing the box but he failed to convert a big chance with a header. Then his poor ball control resulted in him giving away the ball and Bologna’s fourth goal.

He obviously has talent, but this has been a tough start to the season for the teenager in which he has looked sluggish on and off the ball, has taken an age to decide whether to turn or pass upon receiving possession, and isn’t using his size.

He clearly needs the minutes but with the performances shown it’s understandable why he isn’t getting them. This needs to be addressed in January.

It’s hard to judge the defence when there’s so many injuries, though we did also see the impact of what can happen when players do not get a rest after a long run of games.

Koni De Winter and Strahinja Pavlovic have played a lot without being given the chance to recharge. On top of that Fikayo Tomori – who was playing really well – also came of injured at half time and then you had Yunus Musah at right-back which summarised the squad depth problem Milan has.

On the first goal it was poor defending by Davide Bartesaghi and even worse by Estupinan. The Italian continued with an own goal in the second half for Bologna’s equaliser and honestly he should’ve done much better.

He had enough time to react but he was busy watching his man instead of the trajectory of the ball which reminds us of his defensive struggles last season as Milan conceded quite a bit down his side and it was no different this time around.

Pavlovic was also sloppy on the first goal and so was De Winter with the Belgian gifting the free kick for Bologna’s equaliser early in the second half.

Diawara was also very sloppy of the bench as he failed to build upon his performance against Udinese. Tomori was the best Milan defender but he was subbed off at half time because of an injury. When it rains, it pours.

Let’s try to finish with some positives. Starting off with Ardon Jashari: this was one of the best starts by the Swiss. He ran relentlessly throughout the game and won a tonne of duels. As a result he was always open and his passing was quite accurate too.

Omari Hutchinson also had a decent game as his pressing essentially was the reason for the first goal as he forced Theate into committing an error. He also ran a lot and we saw him trying to be direct and take his man on. He maybe took a touch too many at times, but his technical quality and endavour were on display.

The third positive was obviously Cisse, who scored a brace as his positioning was his strong suit once again. He was also good on the ball although he faded a bit in the second half, but even then he should’ve gotten an assist for the great cross he delivered for Camarda.

Having just turned 20, this was his seventh goal in 10 games. He continues to improve and impress, and should absolutely play a key role in the upcoming Derby della Madonnina.

AC Milan and Inter Milan will play at the “Generali Stadium”: the naming rights agreement has been reached.

Details of the agreement between AC Milan, Inter Milan, and Generali, which acquired the naming rights for the new Milan stadium starting in 2031.

This evening, Milan and Inter are presenting the project for the new stadium that will replace San Siro starting in 2031. The project was developed thanks to the work of the internationally renowned studios Foster + Partners and MANICA. As previously mentioned, the stadium will have a prominent sponsor as its name, and will in fact be called “Generali Stadium”.

According to rumors learned by MilanNews.it, Generali has reached an agreement with AC Milan and Inter for the naming rights, estimated at between €25 and €30 million. This process, selling the stadium’s naming rights to a major sponsor, has become commonplace for those building new stadiums in recent years, both in Italy and Europe.

#2063. ‘Emotional’ Marink Reedijk enjoys post-match scenes as Hibernian book final spot

Marink Reedijk was touched by Hibernian fans’ emotional rendition of ‘Sunshine on Leith’ following their landmark 2-1 Premier Sports Cup semi-final win over city rivals Hearts at Barclays Hampden.

Jambos attacker Claudio Braga headed in from a corner only for returning striker Martin Boyle to deservedly level in the 19th minute before Jamie McGrath put the Hibees, bottom of the William Hill Premiership, ahead three minutes before the interval.

Hearts turned up the heat after the break but Hibs held out while retaining a threat at the other end to set up a final with Rangers at the national stadium on December 13.

It was the Dutchman’s first win as Hibs boss at the fifth attempt and Hibs’ first win against Hearts at Hampden after losing in 2006, 2012, 2020 and 2022 and the happy Hibees fans belted out the club anthem after the game.

Reedijk said: “I’m not always showing my emotions, but it’s really touching.

“So maybe it looks like I’m an ice King, so to say.

“Normally in Holland we say ice Queen, but therefore an ice King because I’m not a woman.

“But for me, it is really important that this happens and it comes close to my heart because this is what football is about.

“Guys who inspire people on the pitch with something people off the pitch and in the stands love to see. That is what football is about.”

Hibs midfielder Joe Newell admitted the scenes at the end of the game “will live with me forever.”

“That’s probably my favourite,” he said. “I’m probably getting emotional now, but it’s just seeing that at Hampden, it’s just incredible.

“We’ve been through a lot this season, obviously, already, the fans. So to give them that, it’s unbelievable. You can’t actually put it into words.

“It’s such a special feeling inside. A lot of the boys have probably seen it for the first time today.

“And if they didn’t know now how special the club is, they will do.”

Hearts boss Wouter Vrancken was “really sore and disappointed” after the defeat and believes their woes started when Tomas Magnusson and Calvin Miller had to come off in the first half, adding to a lengthy injury list.

He said: “It didn’t have to go this way because we had control of the game when it started.

“I think it started when Tomas was injured, that’s clear, and afterwards Calvin Miller.

“And those two changes – I am not pointing at the players who came in – but the changes took us off the rhythm.

“We were strong in the duels and second balls, then you lose these profiles, then it is searching again and hesitation and sometimes those hesitations give them too much space and you lose the game in those 20 minutes.

“We dominated the game again but it was just a pity that we didn’t get rewarded because we have had a lot of knocks already, also today, and you just hope they get rewarded.”

#2062. Official: AC Milan and Inter unveil new 71,500-seat ‘Generali Stadium’

The big day has finally arrived: AC Milan and Inter will unveil the details of their new stadium, along with design studios Foster+Partners and Manica.

Just two days before the derby, Milan and Inter fans – as well as the rest of the footballing world – will be able to admire the first images of how the new stadium will look. Some details have been known for some time, but can be hard to visualise.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

For example, the 71,500-seat capacity was known, of which between 8,000 and 13,000 will be dedicated to premium seating. The shape leaked out too, which will be oval rather than rectangular like the current San Siro.

It was also known that the new stadium will only have two tiers (not three) and will be built on a podium (with parking lots underneath the pitch). The stands will have a 37-degree inclination like the ‘Yellow Wall’ in Dortmund.

A lot of other features have made it into the press like the heavy presence of team-specific LED boards as well as all the extra amenities, but as mentioned it can be quite hard to form an image in one’s mind about how that will look. Now, we don’t have to guess.

❗ OFFICIAL: How #ACMilan and Inter's new home the 'Generali Stadium' will look.

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) October 29, 2026

AC Milan and FC Internazionale Milano today unveiled Generali Stadium, their future home: a new stadium conceived to carry the spirit of San Siro into a new era and become a new landmark for Milano.

More than a football stadium, the project represents a long-term investment in the future of two of world football’s most historic Clubs, a new home for generations of supporters, and a destination designed to contribute to the cultural, economic and urban development of the city.

The unveiling marks an important milestone in a journey that continues to transform ambition into reality. It offers the first comprehensive look at a stadium designed to honor the legacy of San Siro while creating a world-class experience built for the future of football.

The project is driven by a shared long-term vision from the Clubs and their respective owners, RedBird Capital Partners and Oaktree, part of Brookfield’s credit platform.

It represents a defining investment in the future of both organizations, creating the infrastructure needed to support sustained sporting success, unlock new opportunities for growth, and strengthen their ability to compete and win at the highest international level.

At the same time, the project reflects a broader ambition: to contribute to the modernization of Italian football while reinforcing Milano’s position as one of Europe’s most dynamic, innovative and globally recognized cities.

The architectural vision has been developed by Foster + Partners and MANICA, bringing together Lord Norman Foster, one of the world’s most influential contemporary architects, and David Manica, one of the leading designers of sports venues worldwide.

Building on a collaboration that dates back to the design of London’s Wembley Stadium, the partnership combines architectural excellence and stadium expertise to create a destination rooted in Milano’s identity while looking firmly to the future.

📸 Other photos of Generali Stadium 🔴⚫️ pic.twitter.com/mSsfW3V52D

— Milan Posts (@MilanPosts) October 29, 2026

The new stadium will carry the Generali name through one of the largest stadium naming rights agreements in global sport.

A partner from day one, Generali – an Italian leader and one of the largest insurance and asset management groups worldwide – shares the Clubs’ long-term commitment to Milano and the ambition to help shape its future, strengthening the city’s position on the global stage while creating a lasting legacy for generations to come.

Beyond naming rights, Generali will also serve as Official Insurance Partner of both Clubs, becoming part of the moments, emotions and shared experiences that will bring the stadium to life.

Every great city is defined by places that become part of its identity. Inspired by Milano’s architectural heritage and design culture, Generali Stadium has been conceived as one of those places.

At the heart of the design is a striking structural form, whose powerful rhythm recalls both the legacy of Italian engineering and the intricate craftsmanship of the Duomo di Milano. The concrete X-frame structure extends from the naturally ventilated colonnades through the façade and rises to support the stadium’s defining roofline.

Diamond-shaped entrance structures welcome visitors and create moments of discovery on arrival, offering glimpses into the stadium before opening onto panoramic concourses with sweeping views across the city.

Above, a distinctive double-curved roof defines the venue’s silhouette. More than an architectural statement, it frames and emphasizes the two iconic “Curvas”, creating a powerful visual identity while integrating photovoltaic technology, acoustic optimization and other sustainability features essential to a modern stadium.

The result is a design that is unmistakably contemporary, yet deeply connected to Milano’s character, creativity and global outlook.

While the architecture is new, the ambition is clear: preserve the atmosphere, emotion and sense of belonging that make San Siro one of football’s most iconic stages.

With approximately 71,500 seats, Generali Stadium has been designed around one principle above all else: bringing supporters closer to the action and maximizing the intensity of the matchday experience.

Two seating tiers form a continuous 360-degree bowl, creating exceptional sightlines and an immersive connection between fans and pitch. At either end, the iconic Curvas rise as single, steep walls of support, drawn forward toward the field of play with seating inclinations of up to 37 degrees to amplify both atmosphere and visual impact.

Engineered to capture and intensify crowd energy, the stadium’s acoustic design ensures supporters remain at the heart of the spectacle, helping create an environment designed to be among the most atmospheric in world football.

Enhanced accessibility, modern hospitality concepts and a broad range of seating options, from world-class premium experiences to popular seating areas, will ensure the venue welcomes every generation of fan, while offering new ways to experience the game.

The result is a stadium designed to bring supporters closer than ever before to the moments that matter most.

A stadium built for the future, while remaining deeply connected to everything that makes San Siro special: the emotion, the atmosphere, the unforgettable European nights, the great champions and, above all, the fans who give the stadium its soul.

Generali Stadium is conceived not only as the home of AC Milan and Internazionale, but as one of the city’s most important new destinations.

At the center of a wider 281,000-square-meter urban regeneration project, the development will transform the surrounding area into a vibrant district that is active throughout the year, integrating new public spaces, green areas, leisure and retail destinations into the fabric of the city.

Designed to welcome residents, visitors and fans from around the world, the district will offer opportunities to experience the Clubs, their heritage and their communities beyond matchdays, creating new places to gather, connect and celebrate. The ambition extends far beyond football. The project will create a year-round destination for sport, culture and entertainment while contributing to the attractiveness and international appeal of Milano.

Sustainability is embedded throughout the development, with solutions including natural ventilation, photovoltaic energy generation and a range of measures designed to improve efficiency, reduce environmental impact and support long-term operational performance.

The unveiling marks another significant milestone in the journey toward delivering the new stadium, following the historic agreement reached between the two Clubs and the City of Milano in 2025, which laid the foundations for the transformation of the San Siro area.

The project will now advance through the next stages of design and planning, with construction expected to begin in 2028 and the first match targeted for the 2031/32 season, subject to the necessary approvals.

For AC Milan and Internazionale, Generali Stadium represents far more than an infrastructure project. It is an investment in sporting ambition, in future generations of supporters and in the long-term future of both Clubs.

It is the platform that will help sustain growth, strengthen competitiveness, and create new opportunities on and off the pitch. Above all, it is a commitment to the people who will fill it. A new home for football. A new landmark for Milano.

#2061. Iraola fumes at bungling fourth official for costing Liverpool a penalty

Andoni Iraola wanted to talk about his team and their need to improve but how could he concentrate on something so straightforward when he had seen something so bizarre?

It is important, first and foremost, to explain this is not painting a narrative about Liverpool being unfortunate. Far from it. Iraola hissed his dismay that Nottingham Forest had shown more intensity and been the better team for long periods in an entertaining 2-2 draw.

But the penalty that changed the contest? Iraola, his coaching staff, even the supporters behind the dugout had been left flabbergasted that the malfunctioning number board of fourth official Tim Robinson presented an avenue for Forest to exploit.

Iraola had tried to make a triple change, wanting to introduce Ryan Gravenberch, Kostas Tsimikas and Rio Ngumoha, but as Robinson pressed buttons to no avail and everyone in Red became frustrated, Forest substitute Liam Delap took a quick throw and the Liverpool house almost caved in.

Neco Williams, once of Liverpool, surged into the penalty area, Alisson Becker arrived a fraction too late after the defender got his shot away and took his old team-mate down. Morgan Gibbs-White exacerbated the damage when sending Alisson the wrong way and this was the last thing a manager wanting to make an impression on a big day needed to see but this was reality.

Alisson takes out Neco Williams and Forest have a penalty! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fX2flY3Tob

Gibbs-White converts from the spot to restore Forest's lead! 🌳🎯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/jeoPiXPArw

“I cannot explain because I don’t have an explanation,” Iraola said. “I wanted to make those substitutions about three minutes before. I mean, it was two, three, four times the ball had gone out. I still don’t know the reason why we couldn’t make the subs.

“I think [the fourth official] was having some problems with the board or something. It [the penalty] wouldn’t have happened if I had made the sub. I asked. I had complained the previous time. The supporters were shouting and they were aware of the situation. But I don’t know what happened and I don’t know why they have given the penalty.”

"A professional fourth official cannot take three minutes." 😳Andoni Iraola was not happy with the time taken to get the substitutes' board ready.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fMfYOjQJPd

He did know, though, why Liverpool had needed to drag themselves off the deck again for the second week in a row. Iraola has shown in his opening weeks on Merseyside that he is not someone who seeks excuses.

“A lack of intensity hurt us,” Iraola said with obvious disdain and it was only down to a show of character in the second period that a slovenly first half did not enable Forest to win at Anfield for the third consecutive year, for all that the travelling fans thought it was “happening again!”

Forest, bruised after two defeats in four days to Leeds, looked like an Oliver Glasner side. They were aggressive and well organised, the only failing was that physically they could not see the job through, but the Austrian insisted that will change in due course.

Once Glasner is settled in and he gets his transfer business done – “definitely one, possibly two and probably three,” was his mischievous reply to how the window will unfold – Forest will be a formidable proposition, especially if the first 45 minutes are a barometer.

They had been knocking on the door before Dan Ndoye eventually broke the deadlock, sweeping a left-footed drive past Alisson after Igor Jesus had won a header from a long clearance. It was a simple goal, marginally onside, but it was absolutely deserved.

Ndoye gives Forest the lead at Anfield! 🌳🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ag0oZ7UjTm

“There were many positive aspects,” said Glasner. “It has been a three-game week; some players played. We are getting more and more fitness, that is just the foundation of how we want to play. It is just a point but it still feels a bit frustrating, so we have to stay humble.”

"I think we were very poor in the first half." 😤Andoni Iraola gives his assessment of Liverpool's performance against Nottingham Forest.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/COZfhwkLeX

Neco Williams and James McAtee react to Nottingham Forest's draw at Anfield 🌳🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BjX0p1yQ1m

"We started the game pretty bad today." 😬Alexander Isak gives his assessment of Liverpool's performance at Anfield.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/3wD0hplmQ6

The playmaker added another goal and assist to his tally this afternoon.

20 - Morgan Gibbs-White has been directly involved in 20 goals in 2026 (15 goals, 5 assists), the joint-most of any Premier League player in all competitions (level with Haaland).His 13 goals in the Premier League in 2026 are also the most of any player.Decisive. pic.twitter.com/p1wQFwXvsI

Liverpool and Forest are both made to wait for their first Premier League wins of the season as the two sides play out a pulsating 2-2 draw at Anfield.

Full-time scenes at Anfield as Liverpool and Nottingham Forest share the points 🤝📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/WqOpfU38es

Sels calmly comes out to claim a deep cross to relieve the pressure on Forest. Munoz runs back to dispossess Delap and win a free kick, giving Liverpool another chance to launch the ball forward.

Glasner makes a very late double change as Hudson-Odoi and Dominguez replace McAtee and Igor Jesus.

There will be five minutes of added time. Liverpool continue their relentless search for a third goal, while Forest are holding on.

It’s wave after wave of Liverpool pressure. Forest are camped inside their own half. Igor Jesus and Delap are chasing every loose ball, but Forest are struggling to get out at the moment.

Munoz’s goal has provided another twist in this pulsating encounter. Isak wins a free kick in such dangerous territory and Szoboszlai steps up to take it. The Hungarian slams a venomous effort wide of the far post. Can either side find a late winner?

What an incredible finish! Wirtz threads a delightful pass through to Munoz. With his back to goal, the winger swivels and takes the ball on the outside of Murillo, before smashing a thunderous effort into the roof of the net, which brushes the crossbar on its way in.

Munoz, take a bow! 🤯👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GD8IAdy2rJ

Igor Jesus does brilliantly to escape Nyoni, before he is pulled to the ground by Arajou, who is booked. It’s been an excellent defensive effort from Forest.

Iraola makes his final two alterations as Araujo and Nyoni replace Jacquet and Mac Allister.  Szoboszlai then swings such an inviting delivery into the penalty area, but Isak miscues his strike with his left foot.

Amid the chaos, Alisson was booked just before the penalty after appealing the decision and Iraola has ordered a triple change, taking off Kerkez, Frimpong and Gakpo for Tsimikas, Gravenberch and Ngumoha. This has seen Szoboszlai move out to right back.

Andoni Iraola is about to make his substitution and this is interesting because he had planned to introduce Rio Ngumoha, Kostas Tsimikas and Ryan Gravenberch 10 minutes ago but told them to sit down after Liverpool had equalised. Forest have put Liam Delap on, giving him his debut after completing his £45m move to the club.

The Forest captain sends Alisson the wrong way, powering a clinical penalty into the net. Gibbs-White demonstrates fantastic composure and Liverpool have it all to do again.

Gibbs-White converts from the spot to restore Forest's lead! 🌳🎯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/jeoPiXPArw

Delap showcases excellent initiative and takes a quick throw-in to send Williams through on goal. Alisson rushes out and catches Williams as he attempts to lob the goalkeeper. Williams crashes to the ground and the referee points to the spot. Alisson is furious. What a chance for Forest to restore their lead.

Alisson takes out Neco Williams and Forest have a penalty! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fX2flY3Tob

This game is being played at a ferocious pace and Forest’s club-record signing Delap enters the action as he replaces Ndoye. Can the former Chelsea striker mark his debut with a much-needed goal?

That leveller has injected so much energy into Liverpool. Anfield believes again. Isak really needed that goal.

So much credit must go to Gakpo. The winger shrugs off Williams and fires a pinpoint cross towards the back post. Isak is there and converts from close range. We’re set up for such an intriguing finale. Liverpool have the momentum now.

Isak equalises for Liverpool at the Kop end! 🔴🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/qKFxq2AqaB

Wirtz’s frustrating afternoon is compounded as he picks up a booking after hauling Murillo to the ground. Iraola looks to be readying some substitutions.

There is a very strange feeling here: it’s almost a case of the home fans waiting for Nottingham Forest to score a second goal rather than anticipating that Liverpool will equalise. The early buzz in the atmosphere has gone and that is because the gaps everyone can see in the make up of the team remain. How Bradley Barcola will transform this situation?

Jacquet’s pass is intercepted and Ndoye is released on the counter. He’s guided out wide by Van Dijk but still squeezes in a brilliant cross. Gibbs-White was running up the pitch in support and slowed down, meaning no one was there to turn in Ndoye’s delivery.

Munoz is the next player to be booked after reacting angrily to a decision. Iraola has to consider making some changes soon.

Aina catches Munoz with a late challenge and he’s the second Forest player to go into the referee’s book.

You can already see in this second half that there is acres of space for Forest to exploit on the counter as Liverpool push for a leveller. Munoz then heads a point-blank header over the bar. Luckily for the Spaniard, the offside flag was up against Gakpo.

We are back for the second half here at Anfield. Can Liverpool find a route back into this game or can Forest hold onto the three points?

It’s a bizarre situation for Liverpool. They could easily be level or be 2-0 down. But they trial just 1-0 at half-time. Wirtz and Gakpo are looking lively, but Isak has struggled to influence the game.

Dan Ndoye scores his first goal in the Premier League in 377 days 🤯 pic.twitter.com/tjSiGoSPyW

Forest have a slender one-goal advantage at the break after a frantic first half at Anfield. Ndoye curled the visitors into a well-deserved lead after 24 minutes, before Wirtz had a goal ruled out for offside. The German was then sensationally denied by Sels’ diving save as he tipped Wirtz’s header over the bar. Alisson then replicated Sels’ heroics, parrying Igor Jesus’ strike against the woodwork to stop Forest from doubling their lead.

What a move and what a save! Murillo sprays an inch-perfect pass out to Aina, who chops inside of Munoz and fires a low cross into Igor Jesus. The Forest striker shoots first-time from inside the penalty area, but his effort is sensationally parried onto the bar by Alisson. That is a world-class stop from the Brazilian goalkeeper.

A world-class save from Alisson denies Forest a second! 🤯🧤📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4NtzROILrU

Igor Jesus receives the game’s first yellow card after clipping Mac Allister with an unnecessary challenge.

Liverpool then fly forward again as Gakpo nutmegs Williams. His cross trickles through to Munoz at the back post. The ball is slightly behind Munoz and he leans back before shooting, causing his strike to narrowly sail over the bar.

There will be three minutes of added time to conclude this first half.

Liverpool are applying all the pressure at the end of this first half. At times, Forest have had every outfield player behind the ball.

Sels makes a superb save! Gakpo takes on his marker on the outside and fires in a cross which Wirtz meets. The attacker gets in between Schlager and Aina to win the header, but his effort is excellently tipped over the bar by Sels.

Out of nothing, Liverpool are level. McAtee attempts to play out from a deep position and his pass is intercepted by Wirtz. The ball breaks to Frimpong, who slips a clever pass to Wirtz. The German playmaker swivels and slides a low effort into the bottom corner. It’s a brilliant finish, but Frimpong was in an offside position before he provided the assist. VAR confirms this and Liverpool’s joy has been cut short. That is a huge let off for Forest, who need to be more careful with possession in deeper areas.

Following that Forest goal, there was a small flurry of Liverpool pressure, with Szoboszlai having a free kick punched away by Sels. Murillo is then very careless with the ball and is dispossessed. This allowed Mac Allister to play in Isak, but the striker is crowded out by multiple Forest defenders before he can get a shot away.

For the third season in a row, Nottingham Forest lead at Anfield. The goal had been coming, too. Liverpool were bright early but suddenly big gaps have started appearing and Forest are wily enough to exploit. There are lots of gripes around the stands about it being “too easy” and this knowledgeable crowd are right. A long ball forward and a simple flick has caused mayhem.

Forest are ahead and are well worth their lead. Sels launches a long ball up to Igor Jesus, who takes it down with an exquisite touch. The ball then breaks to Gibbs-White. The Forest captain plays in Ndoye and the winger curls a clinical effort into the far bottom corner to send the away support wild.

Ndoye gives Forest the lead at Anfield! 🌳🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ag0oZ7UjTm

Liverpool are struggling to find any space in and around Forest’s midfield and defence. Isak and Wirtz have been on the periphery as the time ticks over midway point of the first half.

Huge chance for Forest! McAtee drops deep and picks out Ndoye with a teasing cross. The forward meets the delivery and his header bounces wide. Upon the replays, there looks to have been a push on Frimpong by Ndoye. The referee’s whistle wasn’t sounded so it would have been interesting to see what would of happened if that chance had been converted.

It’s been a really frantic start to this game. Out of possession, Forest are retreating into a really rigid back five formation. Going forward, Aina and Williams are getting up the pitch at every opportunity.

Aina stands up an inviting cross to the back post for Ndoye, who heads it back into the danger zone. Igor Jesus latches onto it, but Jacquet makes a goal-saving tackle to block the striker’s close-range effort.

Sensational block from Jeremy Jacquet to deny Igor Jesus! 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/XuhO1GuE9F

Van Dijk clips a long ball over to the onrushing Isak as Liverpool look to burst forward on the counter. Isak races onto it and enters the penalty area, but he’s chased by Jair Cunha who matches the striker for pace. There’s a shoulder-to-shoulder, and the Forest defender bumps Isak off the ball, before Milenkovic comes back to mop up the danger.

Ndoye attempts to sprint in behind Liverpool’s defence. He’s chased by Jacquet and Ndoye can’t quite take the ball under his spell. That is an early warning sign for Liverpool.

The hosts then go up the other end as Mac Allister threads a delightful pass through to Gakpo. The Liverpool forward tries to swivel and shoot, but Williams tracks back and makes a crucial tackle.

Frimpong gets in behind Forest’s backline and attempts to pick out Gakpo with a cross aimed towards the back post. However, the ball bobbles and the Liverpool right back overhits his delivery.

A very intriguing team selected by Andoni Iraola and one that illustrates his confidence. It could be viewed as big call to drop Ryan Gravenberch and Rio Ngumoha but Victor Munoz and Alexis Mac Allister both made a difference when they were introduced at St James’s Park last Sunday and they warrant their inclusion. Munoz won’t be fit enough to play 90 minutes but it will be fascinating to watch him, particularly as Bradley Barcola will soon arrive to play in the same position on the left flank.

We are now under way at Anfield. Can Iraola mark his first competitive home game with a win or will Glasner get up and running with Forest?

A roaring rendition of You’ll Never Walk Alone has just boomed around Anfield. We will now observe a minute’s applause for Liverpool legend Kevin Keegan, who passed away at the age of 75 in July.

Anfield remembers Kevin Keegan ❤️A special tribute to the Liverpool legend ahead of kick-off. pic.twitter.com/bJgi58vPj7

A very poignant and colourful tribute to Kevin Keegan, with Anfield paying its respects to one of its favourite sons. The atmosphere is good and the onus is on the team to maintain it. This won’t be easy, as Nottingham Forest arrive here with a point to prove under Oliver Glasner. The big story with Forest will come later, with their pursuit of Everton’s Harrison Armstrong. It it is a transfer that is causing huge discussion on Merseyside.

Both sets of players are out onto the pitch and are met by an electric atmosphere at Anfield.

All set for #LIVNFO 💪 pic.twitter.com/IJOZ6NwGNW

Earlier this month, Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group announced they had agreed to sell a minority equity stake to 1892 Holdings, a consortium led and managed by Amit Bhatia, who is in attendance at Anfield today.

On the development, Bhatia told Liverpool’s website: “It feels incredible. It feels surreal when I hear those words, obviously an incredibly proud moment for myself, for my family, for our partners. We’re talking about Liverpool Football Club here, right? I mean, we’re talking about the greatest football club in the world. And so to have the ability to be involved in any capacity is a huge privilege and a huge honour.”

Having been linked to both Tottenham Hotspur and Manchester City, Cody Gakpo’s Liverpool future has looked doubtful at points this summer.

However, Spurs’ signings of Savinho and Omar Marmoush, as well as Manchester City’s potentially big-money pursuit of Enzo Fernandez, means that any exit for the Dutchman looks extremely complicated.

Gakpo scored Liverpool’s first equaliser in their chaotic 2-2 draw with Newcastle United and starts today on the left wing.

When Callum Hudson-Odoi made history at Anfield 🤩 pic.twitter.com/HhJ73WztMd

Last season’s emphatic 3-0 victory in the same fixture under Sean Dyche means that Forest have successive wins at a ground where they could notoriously never manage three points.

Nottingham Forest have smashed their club-record transfer fee to sign Chelsea striker Liam Delap for £50m on a five-year deal, ending a lengthy pursuit by both the club and their head coach Oliver Glasner.

Last summer Delap held talks with Forest and Glasner, while he was in charge at Crystal Palace, before he opted to join his mentor and former Manchester City Under-21 coach Enzo Maresca at Stamford Bridge.

One of the summer’s most talked about and protracted transfer pursuits is nearing its conclusion as Liverpool have agreed a £120m deal with Paris St-Germain to sign Bradley Barcola.

The Frenchman was absent from PSG’s squad on Friday evening as Luis Enrique’s side drew 2-2 with Lille in Ligue 1.

Barcola is yet another big-money addition to Liverpool’s forward line, following on from the signings of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Hugo Ekitike last summer.

He also has the approval of club legend Steven Gerrard, who is at Anfield on duty for TNT Sports.

Anfield will host its first Premier League match of the 2026-27 season.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League match between Liverpool and Nottingham Forest at Anfield.

This encounter pits two summer appointments – Andoni Iraola and Oliver Glasner – against each other as they both search for their first top-flight win at their new clubs.

In the opening Premier League game-week, Iraola’s Liverpool needed a last-gasp 99th-minute penalty from Dominik Szoboszlai to rescue an unconvincing 2-2 draw with Newcastle United at St. James’ Park. Meanwhile, Nottingham Forest have suffered back-to-back home defeats in four days against Leeds United without scoring (1-0 Premier League, 2-0 Carabao Cup).

Iraola has been handed the unenviable task of steering Liverpool back on track following a hugely disappointing campaign under Arne Slot, whose side’s defence of their Premier League ended in a meek fifth-place finish despite spending more than £400m in the previous summer.

The former Bournemouth boss must uncover how to get the best out of big-money recruits such as Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Milos Kerkez and Jeremie Frimpong, and also tighten up Liverpool’s vulnerable midfield and defence. Given the pressure of the job and the club’s hectic schedule while balancing domestic and European football, it’s a tough ask. However, Liverpool have agreed a £120m deal for Paris St-Germain winger Bradley Barcola to bolster their attacking reinforcements, but the transfer hasn’t been finalised in time for today’s match.

Last season, Forest endured an equally tumultuous campaign, churning through a staggering four managers, before eventually stumbling to a 16th-place finish. Glasner has been hand-picked by owner Evangelos Marinakis to usher in an era of stability and success, after winning the FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League in just over two years at Crystal Palace.

Both Marinakis and Glasner are extremely ambitious and demanding figures. You’d imagine a top-half finish would be considered the absolute minimum for Forest, while Glasner’s track record of winning trophies surely indicates that Marinakis is eyeing some silverware at the City Ground.

It’s a meeting of two managers who must deliver. Three points for either side would serve as a much-needed tonic to kickstart their seasons.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

#2059. Cardinale discusses support for Amorim, signings to come, Krösche links and new stadium

AC Milan owner Gerry Cardinale has pledged to back Ruben Amorim as head coach, also promising more reinforcements for the squad.

As a reminder, Cardinale hand-picked Amorim as the successor to Massimiliano Allegri at the start of the summer. Support came in the window, with Goncalo Ramos and Diego Moreira becoming the two most expensive signings in the club’s history.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Results so far have been mixed, however. Milan have lost two of three in the Europa League, with the defeats to Benfica and Bournemouth coming without scoring. Their first Serie A defeat came on Sunday versus Bologna, after a worrying second-half collapse.

Nonetheless, there are signs of what things can become under Amorim, who wants to play an intense and proactive style. It is something that Cardinale intends to see through, as he revealed in an interview with La Gazzetta dello Sport.

Are you happy with the results achieved so far?

“I’m never happy. Let me explain: I’m happy when we win a match, but that doesn’t mean anything. Ask me if I’m happy when I lift a trophy or we win a title. Then I’ll tell you I’m really happy. We still have a lot of work to do, and lately I’ve had injuries that have made me nervous.

“So now I’m nervous and constantly focused on where we can improve. I have a job to do, and I won’t stop until we get what we want. Anyone who knows me and has worked with me knows I’m always dissatisfied until I reach my goal.”

Given the many injuries, do Milan need more players in January?

“We need to continue improving the squad because in the summer I wasn’t able to do everything I wanted. We’re rebuilding the team, and while I like the new arrivals, the ones who stayed, and the names I got rid of, it will probably take a couple more transfer windows to complete everything.

“We’re only a quarter of the way there, and the priority is to build a team that can deal with injuries. If you’re competing in European competitions and playing… Amorim Ball, which is high-tempo football, with quick transitions, where everyone runs between 9 and 11km per game, you have to rotate them.

“That’s why we’ll continue to be aggressive and opportunistic in the January transfer market, and I’ll continue to strengthen our bench. My style is to move decisively and quickly.

“What matters to me is getting what we want, players… that are Milan-worthy. I won’t waste money, but when I set my mind on signing a player, I do everything I can to succeed.”

Will Krösche be AC ​​Milan’s new head of football?

“I’m not close to making an announcement, and I’m in no rush. The choice of sporting director is one of the most important after this summer’s transition, when I fired everyone and took over the club. I’m talking to Krösche and other people, the best in football.

“With a season that ends in May and a transfer window starting in June, I don’t want to rush. I’m directly managing the club now, and I like it, but I can’t do it forever because I have another job. Plus, there are people much more qualified than me.

“However, in May I had to rebuild AC Milan, and only someone like me could do it. Now a sporting director will arrive, but he or she will be a part of a much more complex organisational structure. Someone who will have to work with me.

“We’ll do everything together because I will no longer hand over the keys to a sporting director or sporting director.

“Yes, and I have complete faith in him. At the end of Top Gun, ‘my’ movie, there’s a great line: ‘I’m not abandoning my wingman’ says Tom Cruise. And I’m not abandoning Ruben. He’s absolutely not in danger. I’ll stay by his side [he repeats it twice, forcefully].

“I won’t make the same mistakes I’ve made in recent years. He’s my coach, and we’ll continue to work together until we can make the leap in quality. You can’t win if you keep switching from one coach to another. I chose Amorim. If I’d made a mistake, I’d admit it, but I don’t think I did.

“He learned a lot from what happened at Manchester United, and I hired him because he explained the mistakes I made there. He has the right culture, he’s a leader, a manager, and a well-prepared coach. There’s a different atmosphere at Milanello than in the last four years. The credit goes to him.

“He’s learning things, and the team needs to find its cohesion, understand How can we rotate players while still scoring lots of goals and winning? For me, a draw is a defeat. A point isn’t the goal of the game: three points are. Only with victories can we close the gap to the top teams.”

Can ‘Amorim Ball’ make AC Milan great again?

“In the days before every game, I call him and ask: ‘How can I help you? What do you need?’ and he reassures me by saying: ‘I’ll take care of it, I’ll take care of it.’ He knows I’m there, but he also knows how to do his job.

“He doesn’t need me breathing down his neck: he has everything under control and is a true professional who helps people grow. He’s managing the boys and training the group well. I don’t think this happened before.

“A lightbulb went off in my head when Ibra asked me a few months ago: ‘What does Milan represent?’ Since then, I think about these words practically every day, in everything we do. I like this group, where everyone supports each other, without power games in the dressing room: everyone is killing themselves to win.

“You can see it just by looking into their eyes. In previous years, I asked myself: ‘Why am I the angriest if we don’t win?’ Now I don’t feel that way anymore: the boys and the staff are as angry as I am.”

Tomorrow will be the first derby since AC Milan’s new era began. What kind of match are you expecting?

“As Amorim says, I look at the derby as a ‘simple’ match. I don’t think that, if we win, we’ll move closer in the standings. We have to do our job, play football, score goals, and improve in everything.”

“I respect Marotta and his club’s organisation, which, even when Inzaghi left, didn’t miss a beat. A bit like Liverpool, who had a record-breaking season with Slot replacing Klopp. That’s what I aspire to for us.

“Inter have every right to be where they are now. They’ve earned it, and I respect them for that. Do I feel the competition with them? Of course! Do they keep me awake at night? Absolutely. The competition is good, and I’m confident we can get to that level.

“It’s only a matter of time before we get better, before we lift that trophy (the Scudetto). It won’t be easy, and nothing will be handed to us. I know very well what’s at stake tomorrow, and I know how strong they are. And I can’t wait for the derby. I can’t wait.”

“It’s absolutely possible, one hundred percent. And I say this without meaning to sound arrogant. I wake up every morning hoping for a small glimmer of hope, that Inter will start drawing instead of winning and that we’ll start putting together a series of victories.

“Winning is the only thing that matters to me, but let’s take it one game at a time, gaining ground on those ahead of us, day after day.”

So far you have just the Supercoppa Italiana…

“I’m upset about the four years I’ve lost. I want to create a world-class football organisation, with the right people. I have the feeling that AC Milan isn’t working at full capacity yet.

“My desire is to achieve very rapid change, but I know that’s not compatible with football. ‘You’ll have to be patient,’ they tell me. But… I’m not. And so last summer I took on Moreira, after Ramos and Gila. These are deals I made, with the other owners, and I defend them.”

Which footballers impressed you the most?

“It’s a dangerous question, because I have to love all my… ‘sons’. I adore Pulisic; ditto Rabiot, Moreira, Gila, who’s a beast, Hutchinson, Ramos, Maignan who’s our leader… And I could name all my boys.”

“It’s a project we’ve been working on for four years, a priority. The new San Siro is a fundamental step for Italy, a country where building new facilities seemed impossible. We must find a way to bring Serie A back to the level it deserves. Because a stronger Serie A also means a stronger AC Milan.

“The only way to compete with the Premier League is to start transforming our economic profile. I believe a club like AC Milan and its fans deserve an infrastructure of this quality. This stadium is a powerful statement from me and RedBird of how important all of this is to us.

“We’re doing everything we can to get back to the top. The milestone we’ve reached with the stadium is important, but there’s no stadium in the world that, for me, is as important as a derby victory against Inter.”

Are RedBird interested in buying Al Nassr? Would they like to work with Cristiano Ronaldo?

“There have been conversations to evaluate the Al Nassr opportunity, and they’ve contacted me to explore it, but we’re still at a preliminary stage.

“I work a lot in the Middle East: I’d like to meet Ronaldo because I’m curious to understand what he might want to do when he retires and what his future interest in the Saudi club will be. I’ll continue to evaluate the possibilities of a multi-club deal, considering that I already have Toulouse and AC Milan.”

Will AC Milan support Galliani in the race for the FIGC presidency against Malagò?

“I respect both of them. It’s not a question of names, but rather of what they want to do.”

#2058. Reports: Milan and Inter agree €650m deal with Generali for stadium naming rights – the details

AC Milan and Inter unveiled their new stadium project last night, with a rather interesting detail: the name has already been agreed.

Milan and Inter presented the project for the new stadium that will replace San Siro and host the Milanese clubs’ matches starting in 2031 last night. However, it leaked out ahead of time that a naming rights deal has already been agreed with Generali.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

MilanNews and Calcio e Finanza have confirmed that it is an agreement worth approximately €26m per year. Furthermore, it was highlighted that the partnership contract between Milan and Inter with Generali is expected to last for a full 25 years, meaning a total figure of €650m.

If these are indeed correct, the deal would be second only to the one that Atletico Madrid have with Riyadh Air Metropolitano (€28-33m per year) but surpasses Spotify for Barcelona’s Camp Nou (€20m), as well as Allianz with Bayern Munich (€13m) and Signal Iduna Park with Dortmund (€11m).

The Athletic report that the sponsorship is worth €650m but over 20 years, which would result in a higher annual value. If that were true, it would be potentially in excess of what Crypto.com and SoFi reportedly paid to sponsor the homes of the NBA’s Los Angeles Lakers and the NFL’s Los Angeles Rams, respectively.

Milan’s chairman Paolo Scaroni served on the board of directors at Generali from 2007 until 2014, so there is a pre-existing link there.
